title: Dynamic steel plate storage scheduling in shipyard logistics: A deep reinforcement learning framework
affiliations: Harbin Engineering University, Harbin Engineering University, Harbin Engineering University, Harbin Engineering University, Harbin Engineering University and Harbin Engineering University

detail.title: Dynamic steel plate storage scheduling in shipyard logistics: A deep reinforcement learning framework
detail.abstract: Optimising material logistics is a pivotal challenge for operational efficiency in the contemporary shipbuilding industry. This study investigates the Dynamic Steel Plate Storage Problem (DSPSP) within shipyard stockyards, which is inherently governed by strict Last-In-First-Out (LIFO) physical constraints. Improper vertical stacking frequently causes priority inversions, inevitably leading to redundant crane relocations that significantly disrupt shipbuilding schedules. Complicating this issue further are uncertainties caused by stochastic multi-batch deliveries and dynamic yard capacities. To tackle these intertwined spatial and temporal challenges, this paper proposes an end-to-end Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) framework. Specifically, the continuous stacking process is formulated as a Markov Decision Process (MDP), incorporating a domain dense reward mechanism to guide - policy convergence. Moreover, to effectively extract complex stockyard statuses, a novel Spatio-Temporal Gated Dual-Attention (STGDA) network is designed as the policy representation core. This architecture seamlessly aligns the spatial configuration of current stacks with the temporal sequences of incoming batches, while simultaneously employing a gated fusion mechanism to mitigate the uncertainty of future arrivals. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method consistently outperforms conventional heuristics in both solution quality and real-time responsiveness. Furthermore, the learned policy exhibits robust zero shot generalization across varying stack height configurations. Ultimately, this study delivers an autonomous scheduling solution that minimizes relocation operations, thereby enhancing logistical efficiency and accelerating digital transformation in ship production.

title: Higher-Moments-Robust Monetary Policy Shocks
affiliations: Newcastle Business School

detail.title: Higher-Moments-Robust Monetary Policy Shocks
detail.abstract: This paper develops a novel measure of monetary shocks that accounts for the endogenous response of the Federal Open Market Committee’s (FOMC) to higher moments of expected economic outcomes. First, I use quantile regression to estimate the conditional distribution of Federal Reserve forecasts and construct indicators of uncertainty and skewness. Second, I show that, unlike other measures proposed in the literature, they possess strong predictive power for the changes in the Fed funds rate. This result suggests that considering only first moments is not sufficient to isolate the systematic component of monetary policy, leading to key implications for the identification of monetary shocks. In particular, controlling for higher-moments delivers shocks that exhibit lower autocorrelation and induce theoretically consistent effects on output, prices, and financial variables.

title: Short-term response mechanisms and applicability boundaries for transfer-service recovery under high-speed railway disruptions
affiliations: Dalian Jiaotong University, affiliation not provided to SSRN and Dalian Jiaotong University

detail.title: Short-term response mechanisms and applicability boundaries for transfer-service recovery under high-speed railway disruptions
detail.abstract: Unexpected high-speed railway disruptions rapidly cause timetable infeasibility and missed transfers, deteriorating passenger service. While prior studies advanced train rescheduling and resilience assessment, the short-term response stage lacks sufficient explanation from a mechanism perspective. Specifically, it remains unclear why distinct response logics perform differently under varying disturbance intensities, and when layered coordination creates or loses its collaborative advantage.This paper examines transfer-service recovery within a mainline-hub-branch structure, framing it as a mechanism-and-boundary problem rather than pure optimization. We compare three response logics: train-side adjustment only, service-side opening only, and layered coordination, using a mechanism-oriented framework based on stage decomposition and structural-condition indicators.Results indicate that layered coordination is only effective within a bounded response region. Its collaborative value stems from cross-side compensation: early service opening restores transfer accessibility and reduces passenger loss, while subsequent train-side correction reclaims operational burden. However, once the recoverable transfer stock is exhausted, passenger-side benefits shrink, and the layered strategy degenerates into mere train-side reclamation. This study provides a reproducible explanation of layered coordination's operational mechanisms, weakening conditions, and applicability boundaries in short-term disruption responses.

title: The value of lower and upper bounds in estimating the optimal cost of Inventory Routing Problems through regression models
affiliations: University of Brescia - Department of Economics and Management, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: The value of lower and upper bounds in estimating the optimal cost of Inventory Routing Problems through regression models
detail.abstract: This paper studies linear regression models to estimate the optimal cost of Inventory Routing Problems. We introduce new predictors based on lower and upper bounds on the optimal cost. The upper bounds are obtained by solving a related problem, that is, the Capacitated Concentrator Location Inventory Routing Problem. We collect all feasible solutions generated by a branch-and-cut algorithm in a short time limit, and then build predictors based on the cost components and on the total cost of the best solution found, and on the mean and the standard deviation of the total cost of all collected solutions. Finally, we introducea new lower bound on the optimal cost and use it as a predictor. Combining these predictors with the classical ones used to estimate related routing problems, we obtain very effective linear regression models, able to estimate the optimal total cost of Inventory Routing Problems with Unsplit and Split deliveries, when the Maximum Level and the Order-up to Level replenishment policies are used. The corresponding Mean Average Percentage Error is always less than 1.40% for classical benchmark instances with constant demand, and it is about 1.89% for more complex benchmark instances with time-varying demand. Finally, Fortifiedestimation, i.e., a technique that improves the estimates obtained by regression using ex post lower and upper bounds on the optimal total cost, allows us to reduce the Mean Average Percentage Error to about 1.34% and 1.87%, respectively.

detail.abstract: A transformação do setor da saúde exige que médicos e profissionais da área desenvolvam não apenas excelência técnica, mas também competências relacionadas à comunicação, empatia e relacionamento humano. A entrevista de Willy Marcus França ao podcast O Marketeiro evidencia que o verdadeiro diferencial competitivo na medicina contemporânea está na capacidade de humanizar o atendimento, construir vínculos de confiança e oferecer experiências positivas aos pacientes. Ao discutir marketing médico sob uma perspectiva ética e estratégica, o autor demonstra que reputação, credibilidade e posicionamento profissional são construídos diariamente por meio de atitudes, comportamento e acolhimento. Em um cenário cada vez mais tecnológico e competitivo, a humanização deixa de ser apenas um valor moral e passa a representar um importante instrumento de fidelização, fortalecimento de marca e valorização da prática médica.

title: A Sim-heuristic approach for the last-mile delivery with occasional drivers and uncertain travel time
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, University of Calabria and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: A Sim-heuristic approach for the last-mile delivery with occasional drivers and uncertain travel time
detail.abstract: In this work, we tackle a Vehicle Routing Problem with Time Windows, Occasional Drivers and stochastic travel times (Stoch-VRPODTW). We propose a sim-heuristic approach, that combines a Variable Neighborhood Search metaheuristic with simulation (Sim-VNS) to solve the stochastic variant of the problem. The considered approach takes into account the uncertainty of travel times and the penalties derived by time windows violations. The experimental results show the Sim-VNS has better performance of the existing robust model, significantly reducing routing costs and penalties, improving the reliability of the solutions. In particular, Sim-VNS outperforms the robust model on big instances with at least 100 customers.

title: Knowledge-Enhanced Diffusion Model for Image Captioning in Intelligent Manufacturing
affiliations: South China University of Technology, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Peng Cheng Laboratory and South China University of Technology

detail.title: Knowledge-Enhanced Diffusion Model for Image Captioning in Intelligent Manufacturing
detail.abstract: Image captioning is a functional research problem with broad applications across various domains. In intelligent manufacturing, accurate and context-aware descriptions are essential for automation, quality inspection, and intelligent decision-making. However, most existing methods insufficiently integrate domain knowledge, often resulting in inaccurate or even hallucinated descriptions, which undermines their reliability and practical deployment in industrial scenarios. To address this challenge, we propose KenDiC, a domain knowledge-enhanced image captioning framework based on diffusion model for intelligent manufacturing. Specifically, we design a domain-adaptive visual encoder (DAVE) that leverages contrastive learning to enhance the alignment between visual representations and textual semantics in the latent space. Furthermore, we introduce a domain-centric terminology vocabulary (DCTV) into the generation process to enforce terminology-constrained captioning, ensuring the accurate usage of technical entities. To support rigorous evaluation, we construct IIT-Bench, a domain-specific image-to-text dataset comprising 3,300 high-resolution images paired with 16,500 expert-annotated captions. Extensive experiments demonstrate that KenDiC consistently outperforms state-of-the-art approaches in domain captioning performance, highlighting its effectiveness and practical value for human-machine collaboration in intelligent manufacturing.

title: An Introduction to Generative Structural Philosophy
affiliations: Foods Support MORICA Co., Ltd.

detail.title: An Introduction to Generative Structural Philosophy

keywords: I Ching (Yi Jing) JEL Classification: D83

detail.abstract: This paper proposes Generative Structural Philosophy as a foundational theory for explaining how knowledge becomes judgment, how judgment becomes conduct, and how conduct generates value through relations and virtue. Existing theories of knowledge, organizational learning, practice, and service have clarified important dimensions of explicit knowledge, tacit knowledge, experience, situated action, and value co-creation. Yet they do not fully explain the generative passage by which knowledge, within a concrete field of recognition and action, becomes a situated judgment capable of transforming relations. This paper addresses that gap by defining knowledge not as a static possession but as a generative resource that operates within what it calls the Present Field. The Present Field is not merely the temporal present or a current situation. It is a phenomenological field of recognition: the field of recognizable situations, relations, constraints, and possibilities that arises for a subject within actuality. On this basis, the paper develops a sequence of concepts: knowledge, the Present Field, judgment, Conduct, Relation, Virtue, value generation, knowledge-giving, and NODE NAVIS. The central claim is that value is not produced by information transfer alone, nor by action alone, but by the CRV structure-Conduct, Relation, and Virtue-through which judgment acts upon relations and gives rise to meaningful value. The paper also examines a methodological correspondence with the I Ching, especially the notions of timeliness and non-centralized multiplicity, not as a source of authority but as a comparative philosophical line of reference. Finally, NODE NAVIS is positioned as a practical system for connecting multiple Present Fields and regenerating judgment in organizations.

title: From Pressure to Deviance: Examining the Asymmetric Psychological Pathways of Data Security Stressors
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: From Pressure to Deviance: Examining the Asymmetric Psychological Pathways of Data Security Stressors
detail.abstract: Previous research on information security has typically treated security-related stress and deviant behavior as unidimensional constructs, overlooking the possibility that different types of stress may activate distinct emotional and behavioral pathways. Drawing on conservation of resources theory, psychological reactance theory, and regulatory focus theory, this study develops an asymmetric dual-pathway model in which data security work stress (DSWS) shapes employee deviant behavior through differentiated emotional mechanisms. We partition DSWS into role responsibility stress (RRS) and internal policy stress (IPS); the former depletes resources and triggers state burnout, which in turn produces negligent deviance (the COR pathway), while the latter threatens behavioral freedom and triggers resistance emotion, which produces defiant deviance (the Brehm pathway). Regulatory focus further shapes how emotion translates into behavior: prevention focus buffers the burnout-to-negligence link, whereas promotion focus amplifies the resistance-to-defiance link. Using two-wave, time-lagged data from 418 employees in Chinese banks and internet firms and testing the model with CB-SEM, bootstrap mediation analysis, and latent moderated structural equations (LMS), we find strong support for the type-matched pathways (H2a, H2b) and significantly weaker cross-type pathways (H2c, H2d). Promotion focus robustly amplifies the Brehm pathway (H3b), while prevention focus weakens the COR pathway to a marginally significant extent (H3a). These findings refine the mechanistic understanding of security-related stress, move the field beyond a compliance-versus-noncompliance binary toward a negligent-versus-defiant distinction, and yield pathway-specific intervention priorities for CISOs and ISP owners.

title: Integrating Domain Knowledge into Graph Neural Networks Using Virtual Nodes for Industrial Applications
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and Tokyo University of Agriculture and Technology

detail.title: Integrating Domain Knowledge into Graph Neural Networks Using Virtual Nodes for Industrial Applications
detail.abstract: Deep neural networks (DNNs) are increasingly deployed in industrial applications where consistency with prior knowledge is important.  In these fields, leveraging domain knowledge is important for tasks such as selecting relevant variables, embedding knowledge into the model structure, and incorporating it to define loss functions or regularization terms.  While graph neural networks (GNNs) provide a powerful framework for learning from structured data, existing approaches rarely exploit domain knowledge that includes conditional expressions (e.g., physical or logical equations) and unobserved variables representing latent process states.  To address this limitation, this study develops a method that improves predictive accuracy of GNN models by explicitly incorporating domain knowledge into the graph through virtual nodes.  The proposed approach introduces a structural bias into GNN models, which encourages the learning of hierarchical nonlinear relationships that are difficult for standard GNNs to capture.  By hierarchically representing relationships among observed variables via virtual nodes for condition, unobserved, and target variables, the model can progressively capture nonlinear relationships among features in a localized manner.  This enables the acquisition of an expanded function family compared to conventional additive and nonlinear functions, resulting in improving predictive accuracy. Experiments demonstrated that GNNs augmented with virtual nodes driven by domain knowledge consistently achieved a 15.0\% improvement in area under the curve (AUC) compared to baselines.  The proposed method structurally encodes domain knowledge. As a result, it improves interpretability and robustness and enables reliable deployment in industrial applications.

title: Dynamic Climate-Adaptive Agricultural Stabilization Framework for WTO Reform A Living-Capacity Indexed MSP and Grain Stability Architecture for Developing Economies
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

keywords: reforming agricultural support mechanisms within the World Trade Organization (WTO) Agreement on Agriculture (AoA).
Indexed MSP and Grain Stability Architecture for Developing Economies

detail.abstract: This paper proposes a Dynamic Climate-Adaptive Agricultural Stabilization Framework (DCASF) for reforming agricultural support mechanisms within the World Trade Organization (WTO) Agreement on Agriculture (AoA). Current WTO agricultural subsidy calculations rely heavily on static reference pricing methodologies, particularly the Aggregate Measurement of Support (AMS) framework based on outdated 1986-1988 external reference prices. These frameworks fail to adequately incorporate climate volatility, inflation dynamics, food security requirements, rural purchasing power, irrigation stress, and reserve stabilization needs. The proposed framework introduces a dynamic multi-layer agricultural stabilization architecture integrating: Climate-adjusted Minimum Support Pricing (MSP) Living-capacity indexed farmer support systems Dynamic reserve management Grain stabilization corridors Inflation-linked procurement logic Bilateral food-security reserve agreements Climate-triggered procurement flexibility Sustainable irrigation balancing Adaptive trade stabilization mechanisms The framework aims to transform agricultural support systems from static subsidy structures into adaptive food-security stabilization infrastructure. The proposal seeks to align WTO agricultural governance with modern realities including climate change, supply chain volatility, water scarcity, inflation instability, and geopolitical food-security risks.

title: How Could Emerging-Market Firms Navigate Institutional Deficiencies in Reverse Cross-Border M&As? Evidence from Directors' and Officers' Insurance in China
affiliations: City University of Hong Kong and Renmin University of China

detail.title: How Could Emerging-Market Firms Navigate Institutional Deficiencies in Reverse Cross-Border M&As? Evidence from Directors' and Officers' Insurance in China
detail.abstract: Overseas mergers and acquisitions (M&As) constitute a vital strategic avenue for firms from emerging economies. Utilizing a unique context of Chinese firms' inclination towards reverse cross-border M&As, this study investigates whether and how directors' and officers' liability insurance (D&O insurance) assists firms in alleviating institutional deficiencies during cross-border transactions. Using Chinese listed firms from 2011 to 2019, we find that firms covered by D&O insurance are more likely to initiate cross-border M&As. This finding still holds following the exogenous shock of the Sino-U.S. trade war, simultaneous equations and a series of sensitivity tests. Mechanism analyses indicate two channels: active risk-taking and improved investor protection. To further illustrate the investor protection channel, we show that the effect of D&O insurance is amplified in settings with more pronounced institutional deficiencies, i.e. when acquirers operate in weaker domestic legal environments or targets operate in stronger legal jurisdictions. These results suggest that D&O insurance not only enhances firms' overall capacity for active risk-taking, but also acts as a complement to inadequate domestic investor protection — a pattern particularly pronounced in the unique reverse cross-border context we exploit. Collectively, we highlight the effectiveness of D&O insurance in M&A activities of emerging-market firms, providing evidence on how financial instruments can function as effective complements to legal infrastructure in weak institutional environments.

keywords: Adaptive Non-Compensatory Credit Scoring Framework for Blockchain

detail.abstract:
Existing blockchain-native Real World Asset (RWA) lending protocols rely on binary pass/fail underwriting, single-metric financial ratios, or arithmetic aggregation — allowing strong performance on one dimension to compensate for material weakness on another. No existing protocol integrates cryptographic data integrity, legal enforceability, and identity binding as independently scored credit dimensions, nor addresses the unique risk profile of SME borrowers — particularly key-person concentration and succession failure. This paper addresses both gaps.

We present the 2Q–H–C–T–L–I framework: a three-tier, seven-component hybrid adaptive non-compensatory credit scoring model for institutional RWA invoice financing. All three tiers use adaptive geometric product aggregation: ; (Governance Layer); . The final composite score is where tier weights w₁, w₂, w₃ are adaptive. A score of 0 on any component collapses the tier score to 0 and S_rwa to 0 — the non-compensatory enforcement mechanism requires no separate hard gate. The complete adaptive parameter set (α, β, γ, δ, w₁, w₂, w₃, A₁, A₂, A₃) enables recalibration across jurisdictions, asset classes, borrower types, and lending contexts without structural redesign. For SME contexts where DAO validator infrastructure is unavailable, a six-component configuration (C omitted, T₂ = A₂ × H) is an explicit deployment option.

The framework is validated using a fully synthetic dataset constructed for research, education, and academic demonstration purposes — no real company, individual, or transaction is referenced. The synthetic case represents a Singapore invoice financing application (Tech-Fab Manufacturing Ltd., USD 250,000, Net 90) with 5-year financial statements, 24-month cash flow data, independent field verification, inspection, valuation, legal opinion, DAO governance vote, and full KYC/KYB/on-chain identity verification. Empirical results: T₁ = 0.8297, T₂ = 0.9965, T₃ = 0.9996, S_rwa = 0.9356 — Full Approval (w₁ = 0.35, w₂ = 0.30, w₃ = 0.35). Three stress tests confirm framework integrity across all three tiers. Binding constraints identified: Leverage (Lev = 0.5758) and Succession (score = 0.72) — the latter representing the most critical and commonly overlooked SME credit risk.

Four contributions: (C1) geometric mean non-compensatory aggregation across heterogeneous evidence types; (C2) oracle integrity as a continuously scored credit dimension; (C3) mandatory identity conjunction integrating KYC, KYB, and on-chain token binding; and (C4) a ten-parameter adaptive system (α, β, γ, δ, w₁, w₂, w₃, A₁, A₂, A₃) enabling institutional cross-context deployment with documented ±0.05 calibration guidance. Framework maps to ERC-3643 [1], ERC-4626 [2], Basel III [3], and MiCA [4]. Single-case validation (N = 1); portfolio backtesting and multi-assessor inter-rater study deferred to future work.

detail.abstract: Traditional demoscopy faces a structural validity crisis when attempting to categorize contemporary subjects through static, generational, or socioeconomic labels. This paper introduces a Multidimensional Ontology that conceptualizes the individual not as a fixed demographic unit, but as a system of internal tensions within a continuous state of transformation. By integrating Dynamic Clustering (unsupervised learning for real-time micro-cluster identification) and Multidimensional Narrative Analysis, we propose a "geometry of forces" to map social reality. The study demonstrates how individual concerns (micro-vectors) are pulled by systemic discourses (macro-vectors), creating resonance points that drive political or consumer action. This model transcends descriptive demographics to provide an operative capacity to synchronize with citizens amidst digital "infoxication" and shrinking attention spans.

title: Populism and the Composition of Government Spending
affiliations: and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Populism and the Composition of Government Spending

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that they have no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.

detail.abstract: We examine how left-wing and right-wing populist governments differ in their allocation of public expenditure and whether these differences contribute to government debt accumulation. Using a panel of 60 countries over 1870-2019, we decompose primary public spending into seven functional categories and apply compositional data methods that account for the mechanical constraints on spending shares. We find that left-wing populists systematically reallocate spending from military toward civilian categories, while rightwing populists tilt the civilian budget toward social protection at the expense of education and health. Panel VAR Granger causality tests confirm that the causal direction runs from spending composition to debt rather than the reverse. A mediation analysis suggests that aggregate GDP growth losses account for roughly two-thirds of the populism-to-debt link, with the remaining third attributable to direct deficit-financing effects of the composition shift. These results hold up under event-study pre-trend tests, leave-one-out analysis, lagged specifications, and sample splits by income level and region.

title: The Ecology of Sustainability Accounting:,A Population Ecology Theory of Carbon Reporting
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: The Ecology of Sustainability Accounting:,A Population Ecology Theory of Carbon Reporting
detail.abstract: This paper develops a population ecological theory of sustainability accounting as evolving organizational forms of variation, selection and retention embedded within market oriented socio ecological systems. The structural limits of carbon reporting of accounting-based climate governance specifically affect resource conservation by prioritizing financial disclosure over the circular economy management of material flows, thereby potentially hindering necessary resource efficiency and productivity improvements. Carbon reporting has not achieved convergence or transformative ecological accountability. The International Sustainability Standards Board (ISSB) case illustratively document dominance without displacing alternative reporting frameworks. Accounting-based climate standards prioritize financially oriented governance structures over material reductions in resource management and consumption. By shifting from technical optimization to evolutionary dynamics, this paper provides a novel framework for understanding systemic institutional barriers to global resource sustainability.

title: Quality-Aware Exploration Budget Allocation for Cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
affiliations: Seoul National University, Seoul National University and Seoul National University

detail.title: Quality-Aware Exploration Budget Allocation for Cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
detail.abstract: Cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) requires agents to discover joint strategies in a combinatorially large state-action space, yet effective coordination configurations are exceedingly rare. Intrinsic motivation, which augments task rewards with novelty bonuses, is popular approach for driving exploration, but its effectiveness hinges on the exploration intensity β, where too large a value overwhelms the task signal and causes coordination collapse, while too small a value prevents discovery of rare strategies. We address two complementary challenges, adapting β globally over training, andallocating the exploration budget across agents whose intrinsic reward signals vary in reliability. Our framework combines a return-conditioned sigmoid schedule (RCB) for global intensity control with a per-agent Reward Signal Quality (RSQ) metric that concentrates the exploration budget on agents with reliable signals. The core insight is that agents receiving noisy intrinsic rewards should explore less aggressively, and this allocation can be determined automatically from signal-to-noise statistics. Successor Distance (SD), a quasimetric intrinsic reward, naturally produces distinguishable per-agent signal quality, completing the framework with convergence and ordering preservation guarantees. On seven cooperative benchmarks (MPE, SMAX, MABrax), our method achieves top-tier returns across all environments.

title: The Eight Barrier Categories to Implementing Artificial Intelligence in Research: A Researchers' Consensus Qualitative Assessment
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, Masaryk University, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Maynooth University, affiliation not provided to SSRN, RISE Research Institutes of Sweden, affiliation not provided to SSRN, National Research Council of Italy, affiliation not provided to SSRN and Glasgow Caledonian University - Department of Physiotherapy and Paramedicine

detail.title: The Eight Barrier Categories to Implementing Artificial Intelligence in Research: A Researchers' Consensus Qualitative Assessment
detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly transforming research practices across disciplines, yet its integration into scientific workflows remains uneven and contested. While policy and institutional discussions increasingly promote the adoption of AI in science, less is known about the barriers researchers face in practice. This study addresses this gap through a structured qualitative analysis of stakeholder inputs collected using a concept-mapping approach involving internationally diverse researchers. Through iterative coding and consensus validation, we identify eight interrelated categories of barriers to AI implementation in research: data quality, governance and security; ethical, social and accountability concerns; methodological and epistemic incompatibilities; skill gaps and uneven AI literacy; inadequate technical infrastructure and access; financial and institutional constraints; regulatory and policy gaps; and issues of trust, transparency and explainability. These barriers are not independent but form a coupled system that shapes the conditions under which AI can be meaningfully integrated into scientific knowledge production. Importantly, because these barriers operate at the systemic, organisational, methodological, and epistemic levels of research, they remain relevant despite the rapid evolution of specific AI technologies and tools. The findings highlight a misalignment between top-down policy initiatives and bottom-up research practices, suggesting that current governance frameworks do not sufficiently account for the epistemic and operational realities of research environments. By articulating a researcher-centred typology of barriers and their relative urgency, this study contributes to the literature on innovation systems and the transformation of science, and provides actionable insights for policymakers, institutions, and research stakeholders seeking to enable responsible and effective AI integration.

title: Why Symbols Erode Scarcity: A Cognitive and Empirical Test of the ISSED Framework
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Why Symbols Erode Scarcity: A Cognitive and Empirical Test of the ISSED Framework

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that they have no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.

detail.abstract: This paper extends the Invisible Symbolic Supply Expansion Doctrine (ISSED), introduced in Yıldız (2026), from financialized commodities and cryptocurrency into the domains of human cognition and equity markets. We argue that in the symbolic age, no investment instrument is genuinely scarce. Formal numbers-21 million Bitcoin, 82,000 tonnes of gold, a fixed company share count-remain written on the page, but the actual symbolic claims that operate against those numbers expand without limit. Stated scarcity persists; functional scarcity does not. We propose a three-layer architecture of the doctrine-formal, cognitive, and behavioraland develop tozlaştırma (the act of symbolic dispersal) as the framework's central operative term. We further introduce the concept of the death point: the physical limit at which an asset can no longer be subdivided without losing its function. Assets with distant or absent death points are most susceptible to symbolic dispersal; assets with near death points retain residual scarcity for physical users while losing it entirely for symbolic users. At the cognitive layer, we identify three mechanisms-narrative displacement, unit price illusion, and anchoring disruption-through which the perception of scarcity is eroded. Channel instruments (splits) open access without absorbing flow, transmitting retail inflows directly to price and amplifying volatility. The common outcome-long-run erosion of the scarcity premium-is the signature of ISSED. Volatility direction is a mode-specific fingerprint, not a core prediction. We close with a structural account of how symbolic dispersal operates as an asymmetric distribution mechanism, with the upper tier of holders retaining position while the broader retail base saturates at the symbolic representation, and a brief programmatic extension into land and condominium ownership.

title: Human-Centered Experience Engineering Through Cognitive Design Patterns in Web-Based Systems

detail.title: Human-Centered Experience Engineering Through Cognitive Design Patterns in Web-Based Systems
detail.abstract: Human-centered experience engineering has become a critical discipline in the design of complex web-based systems as interaction density, functional scope, and user expectations continue to grow. Traditional user interface design approaches often emphasize visual aesthetics or isolated usability improvements, while overlooking the cognitive processes that shape how users perceive, reason, and act during interaction. This paper proposes a structured framework for human-centered experience engineering grounded in cognitive design patterns that systematically align system behavior with human cognitive capabilities. The study examines foundational cognitive principles such as attention management, working memory limitations, mental model formation, decision-making effort, and error perception, and demonstrates how these principles can be translated into reusable design patterns for web systems. A taxonomy of cognitive design patterns is introduced and mapped to experience intents, followed by an architectural perspective that explains how these patterns are operationalized within component-based front-end systems. The paper further presents evaluation methodologies for assessing cognitive experience quality and validates the proposed approach through an enterprise web workflow case study. Governance and operationalization strategies are discussed to ensure consistency and scalability across teams and systems. The findings illustrate that embedding cognitive design patterns as architectural constructs leads to improved interaction clarity, reduced cognitive load, and increased user confidence, establishing a sustainable foundation for human-centered web experience engineering.

title: MNEs and startup growth.Do good firms breed good startups?
affiliations: Department of Industrial Economics, Blekinge Institute of Technology, Henley Business School , University of Pisa, affiliation not provided to SSRN and Sapienza University of Rome - Department of Earth Sciences and Forecasting Research Center, Prevention and Control of Geological Risks

detail.title: MNEs and startup growth.Do good firms breed good startups?
detail.abstract: Building on a conceptual framework that links work experience to initial startup quality and post-entry performance through selection and treatment mechanisms, we posit that having individuals with work experience in Multinational Enterprises (MNEs) as a part of the initial startup team positively influences the initial startup size and post-entry performance of new firms. Using detailed Swedish data on over 13,000 new firms over the period 2000-2014, we find support for our conceptual framework. The effect of MNE experience on post-entry growth yet depends on the position the individuals had in the MNE. Our results highlight that MNEs are a specific type of firm that serves as breeding grounds and plays a role as ‘anchor’ firms; they support the development of startups by indirectly ‘feeding’ the economy with relevant experiences and skills.

title: Strengthening Trust and Transparency in Public Administration Through Qualitative Use of Artificial Intelligence
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and

detail.title: Strengthening Trust and Transparency in Public Administration Through Qualitative Use of Artificial Intelligence
detail.abstract: This study investigates the synergistic roles of transparency, explainable AI (XAI), participatory governance, and digital literacy in fostering public trust and enabling ethical Artificial Intelligence (AI) deployment within public administration. The primary objectives are to explore how algorithmic transparency and XAI cultivate public trust, and how participatory governance combined with elevated digital literacy empowers citizens to actively engage with and oversee AI systems throughout their lifecycles. Key research questions address the mechanisms by which algorithmic transparency and XAI can cultivate public trust, and how participatory governance and digital literacy enable citizen engagement with AI within public administration. Employing a comprehensive literature review and thematic analysis, the research synthesizes existing knowledge and proposes a framework for balancing AI innovation with public trust. Main findings reveal that transparency, explainable AI, citizen engagement, and digital literacy are interconnected pillars, collectively crucial for building trust in AI within public administration, where XAI's effectiveness is context-dependent. Key contributions include a comprehensive framework integrating XAI, transparency, participation, and digital literacy, offering actionable insights for enhancing trust and accountability in AI-driven public services. Limitations include the need for additional empirical research to validate and refine the framework

title: Role of a Section of the Bangladesh Armed Forces during the Caretaker Government of 2007-8: A Review

detail.title: Role of a Section of the Bangladesh Armed Forces during the Caretaker Government of 2007-8: A Review

declarations.declarationOfInterest: This is the property of Transparency International Bangladesh
declarations.ethicsApproval: Transparency International Bangladesh maintains research issues very strictly. No personal name, and identity is mentioned in the study report
declarations.funderStatement: Transparency International Bangladesh

contentFormat.other: Research Report; Working Paper on Military Corruption

detail.abstract: The present research report is aimed at assessing the nature, extent, and dimensions of alleged abuse of power by a section of the members of the armed forces, the factors behind corruption, and the implications thereof during the caretaker government of 2007–08. We understand that this report will provide important indications of the possible nature and risks of abuse of power when the armed forces are involved in civilian activities. The so‑called 1/11 situation arose and the armed‑forces‑backed caretaker government emerged primarily because of political divide and associated conflicts. The report shows that a number of positive contributions were made during the period. These include: Production of the national identity card and voter list with photographs within only 11 months; Reforms in some service‑delivery institutions, bringing vibrancy; Steps toward separation of the judiciary from the executive; Contribution to the conduct of a nationally and internationally credited election and transfer of power; Reduction of congestion of ships and containers in Chittagong Port; Drives to control unauthorized land grabbing; Collection of overdue electricity and gas bills However, taking advantage of immunity, a section of the members of the armed forces became involved in abuse of power, irregularities, and corruption, which affected the rule of law and human rights. As a result, the credibility of the armed forces and related intelligence agencies suffered. It may be mentioned that accountability and transparency of the armed forces are often researched worldwide. One example is the Government Defence Anti‑Corruption Index 2013, released by Transparency International UK on January 29, which analyzed various aspects of defence‑sector governance challenges in 82 countries, including Bangladesh (http://www.ti-bangladesh.org/files/GDACI-2013-Main%20Report.pdf). On the other hand, some members of the armed forces were reportedly brought to justice during the caretaker government, though the public has no access to such information. The armed forces are an extremely important public institution, run in the public interest with public resources. Open, information‑based, and objective discourse on their work, successes and failures, promises and challenges is indispensable for public interest. A key objective of this research is to create space for such debate. The Bangladesh Armed Forces have achieved national and international credibility for their commendable work ranging from natural‑disaster response to international peacekeeping. For the sake of further enhancing this credibility, there is no alternative to dispassionate discourse on vital aspects of public interest in the defence sector, especially from the point of view of confronting abiding challenges and reaping the best prospects. In this context, this research will contribute to discourse on ways to further upgrade professional excellence, integrity, transparency, and accountability, as well as create greater appreciation of the risks involved in engaging the armed forces in the civilian agenda. Such appreciation is indispensable for achieving higher levels of democratic practice and democratic institutionalization.

title: Bangladesh Public Service Commission: A Diagnostic Study

detail.title: Bangladesh Public Service Commission: A Diagnostic Study

declarations.declarationOfInterest: Transparency International Bangladesh owns this property

detail.abstract: The Bangladesh Pubic Service Commission (PSC) is one of the most important pillars of the National Integrity System having a key role in promoting excellence and integrity in the public service and administration of the country. PSC’s independence, political neutrality, transparency, accountability, integrity and effectiveness are fundamental prerequisites for carrying out its functions which include holding of competitive examinations for recruitment to the public service, recommend recruitments, promotions, discipline, employee appeal and other related matters. Lack of credibility and integrity of this vital Constitutional body not only leads to undermining of meritbased appointment in the public service, but is bound to have significant negative impact on the prospect of efficient, professional, transparent and accountable governance.  Alleged partisan influence through politically biased appointment of Chairmen and Members of the Commission, recruitment of ruling party activists and supporters, leakage of question papers for examinations, and various other forms of irregularities and corruption have led to erosion of trust upon this Constitutional body. The depth and breadth of corruption and governance failure in the country are widely perceived to be attributable to a significant extent to the failure of the PSC to ensure a credible process of appointments to the public service. However no comprehensive study has yet been done to diagnose the nature and extent of irregularities, corruption, governance problems and institutional weaknesses of PSC. The main objective of this study is to bridge this gap, and to recommend measures that may contribute to combating irregularities and corruption in the PSC. TIB has undertaken this diagnostic study in recognition of the critical importance of this vital institution, and growing erosion of its credibility.  The study was conducted by Md. Rezaul Karim, Research Officer of TIB, with the research support of Rumana Sharmin, Research Assistant. Other members of TIB’s Research Division also provided valuable support including feedback and suggestions at different stages.  Professor Muzaffer Ahmad, Chairman, Board of Trustees of TIB guided and supervised the study, for which we remain grateful. The report has been enriched by suggestions of Mr. M. Hafizuddin Khan, former Adviser to the Caretaker Government and currently Treasurer of TIB.  We gratefully acknowledge contributions of a number of key informants and distinguished individuals who helped the study at various stages by sharing valuable information, knowledge and expert opinion about the subject. For valuable comments and suggestions on an earlier draft of the report we are grateful to Dr. M. Akbar Ali Khan, former Cabinet Secretary & Adviser to the Caretaker Government; Dr. Sadat Hussain, former Cabinet Secretary; Dr. S.M. Al-Hussainy and Professor Md. Mostafa Chowdhury, former Chairmen of PSC; Professor Hamida Banu and Professor Khondoker Bazlul Hoq, former Members of the Commission; Dr. A.M.M. Shawkat Ali, Former Secretary; Professor Syed Giasuddin Ahmed of the  Department of Public Administration, University of Dhaka; and Professor Dr. A.Q.M. Mahboob of the Department of Geography and Environmental Science,  University of Dhaka. We also appreciate that a set of comments on an earlier draft was sent to us from the Commission, which was given due importance in revising the earlier version and annexed with this report.    We hope that the study will benefit the concerned authorities and stakeholders, especially the PSC, and those who will go through the recruitment process by it in the future. TIB would also welcome any constructive critique and suggestion from anyone which would facilitate further enrichment of the study.

title: Presidential Career Trajectories and Multidimensional University Performance: Evidence from a Developing Higher Education System
affiliations: Mohammed V University of Rabat

detail.title: Presidential Career Trajectories and Multidimensional University Performance: Evidence from a Developing Higher Education System
detail.abstract: This study examines how university presidents’ characteristics influence institutional performance in a developing higher education system. Using a panel of 278 president–year observations across 12 Moroccan public universities (2002–2024), it assesses the impact of leadership profiles on both research and funding performance. The findings suggest systematic leadership impact across multiple performance dimensions. On average, the most influential presidential profiles are those of: (i) outsiders; (ii) individuals born closer to their university’s location; (iii) male leaders; (iv) presidents transitioning from lower- to higher-ranked universities; and (v) more senior appointees. A novel measure of political proximity-measured as distance to the capital-indicates directionally consistent estimates across both research and funding outcomes, suggesting that presidents managing universities closer to the capital may exhibit weaker performance effects than those leading more distant institutions, although the estimates remain statistically inconclusive. The findings reveal a positive temporal evolution of university performance over the study period, reflecting broader system-wide dynamics, independently of presidential transitions. The study contributes to leadership and higher education literature by extending evidence to a non-competitive system and by jointly integrating scientific and financial performance into the analysis.

title: When analysts speak negatively: How bearish research reports shape managerial information provision during site visits
affiliations: Nanjing University, Nanjing University, Beijing Technology and Business University and Western Kentucky University - Department of Accounting and Finance

detail.title: When analysts speak negatively: How bearish research reports shape managerial information provision during site visits
detail.abstract: Using data on sell-side analyst site visits to Chinese A-share listed firms from 2013 to 2022, we examine how top executives (the chairperson or CEO) and the firm strategically steer information in response to the tone of the visiting analysts’ prior research reports. We find that when the tone of an analyst’s pre-visit report is more negative, 1) top executives are less likely to attend the visit, 2) the reception team is smaller, and 3) the firm responds to questions with shorter and less detailed answers, all of which indicate that firms adopt an information-avoidance strategy toward analysts who provide negative information. This strategic avoidance is more pronounced when the firm has already faced negative media coverage, when star analysts participate in the site visit, or when more institutional investors are present at the site visit. Further analysis shows that, after site visits attended by top executives, analysts are more likely to prepare a post-visit report. However, these post-visit reports are associated with lower forecast accuracy and smaller post-visit accuracy gains. This pattern suggests that top executives selectively grant access to analysts who previously issued non-negative tone reports, and these analysts manage their subsequent disclosures, thereby worsening the overall information environment of the firm.

title: The Outsider Effect on Innovation: CEO Non-localness and Innovation Novelty
affiliations: Shandong University at Weihai and Shandong University at Weihai

detail.title: The Outsider Effect on Innovation: CEO Non-localness and Innovation Novelty
detail.abstract: Innovation novelty is a critical driver of sustained competitive advantage, yet the influence of executive characteristics—particularly CEO non-localness—remains underexplored. Building on the attention-based view (ABV), this study theorizes that non-local CEOs, by avoiding deep localized embeddedness, are less constrained by familiarity traps and status quo biases, enabling broader exploration of heterogeneous knowledge domains. We further propose dual moderating effects: external regional openness attenuates this relationship through an information substitution mechanism, whereas internal board surname diversity strengthens it by enhancing cognitive inclusiveness and decision-making empowerment. Using panel data from Chinese listed firms (2012–2023) and IPC-based patent recombination metrics to quantify innovation novelty, our analyses provide robust empirical support for these predictions. This research advances the literature on ABV, executive characteristics, and corporate governance by elucidating how contextual boundary conditions shape the impact of CEO non-localness on organizational innovation.

title: The Moving Criterion: Sequential Justification  Shifts in Scientific Access Moderation
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: The Moving Criterion: Sequential Justification  Shifts in Scientific Access Moderation

keywords.keywords: quiet exclusionindependent researchersinstitutional accessscholarly gatekeepingacademic publishingrepository moderation

detail.abstract: Scientific moderation is typically framed as a process based on explicit, actionable criteria that enable revision. This paper identifies a recurrent pattern, termed sequential justification shift, in which initial, localized feedback is followed by broader or non-actionable justifications. Across documented cases from preprint platforms, evaluation moves from correctable issues to global judgments, external constraints, or non-revisable assessments of contribution.These shifts remove any clear path to compliance while preserving the appearance of procedural responsiveness. We interpret this dynamic as a process-level mechanism of quiet exclusion, in which interaction persists but does not lead to resolution or completion. Exclusion thus arises not only through explicit rejection, but through post-engagement changes in evaluative criteria that prevent convergence.

title: Congestion Pricing in Low-Altitude Airspace: A Stackelberg Approachto UTM Markets
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Congestion Pricing in Low-Altitude Airspace: A Stackelberg Approachto UTM Markets
detail.abstract: The rapid expansion of drone operations is turning low-altitude airspace into an economically significant but increasingly congested resource. Although the Unmanned Traffic Management (UTM) literature has advanced substantially in operational, safety, and interoperability issues, the economic mechanisms required to price airspace, regulate market entry, and internalize congestion externalities remain largely underdeveloped. This paper addresses that gap by proposing an analytical framework in which the regulator and competing drone operators interact as a two-stage Stackelberg game. In the base formulation, the regulator sets a unit tariff to maximize regulatory revenue; in the extended formulation, the regulator adopts a Pigouvian stance, internalizing congestion externalities that scale with aggregate traffic density. We derive closed-form expressions for the equilibrium tariff, market quantity, and operator profits, and we prove that the optimal congestion-aware tariff is strictly increasing in the regional congestion parameter, providing a theoretical foundation for spatially and temporally differentiated pricing. The model is calibrated with 2025 operational data from SARPAS the Brazilian national UTM platform administered by DECEA and its robustness is assessed through Monte Carlo simulation over stochastic demand and cost parameters. The results reveal a fundamental trade-off: increased competition enhancesallocative efficiency and price stability but erodes the regulator’s revenue base and amplifies the sensitivity of welfare to congestion costs. The empirical calibration shows that congestion-efficient tariffs in dense urban cells (São Paulo) are 40–60% higher than a uniform national tariff, a magniude that uniform pricing cannot accommodate without substantial efficiency losses. These findings contribute to the transport-economics, market-design, and UTM literatures by integrating strategic regulation, congestion externalities, and empirical calibration within a single framework, and they offer actionable guidance for the design of scalable, financially sustainable UTM systems.

title: Forecast-Performance-Calibrated Robust Scheduling of CHP-Centered Microgrids Under Coupled Electric–Thermal Load Uncertainty
affiliations: Clarkson University

detail.title: Forecast-Performance-Calibrated Robust Scheduling of CHP-Centered Microgrids Under Coupled Electric–Thermal Load Uncertainty
detail.abstract: Combined heat and power (CHP)-centered microgrids are highly sensitive in day-ahead scheduling to uncertainty in electric and heating load forecasts, yet such uncertainty is often represented using fixed-percentage margins or generic uncertainty sets that do not reflect historical forecast behavior. To address this gap, this paper proposes a data-driven robust unit commitment and economic dispatch (UC/ED) framework that links forecast-performance-based uncertainty learning with tractable robust scheduling. Uncertainty bounds are learned from historical actual-to-forecast ratios using empirical quantile analysis and are constructed separately for electric and heating demands to capture season-dependent and load-specific forecast error characteristics. These learned bounds are then embedded in a budgeted robustmixed-integer linear programming model that co-optimizes CHP units, battery energy storage, photovoltaic generation, and grid transactions while preserving electric–thermal coupling. A case study using IEEE Dataport residential building data shows pronounced seasonal differences in learned uncertainty bounds, withwinter 85th-percentile deviations of 24% for electric load and 19% for heating load, compared with 5% and 4% in autumn. These differences lead to markedly different robustness premiums: operating cost increases by 34.0% in winter but only 10.0% in autumn from the deterministic to the most conservative case.

title: Star myopia: Academician leaders and university technology transfer
affiliations: Nanjing University of Finance and Economics

detail.title: Star myopia: Academician leaders and university technology transfer
detail.abstract: Academically accomplished stars in scientific fields are highly sought after by universities and even government departments. However, the actual impact of these academician leaders on university R&D activities remains elusive. Employing a difference-in-differences (DID) approach, this study delves into the causal link between star scientists’ leadership and university technology transfer. Findings reveal that appointing academicians as university presidents significantly diminishes technology transfer levels in the first two years, particularly in non-elite universities and those highly reliant on government funding. Such appointments exacerbate misallocation of research resources and reduce productivity, despite showing no positive effect on the acquisition of research funding. While publication quantity remains unaffected, academic impact wanes. Conversely, universities led by less renowned national-level talents witness improved research efficiency and technology transfer. This study underscores the potential lack of effective research leadership among star scientists, highlighting the perils of “star myopia” in academic appointments.

title: Exploring uncertainties across the modelling chain in ML-based streamflow forecasting
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, University of Belgrade, University of New South Wales (UNSW) - School of Civil and Environmental Engineering, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Exploring uncertainties across the modelling chain in ML-based streamflow forecasting
detail.abstract: Operational streamflow forecasts underpin flood preparedness and reservoir operations, yet their utility is often constrained by poorly characterized and attributed predictive uncertainty. In machine-learning-based forecasting, uncertainty is frequently omitted or reported as a single aggregate output, leaving it unclear which parts of the end-to-end forecasting chain drive overconfidence and forecast degradation, particularly with increasing lead time. In this work, we develop an end-to-end uncertainty decomposition framework for operational streamflow forecasting that attributes predictive uncertainty across meteorological forcing choice, feature design, model architecture, hyperparameter optimization, and training variability, evaluated across multi-day horizons. The decomposition reveals a systematic, horizon-dependent shift in dominant uncertainty sources, with forcing-related contributions increasing with lead time while model-structure and feature choices remain influential at shorter horizons. During high-flow events, predictive intervals remain essential because pipeline heterogeneity can bias the central estimate even when ensemble dispersion widens appropriately. Tuning contributes little to the uncertainty budget but strongly affects compute–skill trade-offs, with Bayesian optimization delivering the most favorable cost–benefit performance under the tested constraints. Together, these results provide actionable guidance for operational freshwater management, showing where investment yields the largest reliability gains: model design at short lead times and forcing quality at longer lead times. This guidance can reduce the risk of costly or unsafe decisions in flood preparedness, reservoir operation, and other critical decision-making contexts in water management.

title: The Evolving Prominence of Framing Approaches in New Ventures Across Development Stages and Innovation Types
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Nyenrode Business University and Erasmus University Rotterdam (EUR) - Rotterdam School of Management (RSM), Amsterdam Business School

detail.title: The Evolving Prominence of Framing Approaches in New Ventures Across Development Stages and Innovation Types
detail.abstract: Entrepreneurship research highlights the importance of communication in securing stakeholder support, yet we have limited understanding of how entrepreneurial framing evolves as ventures develop. In this study, we examine how new ventures adapt their framing over time. Drawing on a qualitative study of 58 ventures in the Netherlands and Germany, we identify three distinct framing approaches, positioning, grounding, and envisioning, and show that they vary in their relative prominence over time. Rather than replacing one another, these approaches can be selectively reweighted as ventures navigate changing legitimacy demands across development stages. We further show that these patterns differ depending on whether ventures pursue radical or incremental innovations. We develop a process model of entrepreneurial framing that explains how ventures can sustain legitimacy over time.

title: Spatiotemporal Propagation of Travel Time Variability in Bus Networks: A Network-Based Analysis of Critical Hubs
affiliations: University of Las Palmas de Gran Canaria and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Spatiotemporal Propagation of Travel Time Variability in Bus Networks: A Network-Based Analysis of Critical Hubs
detail.abstract: Travel time variability is a key challenge in public transport systems, yet its propagation mechanisms across urban networks remain insufficiently understood. This paper introduces a data-driven temporal network framework for reconstructing and analyzing the spatiotemporal propagation of travel time variability from large-scale GPS observations in urban bus systems. Unlike conventional reliability approaches based on predefined topological structures or static metrics, the proposed methodology infers directed propagation pathways directly from empirical temporal interactions.A PageRank-based centrality measure is used to identify critical hubs that drive the spread of variability across the network. The framework is applied to the bus network of Tenerife, revealing a heterogeneous spatial structure with a limited set of dominant hubs. Temporal analysis comparing peak and off-peak periods shows a moderate overlap in hub sets (Jaccard index = 0.60) and a high rank correlation (Spearman rho = 0.865), indicating a stable backbone of influential nodes. However, substantial rank shifts are observed, highlighting a dynamic redistribution of propagation roles under different demand conditions.The results demonstrate that travel time variability propagation is governed by a hybrid structure combining persistent core hubs and temporally adaptive nodes. These findings provide new insights into the dynamics of public transport systems and offer practical implications for network monitoring, robustness analysis, and targeted interventions.

title: Port performance evaluation in a competitive environment: A Multi-Port evidence-based approach
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Port performance evaluation in a competitive environment: A Multi-Port evidence-based approach
detail.abstract: This study aims to provide a new framework for evaluating port performance by incorporating the perspectives of diverse stakeholders. The study’s originality is in introducing transport network of roads and railways and port centrality as indicators for assessing the relative importance of port geographic location and for evaluating port performance. Based on data retrieved from literature and expert opinions, a model for measuring port performance is established in a several hierarchical structure which includes assessments and relative importance of each criterion and sub-criterion. First, the issue of port performance is introduced, followed by its formulation as a multiple attribute decision analysis problem. To deal with a formulated port performance assessment problem of both a quantitative and qualitative nature under uncertainties, rule and utility-based techniques for transforming assessment information are applied. A decision making trial and evaluation laboratory is applied to calculate the weights of dependent criteria in the model, while Evidential Reasoning algorithm is applied to calculate a comprehensive and belief-based assessments as well as to rank ports with expected utilities. By providing a flexible diagnostic framework and model, study enables stakeholders to effectively measure and monitor port performance according to their specific requirements and to identify port’s strengths and weaknesses.

title: A novel dynamic adaptive new information priority grey convolutional model and its application in renewable energy generation prediction
affiliations: Henan Agricultural University, Henan Agricultural University, Henan Agricultural University and Henan Agricultural University

detail.title: A novel dynamic adaptive new information priority grey convolutional model and its application in renewable energy generation prediction
detail.abstract: Accurately forecasting renewable energy is crucial for future power grid planning and operation. However, different types of renewable energy exhibit differentiated nonlinear characteristics, which makes forecasting extremely challenging. To address this, a novel dynamic adaptive grey convolution model is proposed. Meanwhile, hydropower with a saturated “S”-shaped growth trend, and bioenergy with monotonically increasing yet unstable change rates are selected as research objects. A comparison with five benchmark models confirms the forecasting reliability of the proposed model. The forecasting results show that the average annual growth rates of hydropower and bioenergy generation during the forecasting period are 0.55% and 21.13% respectively. Accurately forecasting the growth trajectories of hydropower and bioenergy generation not only optimizes renewable energy integration efficiency but also delivers actionable, data-driven insights to support strategic decision-making in sustainable energy policy.

title: LHEMO: LLM-Based Heuristic Evolution for Multi-Objective Sensor-Weapon-Target Assignment
affiliations: National University of Defense Technology, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, National University of Defense Technology, National University of Defense Technology, affiliation not provided to SSRN, National University of Defense Technology, National University of Defense Technology, National University of Defense Technology and National University of Defense Technology

detail.title: LHEMO: LLM-Based Heuristic Evolution for Multi-Objective Sensor-Weapon-Target Assignment
detail.abstract: The multi-objective sensor--weapon--target assignment (SWTA) problem requires the coordinated allocation of heterogeneous sensing and action resources under conflicting objectives such as mission effectiveness, resource consumption, and response time. Existing SWTA solvers, including classical multi-objective evolutionary algorithms and recent large language model (LLM)-based automated heuristic design (AHD) methods, either rely heavily on hand-crafted search components or transfer poorly to SWTA because of heterogeneous entities, strict feasibility requirements, and the need for Pareto-oriented feedback. To address these challenges, we propose LHEMO, an LLM-based heuristic evolution framework for multi-objective SWTA. LHEMO adopts a bi-level architecture in which the outer level evolves executable heuristic programs through LLM-guided operators, while the inner level evaluates each candidate within a unified multi-objective solver. Within this architecture, two reconstruction operators expand exploration through line-level and module-level code regeneration, a validation-and-repair mechanism recovers invalid candidates, a cross-generation reflection mechanism reuses evolutionary experience, and a structured seed heuristic stabilizes early-stage search. A Pareto-oriented fitness based on hypervolume and a feasibility penalty further guides the evolution toward high-quality trade-off solutions. Experiments on a benchmark ranging from 8 to 320 targets show that LHEMO consistently outperforms both classical multi-objective baselines and representative LLM-based AHD baselines, achieving up to 191% hypervolume improvement on the largest-scale instances. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of LLM-driven heuristic evolution as a practical paradigm for structured, constraint-intensive multi-objective resource allocation problems.

title: Statistical Reliability of Gradient-Boosted Ensembles versus ANFIS for Daily Suspended Sediment Concentration Prediction in a Monsoon-Dominated, Highly Variable River Basin
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and Tribhuvan University - Institute of Engineering Pulchowk Campus

detail.title: Statistical Reliability of Gradient-Boosted Ensembles versus ANFIS for Daily Suspended Sediment Concentration Prediction in a Monsoon-Dominated, Highly Variable River Basin
detail.abstract: Accurate daily suspended sediment concentration (SSC) prediction is essential for hydropower reservoir management in monsoon-dominated, highly variable river systems. This study compares LightGBM and CatBoost against the Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Inference System (ANFIS) using eight years of daily hydrometeorological data from the Jalkundi catchment, West Rapti River, Nepal (WY2016–WY2023). A five-fold expanding-window cross-validation framework was combined with a triple significance protocol comprising a one-sample t-test, Wilcoxon signed-rank test, and 10,000-iteration bootstrap confidence interval, with the sediment rating curve (R² = 0.1545) as the null hypothesis. LightGBM satisfied all three criteria (t-test: p = 0.010; Wilcoxon: p = 0.031; bootstrap 95% CI: [0.299, 0.581]; test R² = 0.627). CatBoost attained marginally higher test R² (0.633) but failed the Wilcoxon test (p = 0.063), indicating borderline reliability. ANFIS achieved test-year R² = 0.495 yet a cross-validated mean of 0.042 ± 0.249 (95% CI: [−0.187, 0.257]), failing all significance tests. This collapse is attributed to the structural curse of dimensionality, which restricts ANFIS inputs to five of thirteen available features, producing severely degraded high-flow performance (R² = −2.083). Annual sediment load errors were −6.5% (LightGBM), −12.6% (CatBoost), and −28.2% (ANFIS). These results establish that gradient-boosted ensembles substantially outperform ANFIS in high-dimensional SSC modelling in monsoon-dominated catchments, and that expanding-window cross-validation with formal significance testing is indispensable for credible model evaluation.

title: The Gilded Cage: A Theory of Covert Control in Leader-Subordinate Relationships
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: The Gilded Cage: A Theory of Covert Control in Leader-Subordinate Relationships
detail.abstract: A financial services manager kept a toxic subordinate busy with choice projects—not to develop him, but to monitor him. A university chair gave a complaining faculty member preferred teaching assignments before he could ask, not because he deserved them, but to prevent him from going to the dean. These leaders built a "gilded cage": a relationship appearing as genuine investment but functioning as covert control. Leaders face this dilemma when subordinates cannot be punished or terminated—due to legal protections, political connections, or organizational constraints—but cannot be ignored. This article introduces containment leadership—a leader's strategic allocation of resources and proximity to monitor, pacify, and limit a subordinate's potential for disruption—and integrates conservation of resources, social exchange, attribution, and surveillance theories to explain why leaders contain, why subordinates remain unaware, and how containment operates. Four dimensions—performative investment, surveillance proximity, preemptive pacification, affective dissonance—articulate containment’s structure. A multi-level model shows how containment creates self-reinforcing dynamics that trap leaders, subordinates, and organizations. The theory challenges core assumptions in leader-member exchange and social exchange theory by revealing that behavioral markers of high-quality relationships can coexist with unilateral deception. It extends conservation of resources theory by demonstrating that resource protection strategies can become resource-depleting traps. Ethical implications and a research agenda address a phenomenon defined by invisibility.

title: A World Without Artificial Intelligence: Economic, Social, and Technological Consequences
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: A World Without Artificial Intelligence: Economic, Social, and Technological Consequences

declarations.declarationOfInterest: NIL

detail.abstract: Artificial Intelligence("AI") has rapidly evolved from a specialised computational tool into a foundational layer of modern economic infrastructure. Governments, corporations, educational institutions, healthcare systems, and financial markets increasingly rely on intelligent automation for decision-making, optimisation, prediction, and operational efficiency. However, as AI systems become more deeply embedded in economic life, concerns regarding labour displacement, the concentration of wealth, democratic accountability, and long-term human dependency have intensified. This paper examines a hypothetical but increasingly relevant policy question: what would occur if individuals, corporations, or governments deliberately slowed, restricted, or abandoned large-scale AI adoption?
