detail.abstract:
This whitepaper presents a practical, enterprise‑scale governance model for Software Bills of Materials (SBOMs) that moves beyond static, compliance‑only generation toward continuous, policy‑driven software supply‑chain assurance. Drawing on real‑world implementations in AI platforms and safety‑critical automotive systems, it defines a full lifecycle architecture that includes automated SBOM generation, ingestion, normalization, enrichment, VEX‑driven triage, and policy‑as‑code release gating. The paper analyzes why SBOM governance remains difficult—fragmented formats, inconsistent supplier deliverables, missing integrity controls, AI/ML‑specific risks, and lack of ownership—and introduces a threat model addressing SBOM tampering, omissions, provenance failures, and model‑weight poisoning. It further maps governance controls to NIST SSDF, CISA minimum elements, and EU Cyber Resilience Act requirements.

The whitepaper provides a reference architecture, implementation RACI, KPIs/OKRs, supplier‑scoring framework, audit‑evidence patterns, and a 90‑day minimum viable program with a one‑year roadmap. By treating SBOMs as a governed data pipeline with continuous evidence, organizations can achieve scalable risk‑based decisioning, faster audit cycles, supplier trust, and regulatory‑ready assurance across complex multi‑product environments—particularly those integrating AI/ML components.

title: Petroleum Inventory Trajectories Under the 2026 Strait of Hormuz Closure: A Mass-Balance Forecast Model with Sensitivity Analysis and Falsifiable Predictions
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: Petroleum Inventory Trajectories Under the 2026 Strait of Hormuz Closure: A Mass-Balance Forecast Model with Sensitivity Analysis and Falsifiable Predictions

keywords: operational floor. JEL Codes: Q41 (Energy: Demand and Supply)

detail.abstract: This paper develops a weekly mass-balance forecasting model for U.S. petroleum inventories during the 2026 Strait of Hormuz closure crisis and applies it to identify the calendar dates at which Strategic Petroleum Reserve, commercial crude oil, motor gasoline, and distillate fuel oil stocks are forecast to cross their respective operational floors. Using publicly available data from the U.S. Energy Information Administration as of the week ending May 1, 2026, the model yields a base-case national motor gasoline floor crossing of July 17, 2026 (± 2 weeks under reasonable parameter perturbation), a distillate inventory level already below the operational floor as of the data cutoff, and a SPR trajectory that does not cross its political minimum within the 16-week forecast horizon at current drawdown rates. Five conditional scenarios are evaluated. Drawing on the well-established structural tightness of PADD 1 (East Coast) and PADD 5 (West Coast) relative to the national average, the paper argues that regional retail gasoline allocation events should be expected approximately 2-4 weeks in advance of national-level floor crossings, placing the most probable window for visible pump-level shortages at June 22 to July 17, 2026. Five falsifiable predictions are stated. The paper concludes by examining the price-quantity coupling that exposes domestic consumers directly to global market clearing and outlines the policy levers-export controls, accelerated SPR releases, and demand-side measures-whose invocation or non-invocation will determine the realized path.

title: A Bayesian-optimized physics-informed neural network for predicting ceiling smoke temperature distribution in compartment fires
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and Dalian University of Technology

detail.title: A Bayesian-optimized physics-informed neural network for predicting ceiling smoke temperature distribution in compartment fires
detail.abstract: Accurately predicting the ceiling smoke temperature distribution is essential for effective fire safety design in compartment fires. This study proposes a Bayesian-optimized physics-informed neural network (BO-PINN) for predicting compartment ceiling smoke temperatures, which consists of a physics-informed neural network aided by Bayesian optimization with a Tree-structured Parzen Estimator (BO-TPE). Compared to a data-driven neural network with the same structure, the BO-PINN model maintains high prediction accuracy under sparse-data conditions. Using 1% of the training data, the BO-PINN model accurately predicts the spatio-temporal evolution of ceiling smoke temperature fields across diverse heat release rate (HRR) scenarios, achieving a coefficient of determination (R²) of 0.988. Repeated random validation demonstrates the BO-PINN model’s stability. The Structural Similarity Index (SSIM) values for the temperature field reconstructed from discrete points remained consistently above 0.92. The proposed BO-PINN model provides an accurate and physically consistent solution for the reconstruction of smoke temperature fields in compartment fires, which demonstrates the potential to contribute to fire risk assessment and safety engineering.

title: Does Program Duration Matter? Evidence from Girls' Education Interventions in Northern Nigeria
affiliations: Florida International University (FIU)

detail.title: Does Program Duration Matter? Evidence from Girls' Education Interventions in Northern Nigeria
detail.abstract: This paper examines the impact of the Girls' Education Project Phase 3 (GEP3), a largescale girls' education programme implemented in northern Nigeria between 2012 and 2022. Using four rounds of the Nigeria Multiple Indicator Cluster Survey from 2007 to 2021 and a triple difference-indifferences design, I compare girls relative to boys, treated states relative to non-treated northern states, and post-programme periods relative to pre-programme periods. The results show that GEP3 increased girls' school attendance and improved grade progression, with substantially larger effects in states exposed to earlier programme phases. In legacy states, girls' attendance increased by 3.2 percentage points, grade-forage progression improved by 0.179 standard deviations, and dropout declined by 1.6 percentage points. Effects in newer programme states are smaller and generally imprecise. Heterogeneity estimates indicate that attendance gains are concentrated among poorer households, while reductions in dropout are strongest in legacy states with longer cumulative programme exposure. Event-study estimates are broadly consistent with the parallel trends assumption and indicate post-programme improvements in girls' schooling outcomes. The findings highlight the importance of sustained implementation and cumulative programme exposure in improving girls' educational participation and progression in low-income settings.

detail.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has emerged as a transformative force in modern Human Resource Management (HRM), significantly influencing the regulation and administration of workforce activities within organizations. This conceptual article examines the role of AI in regulating human resources by analyzing its applications in recruitment, employee performance evaluation, workforce monitoring, payroll management, training and development, employee engagement, and predictive workforce analytics. The study highlights how AI-driven technologies improve organizational efficiency, reduce human bias, enhance decision-making accuracy, and support strategic HR planning through data-driven insights. Furthermore, the article discusses the growing significance of AI in ensuring compliance, enhancing employee satisfaction, and managing remote and hybrid work environments. While AI offers numerous advantages such as automation, cost reduction, productivity enhancement, and predictive capabilities, it also raises important concerns related to privacy, ethical issues, algorithmic bias, cybersecurity, and job displacement. The article emphasizes the necessity of balancing technological innovation with human values and ethical HR practices. It concludes that AI should function as a supportive mechanism rather than a replacement for human judgment in HR regulation. The future of HRM will increasingly depend on the intelligent integration of AI systems that promote organizational sustainability, workforce development, and responsible managerial practices.

title: Analyzing Carbon Removal Technology Hype Cycles Through Large Language Models
affiliations: RWTH Aachen University - RWTH Aachen University, Students and RWTH Aachen University

detail.title: Analyzing Carbon Removal Technology Hype Cycles Through Large Language Models
detail.abstract: This study examines whether Large Language Models (LLMs) can support the development of sentiment-based indicators for technological hype cycles, characterized by optimistic media language during hype phases and negative sentiment during periods of disillusionment. The rapid growth of digital news makes manual tracking of sentiment trends impractical. Traditional computational approaches relying on basic natural language processing often fail to capture context in long-form texts. LLMs offer a scalable alternative by enabling context-aware sentiment analysis across large collections of complex news articles. The study introduces an LLM-driven methodology to analyze temporal sentiment patterns in English-language news coverage over a 16-year period, focusing on carbon removal technologies. The approach extracts sentiments from major news sources and maps them over time to identify media-driven hype dynamics. This framework enables systematic analysis of technologies such as Bioenergy with Carbon Capture and Storage, afforestation/reforestation, Direct Air Capture, and ocean-based carbon capture. The key finding is that media sentiment tracking can complement other innovation indicators in the mapping of a Hype Cycle, revealing that CRT domain as a whole is heading towards a plateau of productivity.

title: A multi-timescale closed-loop scheduling framework for industrial park energy systems considering state evolution of energy storage and energy-intensive loads
affiliations: Inner Mongolia University of Technology, Inner Mongolia University of Technology, Inner Mongolia University of Technology, Inner Mongolia University of Technology, Inner Mongolia University of Technology, Inner Mongolia University of Technology and Inner Mongolia University of Technology

detail.title: A multi-timescale closed-loop scheduling framework for industrial park energy systems considering state evolution of energy storage and energy-intensive loads
detail.abstract: High energy-intensive industrial parks dominated by electrolytic aluminum production are gradually transitioning toward low-carbon energy systems with high renewable penetration. In this process, conventional intra-day model predictive scheduling methods often fail to account for execution deviations in practical operation, thereby causing cumulative mismatches in the state of charge (SOC) of energy storage systems and electrolytic cell temperature. To address this issue, this paper proposes a closed-loop coordinated scheduling framework across multiple time scales. An execution-layer model is introduced to analyze the mismatch mechanisms between the planning and execution layers for both energy storage systems and electrolytic aluminum processes. A state deviation propagation model is subsequently established. Based on the SOC and electrolytic cell temperature states, a dual-state-feedback rolling correction mechanism is then developed to suppress state deviation propagation, and its effectiveness is theoretically validated. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method effectively improves SOC tracking accuracy and electrolytic cell temperature regulation in the presence of forecasting errors and model uncertainty. In addition, cumulative state drift is mitigated, leading to enhanced operational stability.

title: Hybrid optimization for integration of renewable energy systems into smart grids
affiliations: Bahauddin Zakariya University

detail.title: Hybrid optimization for integration of renewable energy systems into smart grids
detail.abstract: Due to the substantial growth in human beings, daily consumption of energy is rising. Increasing electricity production to keep up with population increase is one strategy, albeit it is usually almost unattainable. Electricity usage and related costs may be decreased by managing demand. In order to lower energy consumption, we use Demand-side Monitoring (DSM) to schedule various devices on loads. Two important functions of the smart grid are lowering energy prices and integrating energy from renewable sources. To address the optimisation challenges, we propose a hybrid swarm-driven Harris Hawks' optimisation (S–HHO) technique. The recommended strategy offers a wide range of options for both homes and businesses. The suggested method was contrasted with wind-driven optimisation (WDO), multiple-objective genetic algorithm (MOGA), bilateral particle swarm optimisation (BPSO), and multi-objective particle swarm optimisation (MOPSO). TheMATLAB program was used to generate simulation outcomes. The findings demonstrate that compared to other techniques, such as WDO, BPSO, MOPSO, and MOGA, the enhanced hybrid optimisation technique S–HHO lowers the peak-to-average ratio (PAR) and computation time more effectively.

title: Adaptive Energy Stations for Sustainable Transport Infrastructure: Real-Time Dispatch Optimization Using Marginal Grid Emissions and Low-Carbon Fuel Pathways
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Adaptive Energy Stations for Sustainable Transport Infrastructure: Real-Time Dispatch Optimization Using Marginal Grid Emissions and Low-Carbon Fuel Pathways
detail.abstract: Transport decarbonization requires not only low-carbon vehicle technologies but also infrastructure capable of selecting the lowest-emission energy pathway in real time. This study introduces Adaptive Energy Stations (AES), multi-fuel transport-energy nodes that integrate marginal grid-emission signals, fuel life-cycle carbon intensities, wholesale electricity prices, and vehicle operating constraints into a station-level dispatch optimization. A proof-of-method implementation is demonstrated for the California Independent System Operator (CAISO) zone using 168 hourly service events over 1--8 January 2026, combining WattTime marginal operating emissions, CAISO locational marginal prices, eGRID CAMX annual-average factors, and declared vehicle and fuel-pathway parameters. For plug-in hybrid electric vehicles (PHEVs), AES dispatch reduced mean emissions from 145 to 90~\gcoeqkm{} --- a 38\% improvement over a static annual-average baseline --- by shifting electric charging toward low-carbon grid intervals and substituting cellulosic E85 during high-carbon periods. Monte Carlo uncertainty propagation (10,000 draws) established practical equivalence between CAISO-zone battery electric vehicle (BEV) and cellulosic E85 pathways under a $\pm 25$~\gcoeqkm{} margin, though equivalence failed at $\pm 10$~\gcoeqkm{}. Sensitivity analyses for ERCOT, MISO--MROW, and ISO--NE extension zones revealed region-dependent emission rankings, with BEV advantages diminishing under higher grid carbon intensity. The framework supports performance-based, technology-neutral decarbonization policy by demonstrating that operational life-cycle carbon information materially alters station-level energy-pathway selection. Full deployment requires validated marginal-emission access, supply-chain verification, user-behavior characterization, and cybersecurity safeguards.

title: How Investor Position Influences Innovation: A Complex Network Perspective
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, Southwest Jiaotong University, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: How Investor Position Influences Innovation: A Complex Network Perspective
detail.abstract: This study empirically examines the impact pathways of investors' network positions on corporate innovation from a micro-level perspective. Findings reveal the following: First, an investor's centrality position within the network significantly and positively influences the patent output of its portfolio firms. Second, the impact of network position on innovation collaboration strategies is more complex: an investor's proactive outward connections actually inhibit the breadth and depth of corporate innovation. More critically, the reputation and activity level of an investor's direct neighbors also exert a significant negative influence on the breadth and depth of corporate collaboration, revealing that high-quality partners may trigger relationship lock-in effects. Third, the breadth and depth of innovation collaboration serve as key mediating channels through which network position influences innovation output, with the mediating effect of collaboration depth being particularly crucial. Fourth, these mechanisms are moderated by internal and external contextual factors: the heterogeneity of joint investment teams significantly amplifies the innovation returns from network position advantages, while a favorable market environment weakens the effectiveness of proactive connection strategies. Further causal analysis indicates that macro-level innovation policies significantly enhance innovation output, but their impact primarily relies on direct empowerment rather than restructuring collaborative networks.

title: An interpretable few-shot load forecasting framework integrating feature interaction modeling and adaptive transfer learning
affiliations: Anhui Jianzhu University, Anhui Jianzhu University and Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics

detail.title: An interpretable few-shot load forecasting framework integrating feature interaction modeling and adaptive transfer learning
detail.abstract: Under limited sample availability in the target region, conventional forecasting methods often struggle to fully capture complex interactions among multiple influencing factors, which hard to achieve high forecasting accuracy, and also face challenges in providing transparent explanations of the prediction process. Therefore, developing an effective method that simultaneously ensures forecasting accuracy, generalization capability, and model interpretability has become a critical issue in the fields of energy and power grid operation. To address this challenge, this study proposes a novel forecasting framework that integrates temporal feature interaction modeling, an adaptive transfer learning strategy, and explainable analysis, aiming to improve cross-regional load forecasting performance under few-shot conditions and provide transparent analytical support for power grid dispatch and management. Specifically, a feature selection algorithm is first employed to identify key explanatory variables, after which a PatchTST-STAR-BIGRU model based on feature interaction modeling is constructed. Furthermore, an adaptive transfer learning strategy based on the firefly algorithm is introduced to optimize the freezing and fine-tuning schemes across different encoding layers of the model. The experimental results show that the proposed model outperforms several benchmark models and achieves superior predictive performance using only a small number of target-domain samples. The Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) and the coefficient of determination (R²) reached 1.43% and 0.98, respectively. The model also demonstrated good stability and generalization ability in cross-seasonal testing. Finally, this study employs Shapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) to interpret the contributions of key features and their interactions. The results revealed the dynamic influence mechanisms of historical load, electricity prices, and meteorological factors across different seasons. This further provides interpretable decision support for power system dispatch, operation, and demand-side management.

title: Peer Effects in Active Learning
affiliations: Mackenzie Presbyterian University, Getulio Vargas Foundation (FGV) - Sao Paulo School of Economics and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Peer Effects in Active Learning
detail.abstract: This paper studies peer effects in higher education using an active learning environment where peer interaction is central to instruction. We exploit random assignment of students to tutorial groups, which generates exogenous variation in two dimensions: the ability composition of each group and the number of groups that pairs of students share. We show that both dimensions predict social proximity among peers — pairs who shared more groups and pairs closer in predetermined ability are more likely to interact, a pattern we term social proximity. We then compare outcomes under different social proximity regimes induced by this variation. Among low-ability students, a shift from the 25th to the 75th percentile in the number of peers likely to become socially proximate raises exam scores by 6.2\% per discipline, and increases the probability of an outstanding participation grade by 31 percentage points, which we interpret as evidence of increased effort. There are no detectable effects of social proximity on high-ability students. The conventional ability peer effects regression, which does not distinguish between peers likely and unlikely to become socially proximate, yields a near-zero aggregate estimate. Our results show that peer effects in higher education operate through distinct channels depending on students' ability level, and that policies targeting low-ability students must account for the social proximity that a given group composition actually generates.

detail.abstract: This study analyzes the conditional relationship between Korea’s Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) Official Development Assistance (ODA) and Korea’s bilateral commercial linkages—exports, imports, and outward FDI—using country-year panel data covering 146 recipient countries from 1987 to 2024. We identify 5,523 DPI-related projects from 83,083 OECD CRS projects through LLM-based text classification and construct a novel country-year DPI ODA panel variable. Using PPML estimation with country and year fixed effects, we document three main patterns. First, DPI ODA is positively associated with Korea’s exports and outward FDI with a time lag, while no consistent relationship appears in imports. This asymmetric pattern contrasts with lead-value tests in which all three channels are significant, suggesting a directional commercial spillover not easily explained by a purely symmetric strategic allocation story. Second, the relationship is conditionally stronger in recipient countries with higher digital readiness, measured by internet users, and stronger logistics performance, measured by the Logistics Performance Index, whereas broad governance indicators do not operate as significant conditional channels. Third, we find evidence of a post-2015 structural break in the FDI channel, consistent with a substantive change in Korea’s DPI ODA–commercial linkage structure following the strengthening of Korea’s DPI ODA policy. These findings suggest that DPI ODA may reduce transaction execution costs for donor-country firms, generating asymmetric and conditionally amplified commercial spillovers through recipient-country execution infrastructure.

title: Market integration and nutrition security: The impact of inter-provincial trade costs on healthy diet affordability in China
affiliations: China Agricultural University, China Agricultural University and China Agricultural University

detail.title: Market integration and nutrition security: The impact of inter-provincial trade costs on healthy diet affordability in China
detail.abstract: China's agricultural markets remain fragmented, with intra-provincial trade dominating cross-regional food flows. We argue that high inter-provincial trade costs undermine market integration, thereby reducing supply chain resilience and food availability—ultimately making healthy diets more expensive. Using a gravity model to measure trade costs and linear programming to estimate the cost of a healthy diet (CoHD) over 2011–2023, a two-way fixed effects model confirms that trade barriers significantly raise the CoHD, with the strongest effects in primary marketing regions and eastern provinces. These findings suggest that reducing domestic trade frictions can improve diet affordability and nutrition security, with broader implications for market integration policies in developing economies.

detail.abstract: Digitalization has fundamentally reshaped the architecture of global trade. Unlike previous waves of globalization driven by industrial capacity and physical infrastructure, the current transformation is powered by data, platforms, and digital connectivity (Ahmadova & Mammadov, 2025b; UNCTAD, 2021). For developing countries, digital trade presents both an unprecedented opportunity and a structural challenge. This paper examines the relationship between digital trade and economic development, focusing on productivity growth, export diversification, labor market transformation, financial inclusion, and institutional adaptation. It argues that digital trade can become a strategic development tool, but only if supported by coherent policy frameworks, infrastructure investment, and human capital development (Mammadov et al., 2026; World Bank, 2022). Without such foundations, digital integration may reinforce inequalities rather than reduce them.

detail.abstract: This thesis aims to examine the challenges facing coastal management in Europe, focusing on Turkey's Marmara Sea. Problems like urbanization, climate change, and pollution threaten these crucial areas that are at the center of many human activities. I explore Integrated Coastal Zone Management (ICZM) as a solution to bring together different stakeholder groups to protect the coast. Through a review of ICZM, which is currently lacking in the literature, and a case study in Turkey, I aim to understand the current situation, identify key players, and suggest ways to improve coastal management, providing policy recommendations. My thesis aims to inform better decisions and offer strategies for sustainable coastal development.

detail.abstract: This paper develops an analytical framework for the fundamental valuation of financial assets under radical and unbounded uncertainty, in conditions where the assignment of classical probabilities is epistemologically unjustified. Shackle's (1949, 1961, 1972) potential surprise curve is inverted to obtain a subjective plausibility distribution (S, t) in the Dubois-Prade (1988) sense; the non-additive capacities π machinery of Schmeidler (1989) allows this curve to be enriched with the narrative richness of imagined scenarios, thereby overcoming the operational limitation of Shackle's focal points. The fundamental value is computed through two Choquet integrals (1953-54) over distinct capacities-Hope mass G and Disappointment mass L-weighted by two free surprise aversion functions f and f that operate on the ⁺ ⁻ payoff without modifying the curve, separated over the gain and loss domains in a formulation that π captures the behavioral asymmetry documented by Tversky and Kahneman (1992) without assuming its probabilistic scaffolding. The framework includes: an original Shacklean microinterpretation of speculative prices as a dynamic-tension equilibrium of contradictory plausibilities (four propositions S1-S4 derived from Decision, Order and Time and Epistemics and Economics); a translation into the VIMP language of Shackle's framework for real assets and firm valuation in Expectations, Enterprise and Profit (1970); a reading of the bid-ask spread as a collision of mental architectures with liquidity in the Menger (1892) and Fekete (1996) sense; the treatment of cash holdings as a quasi-pointwise capacity and refuge from excessive masses; and derivative positions reformulated as geometric transformations of the curve. π Discounted cash flow structures the exposition: each block of the framework is introduced alongside its counterpart in classical DCF, which is subsumed as a particular case under solid convention. A second part calibrates the framework empirically: it introduces an Epistemic Term Structure Tensor T(K, t) integrating the implied volatility surface, the term structure of interest rates and the futures convenience yield, and an Epistemic Melting Factor Ωt identified under rolling cross-sectional methodology, with the pairs ( _t, _t) of each asset's representative agent identified moment by moment γ λ over the asset's own option surface —without cross-asset or cross-temporal information importation— and validated on Silicon Valley Bank (2023), Credit Suisse (2023), NVIDIA (2022–2025), and JPMorgan (2015–2019). A lead divergence indicator Δlead is defined between the credit default swap signal and the OTM put options over-premium across two windows ( = 4 and = 8 weeks), and a formal convergence τ τ test to classical DCF on JPMorgan 2015-2019 verified by the stationarity of the trajectories {( _t, _t)}_t γ λ under solid convention. The framework is applied numerically to the SVB collapse (USD 224 VIMP-DCF vs USD 264 classical DCF vs USD 189 market price in January 2023, DIV = 15.2%), it is validated out-of-sample on Credit Suisse (Ωt = 0.71 four weeks before March 15, 2023, without recalibration), and it is applied to NVIDIA's sustained rise during the 2022-2025 AI rally to illustrate that the framework also detects superadditivity due to strong narrative convention (structurally negative VRP on NVDA throughout the period, an observable signature of right-tail appetite). The framework does not aim to predict collapses — triggers are contingent — ; it aims to detect states of structural fragility in which any reasonably foreseeable trigger would produce a discontinuous adjustment. The claim is not to have discovered the mathematical machinery — standard since the late 1980s — but to articulate an operational bridge between the heterodox epistemological tradition and the modern formal apparatus.

detail.abstract: The rapid expansion of the digital economy has significantly transformed financial systems and human decision-making behavior. This study examines the psychological drivers influencing financial decision-making within digital environments, with particular emphasis on the role of cognitive biases, trust mechanisms, risk perception, and behavioral adaptation in the face of artificial intelligence, blockchain technologies, and digital financial platforms. Drawing on a synthesis of behavioral economics theory and recent empirical literature, the paper argues that financial decision-making in digital ecosystems is shaped not only by classical rationality but also by heuristic shortcuts, algorithmic dependency, information overload, and the reconfiguration of trust from interpersonal to technologymediated forms. Foundational frameworks by Kahneman and Tversky (1979) and Thaler and Sunstein (2008) are integrated with contemporary digital finance research to develop a unified analytical model. The findings suggest that digital ecosystems simultaneously enhance efficiency and introduce new behavioral risks, requiring adaptive psychological responses from both individuals and institutions. The study contributes to the growing literature on behavioral digital economics by bridging classical behavioral finance with the unique demands of the algorithm-driven financial landscape.

title: Quantifying the Optimal Mix of Tariffs and Linear Income Taxes
affiliations: The University of Osaka

detail.title: Quantifying the Optimal Mix of Tariffs and Linear Income Taxes

keywords: Quantitative Trade Models JEL classification: F13

detail.abstract: Donald Trump and his supporter, Marc Andreessen, advocate using tariffs as a major revenue source of the U.S. government instead of income taxes. To assess this idea, this paper quantifies the optimal mix of import tariffs and linear income taxes. I develop a two-country general equilibrium model where heterogeneous households elastically supply labor, the two countries exchange goods as in the Armington model, and the Home government finances non-rivalrous and non-excludable public goods with ad valorem tariffs and linear income taxes. A unique equilibrium exists. Calibrating the model for the U.S. and the rest of the world as of 2017, the optimal U.S. tax rates are a 25-percent tariff and a 20-percent income tax. At the optimum, tariffs account for only 3.3 percent of government revenue.

title: Short-term reconstruction of GNSS tropospheric delay based on HGPT2 and residual learning
affiliations: Henan Polytechnic University, Henan Polytechnic University, Henan Polytechnic University, Wuhan University, Henan Polytechnic University and Henan Polytechnic University

detail.title: Short-term reconstruction of GNSS tropospheric delay based on HGPT2 and residual learning
detail.abstract: GNSS-derived Zenith Total Delay (ZTD) is a key quantity in tropospheric sensing and precise positioning. However, its time series from operational CORS networks are frequently interrupted by 2 to 6 hour gaps caused by equipment failures and communication disruptions, which compromises downstream applications including precise point positioning (PPP) convergence and precipitable water vapour (PWV) retrieval. Existing empirical tropospheric models yield RMSE values of 30 to 60 mm against GNSS references and cannot meet short-term gap filling requirements, whereas current machine learning studies mainly target long-horizon forecasting, leaving the reconstruction of short 2 to 6 hour gaps across heterogeneous regions underexplored. To address this problem, this study develops a residual learning framework termed BiLSTM-DRM for short-term ZTD gap reconstruction. The model uses the residual between GNSS-ZTD and HGPT2-ZTD as its primary input, integrates temporal, positional, and spatial features, and applies a backward correction mechanism for iterative gap imputation. HGPT2 is adopted as the background model because its hourly resolution matches CMONOC sampling and because residual construction effectively decouples climatological components from station-level dynamic variability, thereby simplifying the learning task. Experiments are conducted on 234 CMONOC stations from 2018 to 2022, in which 224 stations are used for training and 10 are withheld as independent test stations. The proposed model yields a mean RMSE of 16.56 mm at held-out stations, reducing errors by 53.1% and 54.9% relative to HGPT2 and GPT3. Ablation analysis confirms that the backward correction mechanism and bidirectional architecture constitute the two core components, and removing either causes RMSE degradation of 25% to 34%.

detail.abstract: The interaction between education, technology, and economic development has become a critical determinant of competitiveness and sustainable growth in developing countries. This study empirically examines how educational attainment and technological readiness jointly influence macroeconomic performance. Using multi-country panel data and indicators related to human capital, digital infrastructure, innovation capacity, and productivity, the research analyzes the structural links between these variables. The findings reveal a strong and statistically significant relationship between improvements in education systems, technological adoption, and economic growth. Countries that invest in human capital and digital transformation demonstrate higher productivity, stronger innovation capacity, and more diversified economic structures. The integration of digital tools into education enhances workforce skills and supports participation in technology-intensive sectors. The study concludes that coordinated policies linking educational reform with technological strategies are essential for achieving sustainable economic development and strengthening global competitiveness in developing economies.

title: Reconciliation of Distribution with Exploitation and the Implications for the Transformation Problem
affiliations: National and Kapodistrian University of Athens and Aristotle University of Thessaloniki

detail.title: Reconciliation of Distribution with Exploitation and the Implications for the Transformation Problem
detail.abstract: Class struggle is instrumental in determining the actual production and circulation processes prevailing in any economy, as can been seen both in Marxist and Sraffian literature of Political Economy. Distributional and allocational claims on the surplus of production need to be specified prior to any production decisions are taken; in Marx, this is done through his use of the ‘rate of surplus value’ as an indeterminate variable, while, in the Sraffian literature, it is done through the construction of a wage-profit curve and a consumption-expansion curve that reveal the range of configurations in which the same economy can be reproduced. The two approaches can be interpreted in a similar manner. Our aim is to reconcile both in a unified framework consistent with the Labor Theory of Value, that includes a parametrization of class struggle. Finally, we demonstrate that the solution of the transformation problem is possible in this reconciled framework.

detail.abstract: This paper examines the critical role of digitalization and the Industry 4.0 paradigm in advancing sustainable economic structures. Industry 4.0, driven by the convergence of cyber-physical systems, the Internet of Things (IoT), artificial intelligence (AI), and big data analytics, represents a transformative framework that enhances industrial efficiency while addressing the imperatives of environmental and economic sustainability. title: Occupational Choice, Institutional Quality, and Stagnation Traps
affiliations: London School of Economics

detail.title: Occupational Choice, Institutional Quality, and Stagnation Traps
detail.abstract: This paper develops a microfounded theory of stagnation in which endogenous growth fails despite market clearing and positive savings. The mechanism rests on a three-way interaction between occupational choice, institutional quality, and precautionary liquidity demand. Agents allocate savings between productive entrepreneurship, which advances the technological frontier, and rent-seeking in existing assets, which yields private returns without raising productivity. When expected productive returns are low, agents reallocate toward rent-seeking and increase liquid asset holdings, tightening the condition for positive productivity growth. Unlike stagnation traps driven by aggregate demand shortfalls and nominal rigidities, this feedback is a real phenomenon: it operates through occupational choice even when markets clear and away from the zero lower bound. The effective policy instrument is microeconomic: raising returns to entrepreneurship relative to rent-seeking through stronger appropriability, rather than macroeconomic stimulus. Below a critical institutional threshold the economy converges to a stagnation trap; above a higher threshold sustained growth is uniquely stable; between them history determines outcomes, implying an asymmetry between collapse and recovery. The model distinguishes savings-abundant stagnation, as in Japan, relative to savings-scarce stagnation, as in the United Kingdom.

title: Imputed Survey Dates and Spurious Effects of the Minimum Legal Drinking Age: A Comment on Alonso-Armesto et al. (2026)
affiliations: University of Warwick

detail.title: Imputed Survey Dates and Spurious Effects of the Minimum Legal Drinking Age: A Comment on Alonso-Armesto et al. (2026)
detail.abstract: Alonso-Armesto et al. (2026) estimate the impact of an increase in the minimum legal drinking age (MLDA) in three Spanish regions using a difference-in-discontinuities design. A central claim of their paper is that increasing the MLDA reduces not only alcohol consumption but also tobacco and marijuana use. We show that these findings are spurious due to a fundamental but unacknowledged limitation of the database: it does not allow precise measurement of respondents’ age at survey. The authors attempt to circumvent this problem by combining information on month and year of birth with an imputed single survey date for each region–wave cell, a procedure that generates severe measurement error in the running variable. Fieldwork spans multiple months, yet the same date is assigned to all respondents, and strikingly, in nearly half the waves the imputed dates fall outside the official survey period altogether. More critically, these imputation choices introduce a confounder that is asymmetrically distributed across treatment and control cells. The authors assign January 1st — Spain’s schoolyear enrollment cutoff — as the survey date in 67% of control cells (MLDA=16) but only 20% of treated ones (MLDA=18), so that their estimated discontinuity captures relative age effects rather than MLDA impact. All significant results disappear once birth-month fixed effects are included. The authors’ inference is further undermined by their reliance on asymptotic approximations for cluster-robust standard errors in a context with only six clusters; under wild cluster bootstrap or heteroskedasticity-robust standard errors, significant results similarly vanish.

title: The statistical physics of learning in under- and over-parameterized layered neural networks
affiliations: University of Groningen, affiliation not provided to SSRN and University of Groningen - Bernoulli Institute

detail.title: The statistical physics of learning in under- and over-parameterized layered neural networks
detail.abstract: Using techniques borrowed from statistical physics, we study neural network systems at thermal equilibrium in a student-teacher model setting. The architecture studied here is the so-called Soft Committee Machine, a simple two-layered feedforward neural network with square integrable activation function, with respect to the standard Gaussian measure. Our focus is on understanding the effects that a mismatch in the number of internal units between the student and the teacher networks has in the system's behavior. We introduce two new ans\"atze for the saddle points of the under- and over-parameterized systems (supported by Monte Carlo simulations) and obtain the corresponding free energy and state equations for systems with any degree of over-parameterization and any square integrable activation in the high temperature limit. We show that the critical point grows with the degree of over-parameterization, while the asymptotic error decreases up until the number of internal units is the same as the teacher network's. For larger degrees of over-parameterizations the system always converges to a perfect generalization state. Moreover, we also show that, in an over-parameterized setting, out of all the activation functions analyzed here, the ReLU is the one with the highest decay rate for the order parameter that controls the baseline error created by the extra units.

title: An Integrated Early-Warning Model for Bank Financial Unsoundness: Evidence from Kazakhstan
affiliations: Satbayev University, Aberdeen Business School, Aberdeen Business School, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: An Integrated Early-Warning Model for Bank Financial Unsoundness: Evidence from Kazakhstan
detail.abstract: This paper develops a cost-sensitive integrated early-warning framework for predicting bank financial unsoundness, using evidence from Kazakhstan’s banking sector as a representative transition economy. While multiple discriminant analysis (MDA), logit, and probit models are well established in the bank distress literature, recent research increasingly emphasizes complex machine-learning techniques. However, growing empirical evidence suggests that well-specified statistical models can achieve predictive performance comparable to machine-learning approaches, while offering superior transparency, interpretability, and lower implementation costs – features that are particularly important for supervisory use. This study contributes to this debate by demonstrating how classical statistical models can be effectively combined into a unified, cost-sensitive supervisory framework in a post-Soviet banking system.,Using panel data for 12 commercial banks operating in Kazakhstan over the period 2008 – 2012, individual models and the integrated framework are evaluated through out-of-sample validation for 2013 – 2014. The analysis relies on accounting-based financial ratios capturing capital adequacy, earnings structure, liquidity, leverage, and operational efficiency. Rather than tailoring indicators to emerging markets, the study shows that standard supervisory and accounting measures retain strong predictive power when applied to a transition economy characterized by institutional change and banking sector concentration. The standalone MDA and probit models achieve predictive accuracies of 83.3%, while the logit model attains 87.5%. Crucially, the integrated framework preserves a high overall accuracy of 87.5% while completely eliminating Type I errors, defined as misclassifications of financially unsound banks as sound.,The findings indicate that the effectiveness of early-warning systems in emerging and transition economies depends less on algorithmic complexity than on the integration of complementary statistical signals within a cost-sensitive decision rule. By aligning statistical prediction with asymmetric supervisory costs, the proposed framework offers a transparent, operational, and policy-relevant tool for bank supervision and financial stability monitoring, with implications extending beyond the case of Kazakhstan. ​JEL classification: G21, G33, C53

title: A Moment-Constrained Neural-Network-Based Shock-Capturing Scheme
affiliations: Harbin Institute of Technology, Harbin Institute of Technology and North China University of Technology

detail.title: A Moment-Constrained Neural-Network-Based Shock-Capturing Scheme
detail.abstract: This paper proposes a moment-constrained neural-network-based non-oscillatory difference operator for shock capturing in numerical simulations of hyperbolic conservation laws. Built on a finite-difference scheme with a six-point stencil, the method employs a multilayer perceptron to learn nonlinear corrections to local difference coefficients and then enforces low-order discrete moment constraints through a subspace projection step. This design enables adaptive control of numerical dissipation and suppresses spurious oscillations near discontinuities while retaining resolution in smooth regions. Numerical experiments show that the proposed operator effectively preserves profile shapes in linear advection problems and stably captures the main discontinuous structures in the Sod and Lax shock tubes, two-dimensional Riemann problems, the Double Mach Reflection problem, and Rayleigh--Taylor instability. Compared with WENO-Z, the method exhibits lower numerical dissipation while maintaining satisfactory robustness. These results demonstrate that neural networks can serve as nonlinear correction modules within traditional high-order finite-difference schemes. Moreover, the moment constraints offer a practical route toward data-driven shock-capturing schemes that balance accuracy, resolution, and robustness.

In this context, blockchain provides an innovative framework for immutable record-keeping, real-time data sharing, and decentralized verification, allowing customs authorities, logistics companies, and trade participants to streamline operations and improve trust among stakeholders.This study investigates the practical applications of blockchain technology within customs logistics, including shipment tracking, digital documentation, certificate authentication, and cross-border trade facilitation. title: Heterogeneous AI News and Magnificent SevenHubs: Event-Day Causal Network Evidence
affiliations: Corvinus University of Budapest - Department of Finance and Corvinus University of Budapest

detail.title: Heterogeneous AI News and Magnificent SevenHubs: Event-Day Causal Network Evidence
detail.abstract: Major AI announcements now rank among the key information events for equity mar-kets, yet little is known about their firm-level transmission on the announcement dayitself. This paper asks whether different AI-news types affect different subsets of AI-exposed firms, whether information transmission is centralized around Magnificent Seven(M7) stocks, and whether the main source node depends on the event type. Using high-frequency intraday data for M7 stocks and smaller AI-exposed firms, we estimate event-day networks with a DAG-based Directed R2 connectedness framework. The evidenceshows that AI news does not follow a single market-wide transmission channel: the mainsource node changes across event types. M7 firms emerge as event-day hubs in compute-and adoption-related events, whereas disruption-related information can shift the mainsource node to a non-M7 firm. The results indicate that AI-related information is trans-mitted through event-specific equity-market channels, creating spillover vulnerabilitieswhen information transmission is organized around a few dominant source nodes.

title: Risk-Aware Factor Strategy Selection for Dynamic Portfolio Allocation: A Reinforcement Learning Approach
affiliations: Yonsei University, Yonsei University, Yonsei University and Yonsei University

detail.title: Risk-Aware Factor Strategy Selection for Dynamic Portfolio Allocation: A Reinforcement Learning Approach
detail.abstract: Portfolio allocation in dynamic markets is complicated by the fact that return opportunities and risk conditions evolve differently across market regimes. Traditional portfolio construction methods, such as mean–variance optimization and static factor investing, rely on stable risk premia, while recent reinforcement learning (RL)–based approaches often entangle return prediction and risk control, leading to unstable allocation behavior during regime transitions. This study addresses this limitation by proposing a two-stage portfolio allocation mechanism that distinguishes between factor-driven strategy construction and risk-aware strategy selection. Factor-driven strategy models are learned independently to capture heterogeneous return–risk profiles, while portfolio allocation is determined by a regime-aware selection mechanism that adapts to prevailing market risk conditions. This decision structure enables systematic adjustment of factor exposure across market regimes while preserving stable risk control. Empirical analysis on Nasdaq-100 and DJIA portfolios shows that the proposed approach outperforms traditional factor models and recent RL benchmarks, achieving higher risk-adjusted returns with lower drawdowns, particularly during bear and bull market regimes. These findings suggest that separating factor strategy construction from risk-conditioned allocation improves both the stability and economic interpretability of portfolio decisions.

title: An intervention game approach triggered by triple defense measures for controlling disease transmission in the context of multi-strain epidemics
affiliations: University of Dhaka, University of Dhaka, University of Dhaka and University of Dhaka

detail.title: An intervention game approach triggered by triple defense measures for controlling disease transmission in the context of multi-strain epidemics
detail.abstract: Alternative health interventions play a vital role in controlling the epidemic transmission, especially during the scarcity of appropriate target vaccines. A timely implementation of these alternative provisions can initiate a prompt remission of rapidly developed multi-strain outbreaks. The focal point of this study highlights the role of plural interventions to lessen the frequency of epidemic recurrence. Moreover, the effectiveness of these control measures is highly influenced by human behavioral response to this epidemic. Epidemics having multi-strains are becoming a global health concern that demands particular attention. Here, we present a noble mean-field epidemic game technique for forecasting the evolutionary dynamics of multi-strained influenza-like epidemics. We suggest adoption of multiple provisions can bring back the healthy situation of the epidemic stricken society if it is put into effect immediately. Our model justifies self-protection as a workable strategy that offers defense against either strain in addition to immunization. A modified Susceptible-Vaccinated-Infected-Recovered (SVIR) model is presented to cope with the dynamics of two strains, two vaccinations, and one self-defense measure. The first vaccination is termed the primary vaccine, and it is designed to target the primary strain while simultaneously being effective against the mutant or secondarily emerged strain. The second provision is known as mutant vaccination as it primarily targets the mutant strain while simultaneously being very effective against the earlier strain. Being a reasonably suitable alternative to vaccination, intermediate defense measure or self-protecting strategy has some efficacy against both these strains. The percentage of the population that uses various defensive strategies is shown through a time series analysis. The effectiveness of these defensive strategies under the two imitation dynamics respectively known as Individual-based risk assessment (IB-RA) and Strategy-based risk assessment (SB-RA) is explained in this study. Through the development of 2D heat maps portraying the final extent of the epidemic, the average social payoff, the percentage of the population vaccinated, and the fraction of free riders, a thorough analysis is conducted to compare the cost and efficacy of diverse defensive measures that can help us determining the best suitable imitation process.

title: THE AI REALLOCATION ENGINE: PRODUCTIVITY, ENTREPRENEURSHIP, AND VARIETY CREATION AFTER LABOR-DISPLACING AUTOMATION

detail.title: THE AI REALLOCATION ENGINE: PRODUCTIVITY, ENTREPRENEURSHIP, AND VARIETY CREATION AFTER LABOR-DISPLACING AUTOMATION
detail.abstract: We develop a theoretical model of AI-driven labor reallocation that generalizes and challenges the layoff-trap framework of Hemenway Falk and Tsoukalas (2026). Their model identifies a structural demand externality from competitive automation but suppresses entrepreneurial reallocation by construction (ρ = 0). We endogenize this margin. Displaced workers make an occupational choice-unemployment or entrepreneurship-based on expected startup profits, entry costs, survival probabilities, and outside options. The entrepreneurial conversion rate ρ therefore emerges from an explicit occupational-choice model rather than being assumed. We add three channels absent from the layoff-trap framework: (i) an AI productivity channel, in which AI raises the output of both incumbents (through AI-augmented task performance) and startups (by reducing entry costs); (ii) an entrepreneurship channel, in which displaced workers become founders of new AI-enabled firms that hire additional workers; and (iii) a product variety channel, in which new entry expands the consumption frontier under Dixit-Stiglitz preferences. We derive a reabsorption condition-ρ(1 + h) > 1, where h is equilibrium startup hiring solved from startup profit maximization-under which AI displacement is employment-expanding in net. Our main result is a policy sign-reversal theorem: there exists a threshold entrepreneurial conversion rate ρ* determined explicitly by structural primitives such that the optimal automation policy is a Pigouvian tax when ρ < ρ*, no intervention when ρ = ρ*, and an AI-adoption subsidy when ρ > ρ*. The layoff-trap result is a special case at ρ = 0. The analysis reframes AI displacement as a reallocation problem: the efficient policy is not necessarily to slow automation but to raise ρ above ρ* through entrepreneurship support, AI accessibility, and startup finance.

detail.abstract: This study estimates the long-term causal effects of the SABLA program, an in-kind, gender-focused intervention that provides nutrition, health education, and life skills to adolescent girls in India. Using nationally representative data and a cohort-based Difference-in-Differences design, the analysis shows that program exposure leads to significant improvements in reproductive health outcomes. Specifically, SABLA reduces total births, increases contraceptive use, strengthens women’s participation in contraceptive decision-making, and delays the onset of sexual activity. The program also improves maternal health, resulting in better birth outcomes and higher utilization of antenatal care services. Delivered through Anganwadi centers, sustained engagement with the program is a key mechanism driving these effects. Overall, the findings demonstrate that adolescent-targeted, gender-sensitive interventions can produce lasting improvements in reproductive and maternal health, highlighting their broader potential to enhance women’s well-being in low-resource settings.

detail.abstract: In July 2025, the U.S. Congress advanced the most consequential digital asset legislation to date: a coordinated package comprising the GENIUS Act, the CLARITY Act, and the Anti-CBDC Surveillance State Act. The GENIUS Act, originating in the Senate and enacted into law after approval by the House of Representatives, forms the cornerstone of this legislative agenda. Its companion laws, the CLARITY Act and the Anti-CBDC Surveillance State Act, both originating in the House, have passed their chamber and are now before the Senate for the second reading. This paper analyzes the statutory and executive alignment that redefines the U.S. crypto-financial landscape. It examines the proposed new division of regulatory authority, the codification of stablecoin standards, and the categorical rejection of programmable central bank digital currencies. Anchored in the Trump administration's strategic endorsement of blockchain innovation and decentralized monetary systems, the emerging legislative framework positions the United States as a free-market counterweight to the rise of surveillance-driven digital finance in authoritarian states. The analysis explores how these measures will reshape the conditions for capital formation, strengthen the architecture of regulatory accountability, and recalibrate the dollar's strategic role in an evolving multipolar monetary competition. More than a regulatory shift, the 2025 package articulates a constitutional orientation toward crypto-governance, grounded in individual financial autonomy, competitive innovation, and institutional limits on state power. Overall, it signals a national commitment to digital monetary pluralism over centralized control. * Bepi Pezzulli is a Solicitor in England and Wales and an Avvocato in Italy, specializing in crypto finance. His research interests include financial services policy; global risk governance; and economic statecraft. He analyzes the impact of legislation and case law on financial markets, financial regulation, financial architecture, financial stability, governance, and risk management.

detail.abstract: The United States pharmaceutical industry has a complex revenue recognition framework commonly referred to as Gross-to-Net (GTN) or Gross-to-Net (G2N). This framework entails substantial deductions from gross sales-recorded at Wholesale Acquisition Cost (WAC) or direct contract prices-to arrive at net revenue that accurately reflects realized income. GTN deductions can range from 10% to 80% of gross sales, which depends on many factors such as product type, market competition, customer class, and whether the drug is branded or generic. Despite of the fact that it has significant financial impact, GTN mechanics are rarely discussed outside specialized US pharmaceutical accounting circles, and this leads to an acute deficiency of knowledgeable professionals with the requisite expertise. This paper offers a structured and through exposition of the major GTN deduction categories: time-based discounts (cash/prompt-pay), distribution-channel deductions (chargebacks, admin fees, rebates, bill-backs, and shelf stock adjustments), Group Purchasing Organization (GPO) rebates, supply chain deductions (launch rebates, stocking allowances, failure-to-supply penalties, and sales returns), and government rebates (Medicaid and PHS 340B). The accounting treatment of each deduction under ASC 606 (Revenue from Contracts with Customers) is discussed, along with the associated estimation challenges / issues and financial reporting implications. The necessity for greater awareness of GTN concepts among accounting professionals is emphasized in the paper's conclusion, mainly in the countries like India that supply a substantial portion of the US generic drug market.

title: Effects of the Gender-Focused Adolescent Health Program on Women’s Reproductive Health in India
affiliations: Arizona State University (ASU) - Morrison School of Agribusiness and Resource Management

detail.title: Effects of the Gender-Focused Adolescent Health Program on Women’s Reproductive Health in India
detail.abstract: This study estimates the long-term causal effects of the SABLA program, an in-kind, gender-focused intervention that provides nutrition, health education, and life skills to adolescent girls in India. Using nationally representative data and a cohort-based Difference-in-Differences design, the analysis shows that program exposure leads to significant improvements in reproductive health outcomes. Specifically, SABLA reduces total births, increases contraceptive use, strengthens women’s participation in contraceptive decision-making, and delays the onset of sexual activity. The program also improves maternal health, resulting in better birth outcomes and higher utilization of antenatal care services. Delivered through Anganwadi centers, sustained engagement with the program is a key mechanism driving these effects. Overall, the findings demonstrate that adolescent-targeted, gender-sensitive interventions can produce lasting improvements in reproductive and maternal health, highlighting their broader potential to enhance women’s well-being in low-resource settings.

title: On the Legal Fiction of Transnational Sports Collective Bargaining Law in North America
affiliations: York University

detail.title: On the Legal Fiction of Transnational Sports Collective Bargaining Law in North America
detail.abstract: North American professional sports provide a unique example of truly transnational collective bargaining. Sports leagues and teams negotiate collective agreements with players’ associations that apply to players employed by teams in both Canada and the United States. The parties typically bargain pursuant to the rules in the National Labor Relations Act, including the NLRA’s rules regarding strikes and lockouts, and then behave as if those rules apply in Canada as well. They do not. Canada has its own labor laws that govern the relationship between Canadian-based sports teams and their employees. Most of time, this legal reality does not much matter in practice to the operation of the parties’ private model of transnational collective bargaining. The labor laws of the two countries are similar enough that the model operates relatively smoothly and the parties have an interest in making it work. However, private actors cannot avoid collective bargaining legislation by private agreement. As a result, sometimes the private transnational model the parties have negotiated conflicts directly with Canadian labor laws.  At that point, Canadian labor tribunals can either insist that the parties adapt their model to comply with Canadian laws, or they can defer to the private model, effectively permitting the parties to contract out of Canadian law. This essay examines which options Canadian labor tribunals have taken and examines how some tribunals have resorted to “legal fictions” to insist that parties cannot avoid Canadian labor law by contract, while still permitting them to do so in practice.

title: Time-Varying Fiscal Multipliers in Korea: A Multivariate Rolling ARDL Approach with Constrained Impulse Response Functions

detail.title: Time-Varying Fiscal Multipliers in Korea: A Multivariate Rolling ARDL Approach with Constrained Impulse Response Functions
detail.abstract: This paper estimates time-varying fiscal multipliers for Korea using a multivariate log-log Autoregressive Distributed Lag (ARDL) model applied within a rolling window framework. Using seasonally adjusted quarterly data on real GDP and consolidated government expenditures from 2000Q1 to 2025Q4, we estimate disaggregated multipliers for four spending categories: goods and services, household transfers, other transfers, and capital outlays. To ensure internal consistency, category-specific multipliers are proportionally scaled to match an aggregate total expenditure benchmark estimated by a univariate ARDL. Impulse response functions (IRFs) are derived from rolling-window averaged parameters and further size-adjusted by expenditure weights. Our results reveal substantial time variation in fiscal effectiveness and heterogeneity across expenditure categories, with capital outlays consistently exhibiting higher multipliers than current transfers. The rolling parameter-averaging procedure reduces estimation noise without sacrificing temporal responsiveness. These findings offer practical guidance for fiscal policy design in Korea and contribute to the broader literature on state-dependent fiscal multipliers.

title: The Adverse Tail of Machine Forecasts
affiliations: University of Melbourne

detail.title: The Adverse Tail of Machine Forecasts
detail.abstract: This paper studies whether the adverse tail of machine-learning return forecasts matters for financial markets. I construct Worst-Gap, the distance between the model consensus and the most pessimistic forecast among several out-of-sample machine-learning models. Worst-Gap captures directional model ambiguity rather than symmetric forecast dispersion. High-Worst-Gap stocks are followed by downward analyst forecast revisions, but these revisions do not improve forecast accuracy; instead, high Worst-Gap predicts larger absolute forecast errors and does not robustly predict lower realized EPS. Active mutual funds also reduce exposure to high-Worst-Gap stocks, consistent with institutional avoidance of adverse-tail ambiguity. In returns, high-Worst-Gap stocks outperform low-Worst-Gap stocks on a risk-adjusted basis. The spread is partly driven by the underperformance of low-Worst-Gap stocks, suggesting that model-consensus safety may be overpriced. The return relation is stronger when information frictions, limits to arbitrage, and aggregate uncertainty are high.

detail.abstract: Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) investing has transitioned from a dimension of fervent hype to one under intense scrutiny. This Article examines the shifting landscape of ESG investment, tracing its trajectory from being a self-proclaimed beacon of socially responsible capitalism to becoming a subject of contentious legal proceedings. This Article posits two primary critiques of ESG investing. Firstly, it argues that by delegating public policy pursuits to private entities, ESG frameworks allow companies to obscure political militancy and political motivations behind compliance measures. Secondly, it asserts that ESG metrics can serve as a convenient veil for underperforming companies seeking refuge from accountability for poor financial results. It concludes that in the mercurial world of finance, trends rise and fall with the swiftness of market fluctuations. ESG, once hailed as the herald of a new era in responsible capitalism, now finds itself navigating treacherous waters of skepticism and critique. As the winds of change continue to blow, one thing remains certain: in the ever-shifting landscape of investment, what rises swiftly may fall just as quickly. ESG’s meteoric rise may indeed prove to be matched only by a precipitous fall from favor.

detail.abstract: This paper examines the performance characteristics of multi-scale signal decomposition frameworks applied to market-neutral equity portfolio construction. We demonstrate that ensembling conviction signals across multiple temporal scales produces systematically superior risk-adjusted returns compared to any single-timeframe approach. Using a pointin-time S&P 500 universe over the period March 2022 through May 2026 (1,045 trading days), we construct a 30-long / 30-short equal-weight portfolio rebalanced every three trading days. The multi-scale framework achieves an annualized Sharpe ratio of 2.68 (conservative, 10 bps flat transaction cost) with CAGR of 27.3% and maximum drawdown of-4.1%, compared to single-scale variants that range from 0.74 to 1.52 Sharpe. Walkforward validation shows out-of-sample Sharpe of 3.96 exceeding in-sample Sharpe of 2.11 (OOS/IS ratio of 1.88). Parameter perturbation analysis yields a coefficient of variation of 0.037 across eighteen configurations, with a Deflated Sharpe Ratio exceeding the multipletesting threshold by 2.7×. The strategy generates positive alpha in 6 of 7 major market stress events within the evaluation period.

title: A Block-Coordinate Homotopy Method for Multi-Region DSGE Models with Occasionally Binding Constraints

detail.title: A Block-Coordinate Homotopy Method for Multi-Region DSGE Models with Occasionally Binding Constraints
detail.abstract: This paper develops a block-coordinate homotopy method for computingMarkov perfect equilibria in multi-region DSGE models with occasionallybinding constraints (OBCs). The algorithm decomposes the equilibrium sys-tem into region-specific subproblems solved via semismooth Newton con-tinuation. We prove convergence under a state-dependent coupling bound,establish an O(m^2) theoretical per-iteration flop-count reduction relative tostandard policy function iteration, and verify uniform grid convergence. Ona synthetic 4-region carbon-taxation model the solver handles 98.7% bindingconstraints, converges at 30× the theoretical coupling bound, and achievesmachine-precision accuracy against closed-form LQ solutions. A carbon-policy counterfactual demonstrates that exact OBC projection changes quan-titative policy conclusions: smooth log-barrier approximations understate thewelfare gain from coordinated tax differentiation by 0.46 percentage points—comparable to the estimated loss from unilateral leakage (−1.79%).

title: A Unified Calibration Framework and Synthesis Methodology for High Dynamic Range Imaging with Complementary Vision Sensors
affiliations: Xiamen University, Tsinghua University and Tsinghua University

detail.title: A Unified Calibration Framework and Synthesis Methodology for High Dynamic Range Imaging with Complementary Vision Sensors
detail.abstract: Acquiring high-quality visual data in unconstrained environments remains a fundamental challenge in computer vision, primarily because conventional cameras often produce over- or under-exposed images under extreme illumination. Unlike traditional high dynamic range (HDR) sensors, which rely on homogeneous pixels with uniform full-well capacities and noise floors, brain-inspired complementary vision sensors such as Tianmouc offer an alternative approach with heterogeneous pixels. These sensors achieve HDR by fusing information from two interleaved data pathways: a frame-based RGB pathway and an action-oriented pathway that captures sparse, high-speed spatiotemporal differences. However, these sensors lack a systematic method for defining and measuring their dynamic range to establish performance boundaries, as well as a suitable HDR synthesis technique to fully exploit their data fusion potential. To address this gap, we extend the EMVA 1288 standard to develop a rigorous calibration methodology that quantifies performance variations across different exposure combinations of the multi-pathway data. Anchored by these physical measurements, we then introduce the Progressive Fusion-Alignment Network (PFANet), a novel video synthesis network designed to adaptively merge complementary exposure data streams. By incorporating physical parameters via Feature-wise Linear Modulation and ensuring robust motion alignment, our model effectively integrates the high-frequency difference data from the AOP with the absolute intensity backbone of the RGB pathway. Extensive experiments validate our framework, demonstrating remarkable real-world HDR imaging performance. The proposed approach not only preserves intricate visual details across extreme lighting variations but also significantly mitigates motion artifacts commonly associated with conventional multi-exposure fusion techniques.

title: When Winners Stop Winning Simple and Weighted Market Momentum Fragility Signals for U.S. Equity Left-Tail Risk
affiliations: and

detail.title: When Winners Stop Winning Simple and Weighted Market Momentum Fragility Signals for U.S. Equity Left-Tail Risk
detail.abstract: This paper studies whether lagged market momentum spreads identify U.S. equity left-tail risk. For the Dow Jones Industrial Average, Nasdaq Composite, and S&P 500, I define 12-1 momentum as the cumulative return from months t-12 to t-2, skipping t-1. I construct two predetermined state variables: a simple quick-minus-slow signal based on simple moving averages of 12-1 momentum and a weighted version that gives greater weight to recent 12-1 momentum observations. Both signals are mechanically determined by the end of month t-2, making them early-determined, low-frequency indicators rather than daily trend-following rules. Across markets, negative and fragile states are associated with weaker returns and higher left-tail probabilities. For the S&P 500, the simple fragile state has a 20.7% probability of a monthly loss worse than-5%, versus 6.8% in the strongest state; the weighted fragile state gives a similar 20.4% probability. Moving-average filters remain stronger standalone left-tail classifiers when allowed to use more recent price information. The practical contribution is timing: QS and WQS warning episodes that contain left-tail months begin roughly three to four months before the first left-tail month on average, while the standard 12-month moving-average rule often confirms weakness in the same month. The contribution is therefore not a replacement for moving averages, but an early-determined momentum-deterioration state variable for risk budgeting.

title: Does Green Public Procurement Affect Procurement Performance? Evidence from Minimum Environmental Criteria in Italian Public Lighting Procurement
affiliations: Roma Tre University, Roma Tre University, University of Naples "L'Orientale" and Roma Tre University

detail.title: Does Green Public Procurement Affect Procurement Performance? Evidence from Minimum Environmental Criteria in Italian Public Lighting Procurement
detail.abstract: Green Public Procurement is increasingly used as a demand-side policy tool to promote environmental objectives, with theoretical predictions - rooted in the Porter hypothesis -suggesting market selection but no effect on competition plus negative effects in terms of administrative burden. This paper examines the impact of Green Public Procurement on procurement performance, exploiting the introduction of Minimum Environmental Criteria in the Italian public lighting sector. Using an interrupted time series design, we find a large and statistically significant reduction in market participation. However, we detect no effect on price competition or on time to award. Overall, the results suggest that Green Public Procurement reshapes market structure without altering procurement performance.

title: Most seek higher earnings, some escape unemployment, but none look for a handout: Economic drivers of labor mobility in the European Union
affiliations: Lazarski University, Lazarski University, Lazarski University and Lazarski University

detail.title: Most seek higher earnings, some escape unemployment, but none look for a handout: Economic drivers of labor mobility in the European Union
detail.abstract: This study examines the economic determinants of labor mobility within the European Union using data from 23 EU member states over the period 2000–2019. To address both model uncertainty and reverse causality, we employ Bayesian model averaging within a dynamic panel framework with weakly exogenous regressors. We find strong persistence in EU migration flows, largely driven by network effects operating through migrants already present in destination countries. While both earnings and unemployment differentials influence migration, the effect of earnings is 18 to 24 times stronger, suggesting that the search for higher income dominates the motive of escaping unemployment. This finding challenges the notion that labor mobility currently serves as an effective adjustment mechanism in the EU. However, as unemployment differentials tend to widen during recessions and their aftermath, migration may still contribute to economic adjustment when it is most needed. We find no evidence that differences in social benefits, taxation, or human capital significantly affect migration flows, contradicting prior empirical findings and media narratives suggesting the existence of welfare migration. Our results highlight the importance of addressing model uncertainty and endogeneity to accurately assess the drivers of labor mobility in the European context.

title: CBDCs and Debt management: a portfolio balance approach
affiliations: University College London and Link Campus University

detail.title: CBDCs and Debt management: a portfolio balance approach
detail.abstract: This paper presents a macro-financial model that combines the three-equation Carlin and Soskice (2018) framework with a portfolio-balance block `a la Tobin (1969) and a retail interest-bearing Central Bank Digital Currency (CBDC). The work offers a new perspective on sovereign debt management in incomplete monetary unions. The portfolio-balance approach allows the model to endogenously generate fragmentation dynamics. The introduction of CBDC alters these dynamics. Importantly, CBDC’s net impact on debt management depends on CBDCs issuance design as well as on CBDC holdings. Two issuance designs are here considered: sovereign bonds’ and deposits’ conversion. In the first case, the Central Bank acts a rule-bound absorber and it creates a persistent structural floor for sovereign bonds demand. Under the deposit conversion mechanism, the improvements in debt management pass eventually through commercial banks’ carry-trade behaviour. In both cases, the cap on non-financial private sector CBDC holdings emerges as the key design parameter determining whether CBDC stabilises or amplifies fragmentation during stress episodes. Throughout, Central Bank independence is preserved. The framework is directly applicable to the Digital Euro project and the institutional architecture of the Euro area.
