title: Order of Tone, Information Transmission, and Investor Reaction: Evidence from Analyst Report Text
affiliations: Renmin University of China, Renmin University of China, affiliation not provided to SSRN and Renmin University of China

detail.title: Order of Tone, Information Transmission, and Investor Reaction: Evidence from Analyst Report Text
detail.abstract: From the perspective of information presentation order, this paper investigates how the order of textual tone shapes information transmission in capital markets. Using a sample of analyst research reports on Chinese A-share listed firms from 2009 to 2022, we find that: (1) After controlling for the overall tone of the analyst report, the priority net tone is significantly positively correlated with short-term market reactions following the report release; (2) The market reactions to the priority tone aligns with the “incremental information view,” with no evidence of long-term return reversals; (3) The priority tone of analyst reports predicts firms’ future performance, conveying incremental information about firms’ fundamental prospects; (4) The market reactions to the priority tone of analyst reports is significantly amplified when institutional ownership of the covered firms is higher, the reports are issued by star analysts, or the level of information transparency of the covered firms is lower; (5) Analysts who effectively convey incremental information early in their reports are more likely to advance their careers and be recognized as star analysts. This study reveals the critical role of information presentation order in capital market pricing and attention allocation, providing a new perspective for understanding how market participants process “first-impression information”. Moreover, it extends research on limited attention and market behavior biases, while offering new theoretical support for information disclosure and high-quality investment research.

title: Environmental Criteria and Clauses in Public Procurement: Theory and Evidence on their Effects on Bidder Participation
affiliations: Avignon University, affiliation not provided to SSRN and Université d'Avignon

detail.title: Environmental Criteria and Clauses in Public Procurement: Theory and Evidence on their Effects on Bidder Participation
detail.abstract: Many governments around the world use public procurement as an environmental policy instrument through clauses (i.e., mandatory specifications in the contract performance) and award criteria (i.e., the dimensions of the offers the contracting authority assesses). Green clauses and criteria are often thought to discourage firm participation in procurement procedures. This article evaluates the impact of green clauses and criteria on firm participation from both theoretical and empirical perspectives. From a theoretical standpoint, we show that these instruments have a twofold effect: they may exclude some firms and raise participation costs, while also increasing firm expected margins. We test this prediction empirically using 50,000 procurement procedures in France between 2022 and 2023. We find a robust positive effect of both green clauses and criteria on participation, suggesting that the growing integration of sustainability into public procurement is unlikely to explain the observed decline in participation in procurement procedures.

title: Wave-Mamba: A Dual-Stream Framework for Crack Segmentation Based on Frequency-Domain State Space Learning
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Shaanxi Normal University, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Wave-Mamba: A Dual-Stream Framework for Crack Segmentation Based on Frequency-Domain State Space Learning
detail.abstract: In order to guarantee infrastructure safety, assess its state, and make maintenance easier, crack segmentation is essential. Cur rent automatic segmentation techniques must make a basic trade-off between collecting fine-grained local texture details and maintaining global topological continuity, particularly when high-frequency noise like oil stains and other surface abnormali ties are present. Additionally, Transformer-based models for global context modeling frequently have high computational com plexity, which restricts their use for real-time execution. In order to overcome these constraints, we present Wave-Mamba, a lightweight dual-stream hybrid network that improves topological consistency in crack segmentation by combining Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) with State Space Models (Mamba). In order to distinguish structural topology from background noise, we specifically present a unique Frequency-Domain Structure Stream based on Haar Wavelet Downsampling. In order to im prove robustness under challenging environmental circumstances, this stream is further combined with a Frequency-Gated Fusion Module, which efficiently combines global structural information with local detail characteristics. Using three different avail able datasets—CRACK500, DeepCrack, and CrackForest—we methodically assess the suggested approach. Wave-Mamba obtains 71.62% mIoU on CRACK500, 71.53% mIoU on DeepCrack, and 52.60% mIoU on CrackForest, according to experimental data. After the research is published, the dataset and source code will be openly accessible at https://github.com/Sajawal126/ wave-mamba-pavement-crack-segmentation following the publication of the paper.

title: Global Debt Audit: Detailed Calculation by 9 Elements of the Formula and the SVWORLD STANDARD 73.5 v1.7 on Sovereign Obligations

detail.title: Global Debt Audit: Detailed Calculation by 9 Elements of the Formula and the SVWORLD STANDARD 73.5 v1.7 on Sovereign Obligations
detail.abstract: This paper presents a global audit of world debt based on the SVWORLD STANDARD 73.5 v1.7, applied to the aggregate system of sovereign, private, financial, and hidden obligations. The main objective of the study is to construct a risk-adjusted picture of global debt burden that goes beyond traditional public debt indicators and captures the real channels of systemic stress. The analysis uses a nine-element formula that includes explicit obligations, hidden obligations, off-balance-sheet risks, and a derivative-based adjustment. The resulting framework is interpreted not as a conventional balance sheet, but as a stressoriented index of global financial fragility.

title: Endogenous Task Bundling, Skills and Automation
affiliations: University of Toronto - Rotman School of Management

detail.title: Endogenous Task Bundling, Skills and Automation
detail.abstract: Empirical measures of AI's wage effect typically hold fixed the bundle of activities a worker is paid for at its pre-AI shape. We argue that this assumption hides much of the action. When automation breaks a job apart, firms decide how to recombine the surviving activities; whether they rebundle them into one broad role or split them into specialist roles changes which surviving skills the labour market actually rewards. A skill that played no role in the pre-AI wage can become the dominant component of the post-AI wage, while a skill that anchored the pre-AI wage can disappear from the schedule. We develop an assignment model in which the priced human bundle is endogenous, and we use it to show that a fixed-bundle wage regression can mis-sign the effect of AI exposure. In general, the omitted-redesign bias has no unconditional sign: it is the residual covariance between exposure and role-specific redesign terms. Under explicit sufficient conditions, exposure-correlated unbundling loads specialist comparative-advantage premia onto the exposure coefficient, while exposure-correlated rebundling loads a different, often opposite, omitted term. The sign must therefore be measured from local post-AI partition changes rather than assumed from exposure alone.

detail.abstract: Kautilya, a profound ancient Indian political and economic strategist and author of the Arthashastra developed an encyclopedic framework for statecraft, political economy, warfare and intelligence. Though his ideas date back to the 4th century BCE, Kautilya's principles of governance and state security remain timeless and can be interpreted and applied to the modern-day predicament. His dynamic insights on powerplay, diplomacy and military strategy continue to reverberate in the contemporary geopolitical landscape, particularly with the advent of cybersecurity and hybrid warfare. These new forms of conflicts between and among states or non-state actors can be well understood by Kautilya's principles of espionage, war strategies, alliances and covert operations. This paper delves into integrating classical wisdom with a contemporary plan of action and how military strategists, policymakers and practitioners can implement Kautilyan thought to steer increasingly interconnected and intrinsic problems of the 21st century. The strategies and precepts of Arthashastra must be implemented by India to affirm its paramount position in the international arena. The findings suggest that Kautilya's multidimensional approach to governance offers a blueprint that can be adapted in the modern age of global circumstances defined by digital threats and hybrid conflicts.

title: A bootstrap-supported regional framework for design flood estimation in data-scarce Himalayan basins: Evidence from the Narayani Basin, Nepal
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and Tribhuvan University - Institute of Engineering Pulchowk Campus

detail.title: A bootstrap-supported regional framework for design flood estimation in data-scarce Himalayan basins: Evidence from the Narayani Basin, Nepal
detail.abstract: ​Reliable design flood estimation in ungauged and poorly gauged Himalayan catchments is limited by short records, uneven station distribution, and difficulty in defining statistically homogeneous regions. This study develops a regional design flood estimation framework for the Narayani Basin by combining L-moment-based regional frequency analysis, quantile regression technique (QRT), index flood method (IFM) and station-based bootstrap resampling. Annual maximum series from 14 hydrological stations were used to identify an acceptable homogeneous pooling group, select a regional parent distribution, develop QRT models from catchment descriptors, and compare QRT, IFM, at-site and Modified Hydest estimates at a representative long-record station.The full 14-station pool was not statistically homogeneous and required substantial refinement. The final accepted pool contained 8 stations and 326 station-years, indicating a clear trade-off between hydrological similarity and information support in Himalayan regionalization. Pearson Type III (PE3) provided the best regional fit. Bootstrap analysis showed that simple predictor structures were more robust than multi-variable alternatives, with log(AREA) + log(SD) retained for lower return periods and log(AREA) alone retained from the 10-year return period upward. IFM gave the most consistent agreement with at-site PE3 estimates across return periods, whereas QRT performed well for low to moderate return periods but flattened in the upper tail. Modified Hydest/DHM estimates were consistently higher for Station 420, with overestimation increasing with return period. The results show that bootstrap screening is useful for uncertainty assessment and for identifying the return-period range over which models remain defensible in data-scarce mountain basins.

title: The Impact of Shareholder Activism on the Banking Industry
affiliations: Cornell University, SC Johnson Graduate School of Management, Department of Finance

detail.title: The Impact of Shareholder Activism on the Banking Industry
detail.abstract: I investigate the role of shareholder activism in the corporate governance of banks. Bank shareholder activism is led primarily by a set of hedge funds that specialize in targeting banks exclusively, adapting traditional activist tools to unique aspects of bank governance such as the complex regulatory environment. I use a novel natural experiment to estimate the effect of increased exposure to activist campaigns on target banks, exploiting variation in changes to exposure after a Federal Reserve policy change that reduced regulatory barriers to hedge fund activism. Activist campaigns improve shareholder returns, but increased exposure to activism causes banks to reduce capital buffers and increase credit risk exposure relative to control firms. This finding is maintained after accounting for the disruptions of the Covid-19 pandemic, and is robust to matching and triple-difference specifications. However, hedge fund activism does not have a significant effect on individual bank failure risk or on systemic risk.

title: Comparison of convection-permitting and coarser-resolution regional climate simulations for evaluating precipitation and streamflow in Southern Québec
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Comparison of convection-permitting and coarser-resolution regional climate simulations for evaluating precipitation and streamflow in Southern Québec
detail.abstract: This study evaluates seasonal precipitation and temperature (April-May, summer, fall), as well as Rx1-hour (maximum hourly) precipitation across a domain in southern Quebec, using 3 climate simulations, all configured by Weather Research and Forecasting (WRF) regional climate model, driven by ERA-Interim reanalysis, at spatial resolutions of 4 km (CONUS simulation), 25 km, and 50 km (two CORDEX simulations). The results show that, for extreme precipitation analyses, the high-resolution 4km-WRF model (CONUS simulation) produced the highest RX1-hour values in summer. The simulations were further fed into a conceptual hydrological model to simulate streamflow at an hourly time step across twelve southern Quebec watersheds with surface areas ranging from 61–1550 km². Satellite-derived precipitation product (IMERG) precipitation and ERA5-Land temperature serve as our reference datasets for hydrological model calibration. The results show that in April-May, CONUS simulation produces lower mean snow water equivalent (swe) than those of the CORDEX simulations, primarily due to higher temperatures, which lead to earlier snowmelt and lower mean streamflow peaks compared to CORDEX simulations. Even though CONUS simulation produces higher extreme summer precipitation than the CORDEX simulations, this does not necessarily translate into higher streamflow simulations, most likely because of the higher temperatures that tend to increase potential evapotranspiration. In an event-based analysis carried out in a small watershed, though, CONUS simulation is able to produce short-duration, high-intensity rainfall events that do translate streamflow peaks that are not found in the CORDEX simulations.

title: Expectation-Performance Feedback Theory (EPFT): A Contextual Theory of Expectations, Welfare Politics, and Democratic Feedback in India

detail.title: Expectation-Performance Feedback Theory (EPFT): A Contextual Theory of Expectations, Welfare Politics, and Democratic Feedback in India
detail.abstract: This paper proposes the Expectation-Performance Feedback Theory (EPFT) as a context sensitive conceptual framework for understanding democratic political behaviour in India. The theory argues that Indian democracy is significantly sustained through continuous interaction between citizen expectations and perceived government performance. Citizens support political parties and leaders with the expectation that their socioeconomic , welfare oriented, developmental, and identity-related demands will be addressed through governance mechanisms. Political support is sustained when governments are perceived to satisfy these expectations, while dissatisfaction contributes to anti-incumbency behaviour, protests, and electoral volatility. The theory further argues that expectations within Indian democracy are not uniform and vary across lower-income, middle-income, and upper-income socioeconomic groups. EPFT conceptualizes elections as democratic feedback mechanisms through which citizens evaluate governance outcomes. The framework integrates insights from Rational Choice Theory, Social Exchange Theory, Retrospective Voting Theory, welfare politics, and Indian political sociology.

title: Consumer Learning Under Supply Uncertainty: A Pilot Study of eBay Listing-Volume Shocks in the Pokémon Card Grading Market
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: Consumer Learning Under Supply Uncertainty: A Pilot Study of eBay Listing-Volume Shocks in the Pokémon Card Grading Market
detail.abstract: I introduce a methodology for measuring consumer learning under supply uncertainty using highfrequency observations of secondary-market listings in the Pokémon trading card game (TCG) grading market. Conventional studies of certified-collectible markets rely on grader-published population reports, which are released monthly and reflect the grading firm's internal database rather than the supply consumers actually observe. I propose an alternative supply signal: the count of active eBay listings at a given grade and condition, captured every six hours via the eBay Browse API. I detect supply shocks as weekly listing-count changes exceeding the card's own historical 95th percentile of Δ log(listings), and study price responses around these shocks via a card-andweek fixed-effects event study. The contribution is methodological. The empirical pipeline runs end to end on a single virtual private server, persists observations into a Postgres warehouse, handles regime changes (e.g., API rate-limit changes) via an explicit exclusion register, and produces reproducible monthly snapshots for paper-version pinning. I report a pilot dataset spanning 3 April through 9 May 2026 (37 calendar days), 19 active cards, 2,772 observations, and two confirmed supply-shock events. The pilot is not powered for inference; results are presented to validate the pipeline rather than to support generalisable claims about the response of prices to supply. Companion work in preparation will apply the same methodology to a 98-card universe over a 12-month horizon, at which scale event counts should support publication-grade event-study estimation. I provide the full data-collection and detection code as a public replication package.

title: The Petrodollar Pact
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: The Petrodollar Pact
detail.abstract: The United States has, for decades, extended extraordinary military and diplomatic protection to the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, deploying its forces in the kingdom’s defence, sustaining arms transfers during the Yemen crisis, and withholding sanctions following the September 11 attacks despite the Saudi nationality of 15 of the 19 hijackers. Mainstream international relations scholarship attributes this relationship to oil dependency and regional stability imperatives. This article challenges that explanation as analytically insufficient. Drawing on structural analysis, Kautilyan statecraft theory, and monetary economics, it argues that the true and primary driver of American protection is the petrodollar architecture, a financial arrangement born from the collapse of the Bretton Woods system in 1971 and formalised through Nixon-era diplomacy with Riyadh, which requires global oil trade to be conducted exclusively in U.S. dollars, thereby sustaining American monetary hegemony. Through structured comparative analysis of U.S. responses to Saudi Arabia, Iran, Venezuela, Russia, and the European Union, the article demonstrates that American foreign policy in the Gulf is best explained not by liberal or realist IR theories alone, but by structural analysis of monetary power. The article further considers whether accelerating BRICS de-dollarisation and yuan-denominated oil trades signal the beginning of the petrodollar’s end and what that portends for U.S. global primacy and India’s strategic positioning.

detail.abstract: This essay analyzes the contemporary geopolitical rupture through the lens of institutional isomorphism and political anthropology. We argue that the Western liberal project, facing the limits of a "finite world," has mutated into an "algorithmic Katechon" aimed at stabilizing the world-system through a "cold," procedural identity. Conversely, Russia is constituting itself as a "civilization-state," mobilizing a "hot identity" based on narrative, memory, and sobornost. This "thermal collision" between the universality of code and the sovereign exception produces an irreversible fragmentation of the global space, transforming the international landscape into a pluriverse of thermal niches where survival depends on the ability to re-articulate technique in the service of national destiny.

title: CyRISK - A Capital Shortfall Measure of Cyber Risk in the Financial System
affiliations: University of St. Gallen - Institute of Insurance Economics, Leipzig University, Durham University and University of Leipzig

detail.title: CyRISK - A Capital Shortfall Measure of Cyber Risk in the Financial System
detail.abstract: We develop a market-based, forward-looking measure of cyber-related capital shortfall for the global banking system. The framework incorporates a tradable cybersecurity factor into a dynamic systemic risk model with time-varying exposures estimated via conditional betas. Applied to a broad panel of banks, the measure reveals that conventional market-only stress tests materially understate system-wide capital needs, with incremental cyber-related shortfalls amounting to roughly one quarter of conventional shortfalls at their peak. A small set of globally active banks accounts for the bulk of marginal cyber risk exposure, identifying a dimension of systemic importance that is largely orthogonal to size, leverage, and market beta.

detail.abstract: This paper is the fourth in the helioeconomic working paper series (Valkov 2026a-d). It provides a real-time empirical update to the conflict-outcome framework introduced in Valkov (2026c), building on the HelioEconomic Leading Index (HELI) and the four transmission channels established in Valkov (2026a). The dataset of 42 interstate conflicts spanning 1750-2026 (N=42) includes two ongoing cases provisionally coded in Valkov (2026c)-the Russia-Ukraine war and the US/Israel-Iran strikes (initiated February 2026)-whose outcome coding is updated through April 2026. Both cases occur during K6 Peak/Descent phase and SC25 post-maximum, precisely the conditions under which the framework predicts elevated failure probability for initiating actors (P(failure) = 0.94, 95% CI: 0.72-0.99). Observable dynamics in both cases are broadly consistent with predicted failure trajectories, though the US/Israel-Iran case exhibits partial tactical successes that complicate binary outcome coding and is treated as an anomalous intermediate case warranting further observation. Additionally, this update documents corroborating evidence across five helioeconomic transmission channels: commodity volatility (Urals +158% in 30 days, peak $116/bbl), financial market instability (S&P 500 CAPE ratio = 39.0, CPI re-acceleration to 3.3%), climatic anomalies consistent with SC25 post-maximum geomagnetic activity, institutional stress in Russia (parliamentary warnings, April 2026), and SC25 descent confirmation (WN = 92,-44% from peak). The April 2026 evidence is broadly consistent with-and does not falsify-the forward-looking assessment issued in March 2026.

title: On the Asymptotic Distribution of the Sharpe Ratio under Weak Dependence and Non-Gaussian Returns
affiliations: Abu Dhabi Investment Authority, Cornell University - Operations Research & Industrial Engineering and Khalifa University

detail.title: On the Asymptotic Distribution of the Sharpe Ratio under Weak Dependence and Non-Gaussian Returns

declarations.ethicsApproval: Not needed.
declarations.funderStatement: No funding.

detail.abstract: The Sharpe ratio is the premier statistic for performance evaluation, with promising applications to other fields as a signal-to-noise ratio. Although its asymptotic behavior under independent Gaussian observations is well understood, statistically valid inference under serial correlation and non-Gaussianity remains incomplete. Lo (2002) expresses the asymptotic variance in compact quadratic-form notation. Treating the Sharpe ratio as a smooth functional of first-and second-order moments, we derive an explicit asymptotic normal approximation for its plug-in estimator under weak dependence and finite "fourth plus 𝜖" moments. The resulting variance expression incorporates serial correlation, skewness, and kurtosis, and recovers existing results as special cases. Our results provide a unified theoretical foundation for Sharpe ratio inference beyond the classical i.i.d. Gaussian framework.

title: Programmable Liquidity & Recursive Welfare Stabilization

detail.title: Programmable Liquidity & Recursive Welfare Stabilization
detail.abstract: This paper develops a theoretical framework for purpose-bound monetary systems in which liquidity is programmable, recursively routable, and partially non-fungible. The paper argues that persistent inequality and welfare instability arise not only from distributive failures, but from the recursive dynamics of unrestricted fungible liquidity itself. To address this problem, the study introduces a recursive segmented monetary architecture integrating mechanism design, stochastic control, network dynamics, constitutional monetary governance, and programmable CBDC infrastructure. The framework establishes conditions for recursive equilibrium, bounded capability dynamics, and long-run stabilization, while computational simulations suggest that segmented liquidity systems may reduce recursive inequality amplification and improve welfare resilience under systemic shocks. More broadly, the paper proposes a shift from passive monetary exchange systems toward adaptive coordination architectures designed to preserve long-run human capability continuity.

detail.abstract: Whoever saves a single life saves an entire world-isn't it fair to listen also to that one voice?-Kaveh Dimitri Salahi PREFACE This proposal does not come from a scholar, a government-funded agency, or an institution. It comes from a simple human being with a voice and a solution. Priority Arts Initiative exists on the belief that every voice counts-that every voice reflects what it means to be a human being. History's greatest transformations were rarely born inside institutions. Institutions are funded by the old system and structurally incentivized to protect it. This voice carries no such conflict of interest. Only a idea, and the conviction to share it. SUMMARY Humanity stands at a crossroads. We face converging crises: mass job displacement from artificial intelligence, accelerating climate change, persistent energy poverty, and deepening geopolitical conflict over scarce resources. At the same time, we possess the technological capacity to eliminate scarcity itself. This paper presents a complete, integrated governance and infrastructure system designed to guide humanity from an age of survival and competition into an age of abundance and cooperation. The framework rests on four interconnected pillars: Axiocracy-A governance model grounded in human worth, universal production rights, and equitable access to infrastructure.

detail.abstract: The Common Agricultural Policy (CAP) faces a structural governance crisis: persistently elevated error rates (2.0–5.0%, European Court of Auditors 2015–2023), systematic benefit take-up gaps among vulnerable beneficiary categories, and administrative capacity differentials across Member States and paying agencies. This working paper proposes a computational governance paradigm for the CAP 2028–2034 programming cycle, grounded in six original analytical models: the European Index of CAP Administrative Complexity (IECAP), the CAP Irregularity Risk Scoring Framework (RISK), a New Five-Axis Taxonomy of CAP Measures, the CAP Accessibility Model (MEAP), the Agricultural Territorial Vulnerability Atlas (PVT), and the CAP Territorial Governance Model 2030 (MGT-2030). Each model is formally specified with mathematical equations, variable operationalisation, methodological limitations and an empirical validation roadmap following the OECD/JRC Handbook on Constructing Composite Indicators. The work concludes with a normative proposal for the introduction of a mandatory Complexity Impact Assessment (CIA) in CAP Regulation 2028, analogous to the regulatory impact assessment already required for European Commission acts under the Better Regulation Guidelines. The framework is grounded in the administrative burden literature (Herd and Moynihan, 2018), multilevel governance theory (Hooghe and Marks, 2003) and computational social science (Lazer et al., 2009).

title: Is Geopolitics ending the IMF's role as Lender of Last Resort? - University of Oxford (St Antony's International Review)

detail.title: Is Geopolitics ending the IMF's role as Lender of Last Resort? - University of Oxford (St Antony's International Review)

publicationDetails.detailsText: St Antony's International Review, University of Oxford

detail.abstract:
This article examines how rising geopolitical tensions and shifting global economic power are eroding the International Monetary Fund's credibility as a neutral lender of last resort. Established at Bretton Woods in 1944 under American leadership, the IMF has long served as an instrument of U.S. soft power, with Washington retaining effective veto authority through its 16.49% voting share. However, the 21st-century rise of China, now the world's largest bilateral lender and creditor to developing nations, has fundamentally altered this landscape.

Three cases illustrate the IMF's growing politicization: Sri Lanka's 2022 debt restructuring, where China challenged the principle of multilateral debt seniority; the Russia-Ukraine conflict, during which the IMF cancelled its Moscow mission while expanding lending to Kyiv; and Argentina's $20 billion program, perceived by some board members as politically driven due to President Milei's alignment with Washington. Similar patterns appear in lending to Egypt, Pakistan, and Ukraine, all geopolitically strategic nations. Meanwhile, China's bilateral rescue lending has reached over 40% of IMF levels, positioning Beijing as a credible alternative.

To preserve its relevance, the IMF must strengthen independent decision-making, recalibrate voting shares to reflect contemporary economic realities, and establish clearer multilateral debt restructuring frameworks through G20 cooperation.

detail.abstract: This paper conducts a PRISMA-based systematic review of pension research on Cyprus, focusing on how gender is addressed. Using a structured screening process, a final sample of studies is evaluated through a gender-audit framework distinguishing between central and partial gender analysis. The findings show that only a limited number of studies treat gender as a core analytical dimension, while most incorporate it indirectly or as a secondary variable. This uneven integration limits the understanding of gendered pension outcomes. The review highlights methodological and data gaps and stresses the need for gender-sensitive research and policy approaches addressing life-course inequalities and structural disparities.

title: Optimal MILP Approach to Group Sequential Hypothesis Test
affiliations: ,  and The University of North Carolina at Charlotte

detail.title: Optimal MILP Approach to Group Sequential Hypothesis Test
detail.abstract: Sequential hypothesis tests are widely adopted as a principled way to perform multiple tests on data that arrives over time. In particular, researchers frequently utilize group sequential hypothesis tests (GST) to test the same hypotheses at 𝐾 times or "groups" while data arrives sequentially. In this setting, many methods have been proposed to allow researchers to uniformly control type-1 error across 𝐾 checks (often known as various alpha-spending budgets). Although these methods are all successfully valid in controlling uniform type-1 error, it is not clear which of these methods are optimal when trying to reject the null as soon as possible. In this paper, we directly optimize the rejection criterion in the GST setting under the same constraints of controlling type-1 and type-2 errors. We use a sample average approximation combined with mixed integer linear programming (S-MILP) approach for this problem and show how our S-MILP approach dominates classical GST procedures such as Lan-DeMets, Pocock, and O'Brien-Fleming methods. We also find that the optimal solution typically aggressively spends 1 the alpha-budget early, shedding insight to the long-standing debate of which alpha-spending budgets are more efficient. We finally apply our optimal S-MILP approach to a recent study on acute kidney injury interventions and find our optimal S-MILP approach can reach the same statistically significant conclusion faster than the original study and other GST methods.

title: LAWE-IDS: A Learnable Adaptive Weighted Ensemble for Intrusion Detection in IoT Networks
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: LAWE-IDS: A Learnable Adaptive Weighted Ensemble for Intrusion Detection in IoT Networks
detail.abstract: IoT networks require intrusion detection systems that combine high accuracy with deployment footprints small enough for resource-constrained gateway nodes. We propose LAWE-IDS, a modular ensemble that fuses four heterogeneous classifiers (XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost, and a CNN-BiLSTM with self-attention) through a lightweight attention-based meta-learner producing per-sample fusion weights and feature gating. The meta-learner serves a primarily diagnostic purpose: examining the learned weights identifies which base learners contribute and which are redundant. Evaluated on three IoT-oriented benchmarks (TON-IoT, CICIoT2023, CIC-IDS2017) and two generalisation references (UNSW-NB15, NSL-KDD), LAWE-IDS exceeds 99% accuracy on all five datasets with AUC-ROC between 0.9995 and 1.0000 and cross-seed standard deviations below 0.13% over three random seeds. Ablation reveals that base-learner diversity drives the predictive performance: fixed-weight fusion performs within 0.02% of the full configuration. Attention analysis shows CatBoost consistently receives only 1 to 6% of the weight while occupying 77 to 86% of the model size, motivating LAWE-IDS Lite, a reduced variant dropping CatBoost that cuts the footprint by 79% (from approximately 161 MB to 35 MB) with less than 0.03% accuracy loss, suited to IoT gateway deployment.

title: Weighted Suffrage by Wealth and Education: Prospective Electoral Simulations in the Democratic Republic of the Congo

detail.title: Weighted Suffrage by Wealth and Education: Prospective Electoral Simulations in the Democratic Republic of the Congo
detail.abstract: Abstract This article evaluates, through simulation, the institutional and probabilistic consequences of introducing a voting system weighted by educational attainment and income in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. Starting from the persistence of representational distortions and weak democratic performance across successive electoral cycles, the study examines whether vote weighting can improve allocative efficiency, decisional coherence, and aggregate signal extraction while avoiding institutional capture. The simulations indicate that weighted suffrage shifts the political system from a diffuse democratic equilibrium toward a concentrated regime combining higher apparent efficiency with greater systemic fragility. The results further show that weighting mechanisms erode democratic legitimacy, amplify oligarchic concentration, and intensify elite capture without producing measurable improvements in democratic quality. Given the chronic dysfunctions of electoral representation in the DRC, the article argues that, if weighting mechanisms are to be considered, only a temporary and consensual censitary arrangement could limit the destabilizing effects associated with educational and income-based vote differentiation.

title: A CRITICAL INTERPRETATION OF THE BANK OF GHANA'S 2025 FINANCIAL STATEMENTS
affiliations: University of Buckingham

detail.title: A CRITICAL INTERPRETATION OF THE BANK OF GHANA'S 2025 FINANCIAL STATEMENTS
detail.abstract:
When one sits down with the Bank of Ghana's financial statements for the year ended 31 December 2025, the figures do not merely speak; they shout. This is not a report of gentle adjustments or modest corrections. It is, rather, a document that captures a central bank in the throes of one of the most severe financial stress episodes in its modern history. The bank recorded a loss of GH¢15.63 billion in 2025, up from GH¢9.49 billion the previous year. That represents a deterioration of roughly 65 percent. Its equity position has plunged to negative GH¢96.28 billion, from an already troubling negative GH¢61.32 billion in 2024. These are not abstract numbers on a ledger. They represent a fundamental question about the capacity of Ghana's monetary authority to discharge its constitutional mandate without recourse to extraordinary fiscal support.

What follows is an attempt to make sense of this financial landscape not through the detached language of accounting standards alone, but through an interpretive lens that asks what these numbers mean for the Ghanaian economy, for monetary policy, for the credibility of the central bank itself, and for the ordinary citizen whose daily life is shaped, often invisibly, by the decisions taken at the Bank Square on Castle Road.

title: Learning-Augmented Model Predictive Control for Energy Management in Hydrogen-Battery Hybrid Trains: A Comparative Deep Learning Study
affiliations: Politecnico di Torino, Polytechnic University of Turin, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Learning-Augmented Model Predictive Control for Energy Management in Hydrogen-Battery Hybrid Trains: A Comparative Deep Learning Study
detail.abstract: In hybrid vehicle applications, integrating hydrogen fuel cells and batteries presents energy management challenges that require real-time power optimization to protect components, improve fuel economy, and maintain charge levels. This paper introduces a learning-augmented model predictive control (MPC) framework for hydrogen-battery hybrid trains, comparing four deep learning models, long short-term memory (LSTM), gated recurrent unit (GRU), convolutional neural network (CNN), and echo state network (ESN), for power demand prediction. Trained on data from Italy's Brescia-Iseo-Edolo railway and validated on two other lines, the system uses a zero-dimensional model combining train dynamics, fuel cell polarization, and battery energy. Starting from a baseline MPC without machine learning, the study evaluates models over the round trip. Results indicate architecture-specific trade-offs: ESN has the lowest prediction error and excels in precise power demand prediction; LSTM/GRU models support fuel economy and performance; CNN struggles across scenarios. Prediction accuracy declines with longer horizons, especially for CNN.

title: Comparison of random field discretizations for high-resolution Bayesian parameter identification in finite element elasticity
affiliations: KU Leuven, KU Leuven and KU Leuven

detail.title: Comparison of random field discretizations for high-resolution Bayesian parameter identification in finite element elasticity
detail.abstract: We compare three random field discretization strategies for probabilistic identification of spatially varying material parameters in high-resolution finite element models. These strategies are (i) the Karhunen-Lo\`eve expansion, (ii) a wavelet expansion, and (iii) local average subdivision. The methods are assessed in the context of multilevel Markov chain Monte Carlo applied to plane stress elasticity with high-resolution displacement observations. Emphasis is placed on numerical efficiency, initialization cost, Markov chain mixing, and cost-to-error behaviour as the discretization resolution increases. While all approaches yield comparable posterior estimates, significant differences are observed in multilevel variance reduction and sampling efficiency. In particular, local average subdivision exhibits improved mixing and lower cost-to-error ratios at fine resolutions, despite its higher nominal parameter dimension. The results provide practical guidance for selecting stochastic field representations in uncertainty quantification in finite element simulations of heterogeneous materials.

title: Integrated Modeling and Energy Generation Optimization of a Wind Turbine System at Nsude Hill Using a Hybrid PSO-GA Algorithm

detail.title: Integrated Modeling and Energy Generation Optimization of a Wind Turbine System at Nsude Hill Using a Hybrid PSO-GA Algorithm
detail.abstract: Abstract-This paper presents an integrated modeling and optimization approach for enhancing wind energy generation at Nsude Hill using a hybrid Particle Swarm Optimization–Genetic Algorithm (PSO-GA). The study evaluates the effect of turbine height and time variation on maximum power output, demonstrating a direct relationship between increased altitude and improved energy generation. The hybrid PSO–GA technique is applied to optimize system performance under varying environmental conditions. Results indicate that the model achieves progressive improvements in power output, with values increasing from 658.01 W at 100 m to 1653.41 W at 480 m. Comparative analysis further highlights that while PSO-GA enhances efficiency, other algorithms such as the Firefly Algorithm (FFA) produce higher outputs under similar conditions. The findings validate the effectiveness of hybrid optimization in wind turbine systems and emphasize the importance of algorithm selection for maximizing energy yield in high-altitude wind energy applications.

title: DPINN: Denoising Physics-Informed Neural Networks for System Identification from Noisy Observations
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, Beijing Institute of Mathematical Sciences and Applications, Beihang University (BUAA), Beijing Institute of Mathematical Sciences and Applications, Yanqi Lake Beijing Institute of Mathematical Sciences and Applications and Beijing Institute of Mathematical Sciences and Applications

detail.title: DPINN: Denoising Physics-Informed Neural Networks for System Identification from Noisy Observations

keywords.keywords: System Identification Denoising Gaussian Mixture Model Non-Gaussian Noise Inverse Problems

detail.abstract: This paper presents a novel framework combining Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) with denoising techniques to address the challenge of learning dynamical systems from noisy observational data. While standard PINNs have shown promise in system identification, their performance significantly degrades when handling noisy measurements. Our proposed method, namely, denoising PINN (DPINN), integrates a denoising module into the PINN architecture, which simultaneously reduces measurement noise and preserves underlying physical constraints.Through systematic experiments on benchmark dynamical systems with various noise types and levels, we demonstrate that DPINN achieves superior accuracy in parameter estimation and equation discovery compared to standard PINN, Energy-Based Model PINN and Bayesian PINN. From an information theory perspective, we further demonstrate both theoretically and numerically that when the noise energy is comparable to or strongly correlated with the underlying signal, the mutual information $I(u; v)$ becomes small. In this regime, the inverse problem is inherently ill-posed, imposing a fundamental limit on the accuracy of any identification method. This work provides a paradigm for data-driven scientific discovery in noisy experimental environments, significantly expanding the practical applicability of physics-informed machine learning.

title: Mind the Self-Promotion Gap: Gendered Perceptions and Responses to an Informational Intervention
affiliations: Northwestern University, University of Michigan School of Information, University of Michigan School of Information and Independent

detail.title: Mind the Self-Promotion Gap: Gendered Perceptions and Responses to an Informational Intervention
detail.abstract: Promoting one’s research on social media has become an increasingly important part of academic careers, with implications for career advancement and the circulation of scientific knowledge. Prior research finds that men tend to self-promote their research papers more than women. This study draws on a survey of 3,111 U.S.-based academics to examine why this gender gap persists and experimentally test whether informing participants of the gap influences their intentions to self-promote in the future. We find that women are more likely than men to report reputational benefits (e.g., recognition, networking opportunities) but also higher interpersonal and professional costs (e.g., harassment, credibility loss, and time constraints). Men, by contrast, more often report skepticism about usefulness or audience presence as reasons for not self-promoting. Exposure to information about the gender gap is associated with significantly lower stated intentions among men to promote their next paper on social media. Women’s intentions, by contrast, remain unchanged, consistent with perceived costs of self-promotion, not lack of information about the gap, being the primary barrier among women. Overall, we conclude that increasing women’s intentions to self-promote their research requires systemic changes to evaluation criteria, anti-harassment infrastructure, and institutional support for public engagement.

title: Delayed Feedback Trading and Return Reversals: Evidence from China's 'T+1' Rule
affiliations: School of Economics, Fudan University and Fudan University

detail.title: Delayed Feedback Trading and Return Reversals: Evidence from China's 'T+1' Rule
detail.abstract: This paper exploits China's T+1 trading rule to examine the connection between positive feedback trading and short-run return reversals. The T+1 rule prohibits the same-day resale of shares purchased on day t while leaving same-day buying unconstrained. The rule makes holders of positions newly initiated on day t delay their sell-side feedback response until the next trading day. We refer to this as the T+1-delayed feedback trading channel. Consistent with the proposed channel, we find that turnover-dependent return reversals are stronger after negative-return days than after positive-return days and arise primarily during the intraday session of day t+1 rather than overnight. Moreover, this asymmetric intraday pattern is present in A-shares traded under T+1 but absent in matched H-shares traded under T+0. The results are consistent with the notion that positive feedback trading, in conjunction with institutional frictions, becomes a source of return reversals.

title: Private Languages
affiliations: Washington University in St. Louis - John M. Olin Business School

detail.title: Private Languages

keywords: compliance and informativeness JEL Codes: D82

detail.abstract: Strategic communication often relies on anchors observed by the sender but not by the receiver. An analyst may report against a proprietary valuation model, an auditor against an internal score, a manager against an accounting estimate, or an institution against its own standard. I study a sender-receiver game in which reports are costly to move away from such privately observed anchors. Anchor heterogeneity changes the geometry of communication. Rather than producing only cheap-talk partitions, privately anchored reporting generates continuous variation in messages because different senders find different reports costly to make. This mechanism can improve information transmission, but it can also pull reports toward noisy private anchors. Small positive reporting costs can make communication approach full revelation, even though zero costs return the model to cheap talk. Further, uninformative anchors can transmit information through strategic distortions, and anchored reports and cheap-talk messages can coexist as endogenous hard and soft information.

title: Implicit Government Guarantees and Earnings Management: Evidence from the First SOE Bond Defaults in China
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Implicit Government Guarantees and Earnings Management: Evidence from the First SOE Bond Defaults in China
detail.abstract: This study examines the effects of the weakening of implicit government guarantees (IGG) on earnings management in Chinese state-owned enterprises (SOEs). While prior research attributes earnings management discipline primarily to internal governance or formal supervision, we identify a different force: market-based financing pressure driven by IGG erosion. We exploit the staggered timing of first-ever SOE bond defaults across Chinese provinces as a quasi-natural experiment, using 23,431 firm-year observations from Chinese A-share-listed firms over 2010–2020. We find that the weakening of IGG significantly reduces earnings management among SOEs by approximately 13% of the sample mean. The financing-constraint channel drives this effect: the disciplinary impact is more pronounced among firms facing severe financing pressure, weaker profitability, intense market competition, high growth potential, smaller scale, or dispersed ownership. Beyond earnings management, IGG erosion also enhances transparency in information disclosure and reduces financial violations. Together, these findings indicate broader governance improvements following the withdrawal of implicit support, offering insights for regulators pursuing market-oriented reforms in state-led economies and for investors incorporating implicit guarantee risk into credit assessments.

title: Mandatory Industry Disclosure, Proprietary Costs, and Bond Credit Spreads: Evidence from China
affiliations: and Xiamen University

detail.title: Mandatory Industry Disclosure, Proprietary Costs, and Bond Credit Spreads: Evidence from China
detail.abstract: A central premise of mandatory disclosure regulation is that greater transparency reduces information asymmetry and lowers borrowing costs. We challenge this premise by examining industry-level operational disclosure - a regulatory form that reveals horizontally comparable information across peer firms rather than refining individual firm fundamentals. Exploiting the staggered introduction of mandatory industry-specific disclosure guidelines by Chinese stock exchanges between 2013 and 2019, we find that enhanced industry disclosure significantly widens bond credit spreads by approximately 54 basis points - the opposite of what standard disclosure theory predicts. This counterintuitive effect is more pronounced in non-homogeneous industries, among smaller firms, and for bonds restricted to institutional investors. Mechanism tests confirm two opposing channels: disclosure reduces information asymmetry while simultaneously intensifying product market competition by exposing strategically sensitive operational metrics. Our evidence challenges the one-size-fits-all approach to disclosure regulation and highlights that the competitive implications of disclosed information - not merely its quantity - shape credit risk pricing.

title: Reconfiguring Trust and Governance: Blockchain in Entrepreneurial Ecosystems
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and Federal University of Parana

detail.title: Reconfiguring Trust and Governance: Blockchain in Entrepreneurial Ecosystems

keywords.keywords: BlockchainEntrepreneurial EcosystemsGovernance InfrastructureData SovereigntyIndigenous EntrepreneurshipDecentralized Governance

detail.abstract: Entrepreneurial ecosystems often face persistent challenges of trust, transparency, and exclusion, particularly in Indigenous and community-led contexts. This paper examines blockchain as an enabling governance infrastructure for more inclusive and accountable entrepreneurial ecosystems. Drawing on entrepreneurial ecosystem theory, sustainability scholarship, and research on decentralized systems, it develops a conceptual perspective linking blockchain features such as immutability, traceability, programmability, and distributed validation to ecosystem functions including trust formation, resource coordination, data sovereignty, and participatory governance. Using illustrative cases from Australia, Aotearoa New Zealand, and Colombia, the analysis shows how blockchain can reconfigure relationships between actors, institutions, and communities. The paper argues that blockchain is not a universal solution but a socio-technical system whose impact depends on ethical design, cultural alignment, and community control. It contributes by reframing entrepreneurial ecosystems as governance structures shaped by technological infrastructures and offers design and policy insights for building more inclusive and context-sensitive ecosystems.

title: Government Data Opening and Corporate Leverage Manipulation
affiliations: Shanghai University of Finance and Economics, Shanghai University of Finance and Economics and Wuhan University

detail.title: Government Data Opening and Corporate Leverage Manipulation
detail.abstract: We examine the relationship between government data opening and corporate leverage manipulation. Leveraging the staggered establishment of province-level open government data platforms in China as a quasi-natural experiment, we find that government data opening significantly reduces corporate leverage manipulation. This policy effect is more pronounced among firms with low capital intensity, firms with limited analyst coverage, and those located in regions with low banking competition. Mechanism analysis suggests that government data opening affects the cost-benefit trade-off of corporate leverage manipulation by alleviating financing constraints and enhancing corporate governance, thereby mitigating leverage manipulation practices. Our research contributes to the literature on government data opening, highlighting its role in reducing leverage manipulation and offering valuable implications for mitigating significant financial risks.

title: Unified Camouflaged Object Inpainting with Semantic, Texture, and Color Guidance
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Unified Camouflaged Object Inpainting with Semantic, Texture, and Color Guidance
detail.abstract: Camouflaged object generation aims to synthesize images in which a given foreground blends into the background with low perceptual salience while remaining semantically plausible. Existing pipelines often address only a subset of the camouflage triad--semantic pairing, texture similarity, and color consistency--leading to failures such as implausible foreground--background relations, texture discontinuities, or global tone mismatch. Building on a BrushNet-based diffusion inpainting framework, we propose a unified diffusion framework for jointly modeling semantic pairing, texture consistency, and color alignment: (1) a language-annotated semantic-camouflage dataset that constrains plausible foreground--background pairings; (2) a camouflage-domain VAE that provides a latent prior over local background textures to regularize masked-region synthesis; and (3) an ultra-light Color Adapter that injects foreground color statistics via mid-block affine bias for controllable tone alignment.We evaluate on in-domain and cross-domain benchmarks using FID/KID, CLIPScore for text--image semantic consistency, and LPIPS for perceptual similarity. Our model achieves consistently stronger semantic alignment and perceptual realism than representative baselines, and a dedicated comparison between the standard VAE and our camouflage VAE confirms the benefit of domain-adapted texture priors. Frequency-domain visualizations further reveal that our texture modeling restores high-frequency components coherently. Finally, human studies on identification difficulty, naturalness rating, and A/B preference demonstrate that our results are harder to detect and judged more natural.

title: Greenium Fragility: Physical Climate Shocks, Mandatory ESG Disclosure, and Corporate Credit Spreads
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Greenium Fragility: Physical Climate Shocks, Mandatory ESG Disclosure, and Corporate Credit Spreads
detail.abstract: Whether physical climate shocks erode pricing conditions in sustainable fixed-income markets remains empirically unresolved. We investigate how major climate disasters affect the Baa-Aaa corporate credit spread and whether the European Union's Sustainable Finance Disclosure Regulation (SFDR) Level 2 moderates this relationship. Combining daily Moody's corporate bond yields from the Federal Reserve Economic Data (FRED) repository with geolocated climate disaster events from the EM-DAT International Disaster Database, we exploit the January 2023 regulatory discontinuity as a quasi-experiment. In the pre-SFDR period (2018--2022), climate disasters are associated with a significant widening of the Baa-Aaa spread, consistent with heightened risk aversion in the investment-grade segment. After the implementation of SFDR Level 2, this post-disaster widening is attenuated by 1.36 basis points in the immediate window (days +1 to +5) and by 2.28 basis points over the medium term (days +6 to +10), representing a 40--60 percent reduction in shock transmission. Mechanism tests indicate that the buffering effect is strongest during elevated market volatility and inverted yield curves, aligning with an information-asymmetry-reduction channel. These findings offer quasi-experimental evidence that standardized ESG disclosure stabilizes credit market pricing during periods of acute climate risk, informing regulatory deliberations at the SEC, ESMA, and IOSCO.

title: Inliers Confidence Estimation with Soft-assignment Network for Robust Point Cloud Registration
affiliations: Harbin Engineering University, Harbin Engineering University and Harbin Engineering University

detail.title: Inliers Confidence Estimation with Soft-assignment Network for Robust Point Cloud Registration
detail.abstract: Point cloud registration is the problem of estimating a rigid transformation between point clouds. Due to measurement errors between the point cloud position and the actual physical position during sensor scanning, the algorithm is prone to finding incorrect correspondences. Additionally, previous registration methods often struggle with generating the correct extremum, particularly when faced with significant initialization errors and noise. However, a small number of outliers can lead to systematic deviation of model performance. To address these issues, we propose the Inliers Confidence Estimation Network (ICENet), which includes a two-branch feature interaction network and an adaptive inliers prediction network to reject potential correspondences with outliers for robust point cloud registration. First, the two-branch Feature Interaction network (FI) consists of a Global Feature (GF) embedding layer based on unique spatial position information and a deep Feature Fusion (FF) module, which can enhance the discriminativeness of learned point-wise features by collaboratively learning local and international features. Besides, the Inliers Prediction network (IP) is developed using an Inliers Estimation (IE) module that integrates consistency features for a comprehensive understanding of the shape and structure of the point cloud. A Soft-Assignment (SA) layer is designed to ensure the effect of inliers in the correspondences. Extensive experiments conducted on the ModelNet40 and KITTI datasets illustrate the superior registration performance of INENet compared with other state-of-the-art methods. Its effectiveness in resisting noise and generalizing to partially overlapping scenarios validates strong robustness and suitability for real-world applications.

title: This Time Is Not So Different: Volatility Regimes In The Cryptocurrency Market
affiliations: Universidad Diego Portales and Universidad Diego Portales

detail.title: This Time Is Not So Different: Volatility Regimes In The Cryptocurrency Market
detail.abstract: In conventional markets, volatility admits a decomposition into a systematic component and an idiosyncratic residual. No such decomposition yet exists for a contemporary cryptocurrency universe at the individual-asset level. We build it by applying to a panel of 38 cryptoassets (91% of market capitalization, October 2018 to February 2026) the asymptotic principal components factor model of Connor et al. (2006) and the residual COVOL framework of Engle & CamposMartins (2023), and we obtain a daily per-asset decomposition into common and idiosyncratic components. The cross-section alternates between two regimes that a Markov-switching regression separates sharply: systemic stress with a common share above 55%, and speculative below 30%. Within that architecture, the two largest single-day shocks in the sample do not occur during the crypto-native failures, but at the SEC v. Ripple ruling and the spot Bitcoin ETF approval; LUNA/ Terra is the only episode with sustained elevation. Macro-financial transmission turns out to be selective: crypto-native sentiment, captured by the Fear & Greed index, reaches the idiosyncratic volatility of nearly the entire cross-section, while the VIX, the EPU, the NFCI, the GPR, the dollar and oil add no explanatory power at the daily frequency. Applied to 38 S&P 500 stocks and 11 SPDR sector ETFs under the same procedure, the exercise yields an indistinguishable regime architecture; the differential concentrates in the upper tail and in crypto-native events. In the space of volatility, this time is not so different.

title: Understanding Public Acceptance of Road Pricing: Behavioural Modelling for Sustainable and Multimodal Transport Policy
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, Swinburne University of Technology and Swinburne University of Technology

detail.title: Understanding Public Acceptance of Road Pricing: Behavioural Modelling for Sustainable and Multimodal Transport Policy
detail.abstract: This paper examines the factors shaping public support for road pricing in Australia through a comparative modelling framework applied to stated preference data from Melbourne and Sydney. We develop and contrast Multinomial Logit (MNL) and Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) neural network models to analyse how socio-demographic traits, travel behaviours, and perceptions of revenue use influence acceptance. Support increased significantly when revenue was earmarked for public transport improvements and infrastructure upgrades, highlighting the critical role of transparent and equitable revenue framing. Education, income, and work-from-home flexibility were associated with greater support, while frequent travel to central business districts reduced it. MLP models outperformed MNL models in predictive accuracy, particularly in capturing non-linear behavioural interactions. These findings offer insights for designing equitable pricing strategies that can encourage shifts away from private car use and support more sustainable, multimodal urban mobility systems. The paper also underscores the importance of transparency, trust, and explainable AI in building institutional legitimacy for future transport reform.

title: From the Platforms to the Surroundings: How Station Environment Shapes Public Transport Route Choices
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, Technical University of Denmark and Technical University of Denmark

detail.title: From the Platforms to the Surroundings: How Station Environment Shapes Public Transport Route Choices
detail.abstract: Station environments shape the passenger experience, yet their influence on actual route-choice behaviour remains poorly understood. This study examines the impact of station attributes on public transport route choice by combining large-scale revealed preference data from the Danish Rejsekort smart-card system with perception-based indicators derived from a nationwide online survey of train stations in Denmark (N = 4,801). Five key station attributes are identified through factor analysis: Cleanliness, Urban Life, Crowding, Environment, and Lighting. A discrete choice model is estimated by maximum likelihood using 141,000 route-choice observations from the multimodal transport network of Eastern Denmark.The results show that station quality significantly influences route attractiveness and explains a substantial share of the observed preference for rail. Improvements in urban life, cleanliness, and the environment, from average to good, yield utility gains equivalent to 2.2, 1.6, and 1.4 minutes of bus in-vehicle travel time, respectively. These findings suggest that investing in station quality is a cost-effective lever to increase rail ridership, complementing traditional service improvements such as reduced travel time or higher frequency.

title: Inflation Co-Movement in the Euro Zone: Headline versus Core, Trends versus Cycles, and the Impact of Debt Crises
affiliations: Wichita State University - W. Frank Barton School of Business

detail.title: Inflation Co-Movement in the Euro Zone: Headline versus Core, Trends versus Cycles, and the Impact of Debt Crises

keywords: F45. Inflation Co-Movement in the Euro Zone: Headline versus Core
and the Impact of Debt Crises

detail.abstract: A high level of inflation co-movement across member countries is important for the functioning of the euro monetary union. While some previous studies on euro zone prices do distinguish between cohesion in core versus headline inflation, with the former being more vital, none formally differentiate between co-movement in the cyclical versus trend components of inflation. Importantly, trend and core (as well as cyclical and headline) inflation are clearly distinct, as our results will indicate. The distinction between trend and cyclical inflation is important; while common external shocks may lead to temporary co-movement of inflation across countries, a failure to attain high cohesion in the trend component can cause more lasting divergence of prices across countries, making the ECBs duties more difficult and the common currency unviable.

title: Should I stay or should I travel?An analysis of increasing petrol prices on travel behaviour
affiliations: The University of Sydney, The University of Sydney and The University of Sydney

detail.title: Should I stay or should I travel?An analysis of increasing petrol prices on travel behaviour
detail.abstract: This paper examines how rising petrol prices affect weekly travel behaviour, with particular attention to modal substitution and trip suppression. The analysis draws on stated responses from 808 Queensland residents, each of whom first reported their travel behaviour for the week prior to the survey and then indicated how that behaviour would change under three hypothetical petrol price scenarios set at AUD 2.50, AUD 3.00, and AUD 3.50 per litre (noting fuel prices at the pump varied between an average of AUD 2.20 and AUD 2.53 during the survey period). Weekly trip frequencies are jointly modelled for eight travel outcomes, including car travel as driver, car travel as passenger, public transport, taxi, rideshare, cycling, walking, and avoided trips. The latter category is included within the hypothetical setting to capture the extent to which increase in petrol prices may lead travellers to cancel or forgo trips altogether, rather than simply reallocate travel across modes. The empirical analysis is performed implementing a multivariate Generalised Poisson framework with dependence across travel alternatives introduced through a Gaussian copula. The results indicate that higher petrol prices substantially reduce car travel both as driver car passenger, while increasing public transport use, particularly at the higher price scenarios. However, the substitution towards public transport is only partial. A sizeable share of the adjustment instead occurs through avoided trips, suggesting that fuel price increases are more likely to suppress travel rather than simply induce a reallocation across modes. The findings further show that behavioural responses vary with socio-economic circumstances and perceived transport disadvantage, implying that the burden of higher fuel prices is unevenly distributed. Overall, the paper shows that rising petrol prices affect not only mode choice, but also the ability of individuals to maintain everyday mobility and activity participation.

title: Diminishing Returns to Road Investment: Evidence from Cost-Benefit Analyses
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU)

detail.title: Diminishing Returns to Road Investment: Evidence from Cost-Benefit Analyses
detail.abstract: We study long-run trends in the economic returns to Norwegian road investments using a harmonised dataset of 360 ex ante cost-benefit analyses from 1974 to 2024. Projects are drawn from official planning documents and adjusted for changes in appraisal parameters and construction cost inflation. Using the net benefit-cost ratio (NBCR) as our measure of economic return, we find a significant negative time trend in NBCR that remains after conditioning on observed project characteristics. When investment costs are deflated with the construction cost index and appraisal parameters harmonised, the trend remains negative and is possibly hump-shaped. We further show that the decline in economic return is associated with lower travel-time savings, consistent with diminishing returns in a mature road network. By contrast, the decline does not appear to be driven by increasing project size or by shifts towards projects with a larger share of costly components, such as tunnels and bridges. Taken together, the evidence suggests that as the road network matures, economic returns decline, and that future welfare gains are more likely to come from priorities other than large‐scale road-network expansion.

title: The Measurement Problem in Economics: Production, Price, and the Missing Unit of Observation

detail.title: The Measurement Problem in Economics: Production, Price, and the Missing Unit of Observation

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no known financial interests, personal relationships, or competing interests that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This paper is a theoretical and conceptual study and does not involve human participants, patient data, or experimental procedures requiring ethics approval.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract:
Economics seeks to explain production, exchange, wealth, growth, and public coordination, yet it continues to rely primarily on nominal representations—prices, monetary aggregates, accounting values, and national income statistics—as the principal means of observing economic activity. These instruments provide important information regarding exchange relations and financial flows, but they do not constitute a unified objective measure of productive reality itself. This distinction raises a fundamental methodological question: what exactly does economics objectively measure?

This paper argues that modern economic observation remains structurally dependent on representation rather than direct measurement. Prices emerge within exchange and reflect scarcity, negotiation, institutional arrangements, expectations, and market conditions, yet they do not directly measure the productive burden associated with bringing goods and services into existence. Likewise, monetary aggregates and nominal accounting systems describe financial expression without independently observing the underlying physical economic reality from which output arises.

The paper further distinguishes between nominal representation of wealth and wealth as real productive abundance. Goods, services, infrastructure, productive capacity, and stored productive value constitute the material foundation of economic life, while monetary representation remains an exchange language rather than an objective unit of production-based observation.

From this perspective, the central methodological limitation of economics is identified as the absence of a unified objective unit capable of observing production itself across the wider economic structure. The paper examines the distinction between production, market exchange, and distribution as separate yet connected layers of economic reality, and argues that a unified economic unit of expression may provide the conceptual basis for observing economic activity within a common comparative framework. Within such a framework, goods, services, and distributive outcomes may become comparable through a shared unit of economic expression while preserving the distinction between production and exchange.

Before economic systems can be meaningfully restructured, economic reality must first become objectively observable. The measurement problem is therefore not peripheral to economics—it stands at its methodological foundation.

title: Corporate Innovation and Insider Trading
affiliations: Cornell University - Samuel Curtis Johnson Graduate School of Management, National University of Singapore (NUS) - NUS Business School and National University of Singapore

detail.title: Corporate Innovation and Insider Trading
detail.abstract: We examine whether insider trades convey information about innovation activities. We find evidence that insiders trade following the release of exogenous news about the firm's patent applications. Such insider trading is mitigated when the market reacts strongly to the patent news. Insiders of innovative firms also trade more after earnings announcements and other major corporate disclosures than before. Insider trading is more informative about innovative firms than non-innovative firms, eliciting stronger market responses, improving liquidity, and better predicting future profits and innovation. Several of the patterns we document are stronger for insider purchases than for insider sales. Moreover, insider purchases, but not sales, are profitable for insiders of innovative firms, even among those that are well-governed and in the period after the Sarbanes-Oxley Act of 2002. Collectively, our findings suggest that insider trades convey information about corporate innovation to outsiders.

title: A Deterministic Mean-Field Surrogate for a Success-Driven Agent-Based Model of Speculative Participation
affiliations: University of Bari

detail.title: A Deterministic Mean-Field Surrogate for a Success-Driven Agent-Based Model of Speculative Participation
detail.abstract: We derive a deterministic mean-eld surrogate for an agent-based model of speculative participation with endogenous wealth feedback. In the ABM, heterogeneous agents accumulate wealth and revise discrete exposure rules through success-driven softmax imitation. The reduced system closes the aggregate dynamics with rst moments of group wealth. Numerical results show that the surrogate tracks the ABM ensemble average closely across the explored (β, ε) region. It reproduces both aggregate participation and group mean wealth, residual errors shrink with population size, and the largest discrepancies occur near the low-exploration boundary, where run-to-run variability is highest. These results show that a low-dimensional deterministic model provides an accurate aggregate representation of the ABM over a broad parameter region while identifying where nite-population eects matter most.

title: Volatility Scaling in Multi-Asset Portfolios: Evidence from a Systematic Risk-Targeting Strategy
affiliations: Federal University at Rio Grande do Norte - UFRN and Universidade Federal do Rio Grande do Norte (UFRN)

detail.title: Volatility Scaling in Multi-Asset Portfolios: Evidence from a Systematic Risk-Targeting Strategy
detail.abstract: This paper empirically evaluates volatility scaling-the dynamic adjustment of portfolio exposure to maintain stable realised risk-applied to a multi-asset universe of global equities, fixed income, inflation-linked instruments, and commodities. Motivated by Man AHL's TargetRisk and similar funds methodology, we compare four strategies from December 2014 to January 2026: a static 60/40 benchmark, an equal-weight unscaled portfolio, and portfolio and sector-level volatility-scaled strategies. Volatility scaling reduces the coefficient of variation of quarterly realised volatility by approximately 50% relative to the unscaled benchmark (Levene W = 270.0, Bartlett χ 2 = 3,950.2, both p < 0.001). Regime analysis reveals a sharp asymmetry: scaled strategies excel during calm markets (Sharpe 0.746 vs. 0.412 for 60/40), while static benchmarks outperform during stress episodes as the mechanism endogenously de-levers. The leverage scalar is strongly counter-cyclical (Pearson r =-0.84; Spearman r =-0.99). Transaction costs at 10 bps reduce the gross Sharpe by only 0.044 units. These findings contribute to the literature on dynamic position sizing and target-volatility fund construction.

title: Разработка методики оценки экономического эффекта от внедрения искусственного интеллекта в различных отраслях
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Разработка методики оценки экономического эффекта от внедрения искусственного интеллекта в различных отраслях
detail.abstract: В статье предлагается методика количественной оценки влияния искусственного интеллекта на экономическое развитие регионов в условиях цифровой трансформации. Подход основан на сочетании теоретического моделирования и анализа панельных данных с учетом временных лагов и региональной неоднородности. Формализуются ключевые каналы воздействия ИИ на производительность и инвестиционную активность, строится симуляционная модель, а также проводится кластеризация регионов по уровню цифровизации. Эмпирические результаты, полученные с использованием моделей с фиксированными эффектами и распределенными лагами, свидетельствуют о наличии отсроченных эффектов и существенной гетерогенности воздействия ИИ между кластерами. Практическая значимость исследования заключается в возможности применения полученных выводов для обоснования мер региональной инновационной политики и оценки эффективности цифровой трансформации.
