title: Sharp Minds, Tired Brains-WHY " Decision Fatigue" is the enemy of our education system?
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Sharp Minds, Tired Brains-WHY " Decision Fatigue" is the enemy of our education system?

publicationDetails.detailsText: No it’s a article written by me which I want to get publish here.

detail.abstract:
This article examines the pervasive impact of decision fatigue within the education sector, exploring how the constant pressure of micro-negotiations and high-stakes choices taxes the cognitive resources of educators and administrators. Drawing on the Strength Model of Self-Control, the discussion illustrates how mental energy is a finite resource that, when depleted, shifts leadership from visionary, proactive strategy to reactive, "survival mode" firefighting.  

The piece outlines practical, human-centered frameworks to combat this fatigue, including the "Early Bird" rule for high-leverage decision-making, the automation of routine administrative tasks, and the necessity of cognitive sustainability in organizational culture. By prioritizing the quality of mental energy over the quantity of tasks, educational leaders can reclaim the clarity needed for empathetic and effective leadership. Ultimately, managing decision fatigue is presented as an essential act of care that ensures student outcomes are guided by thoughtful, strategic intent rather than mental exhaustion.

title: A PRISMA-Based Systematic Review of Gender Inequality in Uruguay's Pension System

detail.title: A PRISMA-Based Systematic Review of Gender Inequality in Uruguay's Pension System

declarations.ethicsApproval: This study was based exclusively on published literature and did not involve human participants, personal data, or patient records. Therefore, ethics approval was not required. ChatGPT was used only for minor language editing and proofreading assistance.

detail.abstract: This paper examines the gendered effects of pension and retirement systems in Uruguay through a systematic literature review, motivated by persistent inequalities arising from contributory social protection models that reflect labor-market disparities and unequal caregiving responsibilities. Using the PRISMA 2020 framework, the study identifies and evaluates 21 relevant studies selected from an initial pool of 205 records, applying a gender-audit approach to distinguish between research with central and partial gender analysis. The findings reveal a methodologically diverse body of literature, largely dominated by quantitative approaches, but characterized by an uneven integration of gender as an analytical dimension. While some studies explicitly link pension outcomes to gendered life-course trajectories, highlighting the role of interrupted employment, unpaid care work, and lower contribution densities among women, others treat gender as a secondary factor or descriptive variable. Evidence from the literature indicates that reforms such as caregiver pension credits have improved women's access to pensions and reduced gender gaps, yet these measures remain insufficient to fully address structural inequalities. Overall, the review demonstrates that pension systems are not genderneutral and emphasizes the need for more comprehensive, gender-sensitive research and policy design to ensure equitable and inclusive retirement outcomes.

title: A PRISMA-Based Systematic Review of Cumulative Disadvantage and Gendered Pension Inequality in Luxembourg

detail.title: A PRISMA-Based Systematic Review of Cumulative Disadvantage and Gendered Pension Inequality in Luxembourg

declarations.ethicsApproval: This study was based exclusively on published literature and did not involve human participants, personal data, or patient records. Therefore, ethics approval was not required. ChatGPT was used only for minor language editing and proofreading assistance.

detail.abstract: Population ageing and changing labour market structures have intensified concerns about the adequacy and fairness of pension systems, particularly regarding gender inequality. This study presents a systematic review of the Luxembourg pension and retirement system, examining how gender influences outcomes in later life and assessing the extent to which existing research incorporates gender as a core analytical dimension. Using the PRISMA 2020 framework, a structured search of the Scopus database identified 266 records, which were screened down to 10 relevant studies based on predefined criteria, including focus on Luxembourg and gender-differentiated outcomes. These studies were analysed through a gender-audit framework, distinguishing between central and partial gender perspectives. The findings indicate that gendered labour-market trajectories, especially caregiving interruptions and part-time employment, significantly shape pension inequalities; although public pension systems mitigate some disparities, they rarely eliminate them entirely, and their effectiveness depends on institutional design. The review also reveals a fragmented body of literature with limited integration of income, wealth, health, and demographic dimensions, underscoring the need for more 1 comprehensive, gender-sensitive research and policy approaches that address structural inequalities across the life course.

title: Does Party Embeddedness Drive Corporate Empire Building?
affiliations: Capital University of Economics and Business, Capital University of Economics and Business and Capital University of Economics and Business

detail.title: Does Party Embeddedness Drive Corporate Empire Building?
detail.abstract: This study examines how Party embeddedness affects corporate investment by exploiting a unique institutional arrangement that allows Party members to participate in firms' decision-making processes. We find that Party embeddedness significantly increases firms'  expansion. The results are robust to alternative variable definitions, entropy balancing, and placebo tests. Heterogeneity analysis shows that the effect is more pronounced among private-owned enterprises (POEs), firms without prior misconduct, and firms with lower ESG engagement. Mechanism analyses indicate that the expansion effect is unlikely to be driven by long-termism induced by Party involvement; instead, it primarily operates through the alleviation of financing constraints. Overall, our findings highlight the important role of internal political institutions in shaping corporate investment incentives.

title: Biodiversity Loss, Firm Risk, and Bank Exposure: Evidence from Italian SMEs
affiliations: and University of Florence

detail.title: Biodiversity Loss, Firm Risk, and Bank Exposure: Evidence from Italian SMEs

keywords: Nature-related financial risk JEL Classifications: G32

detail.abstract: We study whether biodiversity loss affects the financial performance of Italian small and medium enterprises (SMEs) and whether these exposures translate into risks for the banking system. We combine firm-level accounting data for 2014-2024 with high-resolution geospatial measures of biodiversity loss and climate shocks. To address endogeneity, we instrument biodiversity loss using exogenous drought conditions. Baseline estimates suggest a statistically significant negative association between biodiversity loss and profitability (-0.0002***), along with small positive correlations with revenues (+0.0003*) and production costs (+0.0005***). Nevertheless, these relationships do not survive instrumental-variable identification, in which the estimated effects become economically small and statistically indistinguishable from zero. However, this average masks substantial heterogeneity. Micro-enterprises experience a significant contraction in activity, with revenues declining more than costs. In addition, firms operating in sectors more dependent on ecosystem services exhibit significantly lower profitability when exposed to biodiversity loss. Aggregating firm-level exposures through bank branch networks reveals pronounced and persistent cross-bank heterogeneity in biodiversity-related risk, with a high concentration of exposure among a small number of institutions. These findings suggest that, while average effects at the firm-level are limited, biodiversity loss may still pose localized risks with potential implications for financial stability.

title: Users Complete Tasks but Still Cannot Explain Why: Measuring Cognitive Distance in Information Systems

detail.title: Users Complete Tasks but Still Cannot Explain Why: Measuring Cognitive Distance in Information Systems

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study does not involve human participants, personal data, or identifiable records. Ethical approval was therefore not required.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: Users often complete a digital task and still cannot explain why the system produced the outcome it did. This recurring paradox exposes a blind spot in usability research: performance metrics can register success while overlooking whether users understand system logic. Existing frameworks, especially those centered on cognitive load, capture the effort required to interact, but they do not adequately capture whether a system's conceptual structure aligns with the mental model users construct during use. This paper introduces cognitive distance as a distinct construct for analyzing that alignment in information systems. Drawing on cognitive ergonomics and human-computer interaction, the paper develops an operational framework and a Cognitive Distance Index built from four dimensions: perceived understanding, predictive accuracy, interaction confidence, and conceptual transparency. The framework positions comprehension as a core dimension of both accessibility and usability and outlines measurement procedures and empirical pathways for validation. The paper moves cognitive distance from theoretical intuition to a research-ready construct that explains how users can succeed behaviorally while failing interpretively, thereby enabling more inclusive, intelligible, and cognitively sustainable system design.

title: Integrated On-Campus Renewable Energy System Prioritizing Electric Vehicle Charging Demand Optimized through Multi-Objective Optimization
affiliations: Islamic University of Technology, Islamic University of Technology, Islamic University of Technology and Islamic University of Technology

detail.title: Integrated On-Campus Renewable Energy System Prioritizing Electric Vehicle Charging Demand Optimized through Multi-Objective Optimization
detail.abstract: This study introduces an unprecedented energy management system prioritizing the charging of on-campus electric vehicles (EV) at Islamic University of Technology (IUT), Bangladesh. The suggested model uses solar energy to fulfill on-campus EV load demand first and supply excess electricity to partially meet IUT’s load demand. A modified version of the multi-objective particle swarm optimization algorithm (MOPSO) was utilized to numerically calculate the different parameters of the RES and determine the system’s viability in off-grid scenarios. Results demonstrate that the proposed model yields Levelized Cost Of Energy (LCOE) as low as 0.064 USD/kWh, Loss of Power Supply Probability (LPSP) as low as 2.6% and SOC deviation at 20.38%, while mitigating CO2 emissions by nearly 297,000 kg every year. Furthermore, the nature and the results of this research are aligned with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), particularly SDG 7 (Affordable and Clean Energy), SDG 11 (Sustainable Cities and Communities), and SDG 13 (Climate Action), focusing on the planning and the design of an efficient on-campus energy management system for developing countries.

title: Расходы на общее образование в России: факторы, влияющие на региональные различия

detail.title: Расходы на общее образование в России: факторы, влияющие на региональные различия
detail.abstract: В работе анализируется связь между расходами на общее образование в расчёте на одного учащегося и результатами образовательного процесса в регионах России, а также факторы, определяющие региональные различия в финансировании образования. На основе пространственной регрессии (данные по 81 субъекту Российской Федерации за 2015 г.) не удалось выявить статистически значимую зависимость между величиной расходов на одного ученика и долей выпускников 11 классов, получивших аттестат. Положительное влияние на долю выпускников, получивших аттестат, оказывают такие показатели как доля обучающихся в первую смену и доля населения с высшим образованием. Основными факторами, определяющими объём расходов на образование в субъектах Российской Федерации, выступают показатели «богатства» региона (ВРП на душу населения, налоговые и неналоговые доходы, средняя заработная плата по экономике), а также доля сельского населения.

title: Can Multimodal Large Language Models Extract Investment Signals from Financial Charts? Evidence from Portfolio Backtests
affiliations: Yonsei University and Yonsei University

detail.title: Can Multimodal Large Language Models Extract Investment Signals from Financial Charts? Evidence from Portfolio Backtests
detail.abstract: This study examines whether a pretrained multimodal large language model (MLLM) can extract investment-relevant signals from financial chart images. Using stocks from the Dow Jones Industrial Average and Euro Stoxx 50, we evaluate signals derived from a pretrained MLLM across directional prediction, cross-sectional ranking, and portfolio back testing. To analyze the role of visual information, we construct a tiered chart representation that progressively incorporates technical indicators. The results show that chart-based visual information alone provides useful signals for cross-sectional asset ranking and portfolio construction, while directional prediction remains close to random. Signals derived from the pretrained MLLM improve ranking performance relative to price-only charts and conventional rule-based strategies, and these improvements are reflected in portfolio outcomes. Increasing chart complexity does not consistently improve performance. These findings suggest that pretrained MLLMs exhibit useful capabilities for financial chart interpretation and highlight the importance of information selection in chart-based analysis.

title: Comparative Analysis on Players and Non-Players for Determination of Rhythm Games' Benefits Beyond Entertainment Purposes
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Comparative Analysis on Players and Non-Players for Determination of Rhythm Games' Benefits Beyond Entertainment Purposes

declarations.declarationOfInterest: This research does not interfere with interest from any organization or individual.

detail.abstract: As a video game genre originated in 1990s Japan as a form of arcade game, rhythm game has expanded its popularity in its 30 years of development. There are various kinds of rhythm games across different platforms nowadays, and this genre is growing its popularity not only in Japan, but also in many other countries across the world. Preexist studies primarily explores rhythm games in the lens of its psychological influences or its application in serious fields such as education or special training, but rarely discuss rhythm games' impact on players' physical performance factors such as reaction time and finger dexterity (e.g. clicking speed). Such a phenomenon is counterintuitive, since people are often in awe of high level rhythm game players' (RGPs) skills and assume that RGPs have better reaction and handspeed. With regards to this, this paper aims to find out whether "rhythm game enhances reaction time and clicking speed" is a reasonable conclusion through performing a comparative analysis on RGPs and non-player by recruiting participants in each group to perform reaction and clicking speed test. The results indicate that RGPs had significant advantage in both reaction and clicking speed test compared to the non-players. This paper then analyzes the characteristics of rhythm games to explain such improvement, as well as interpret the significance and potential applications of rhythm games on these two aspects.

title: The K-A-T Framework: A Unified Framework for Macro-Financial Propagation Through Funding Constraints, Networks, and Policy Backstops

detail.title: The K-A-T Framework: A Unified Framework for Macro-Financial Propagation Through Funding Constraints, Networks, and Policy Backstops
detail.abstract: We propose K-A-T as a unified framework for macro-financial propagation with three structural channels: (i) funding and collateral constraints (K), proxied by USD cross-currency basis deviations and high-frequency monetary surprises; (ii) network amplification (A), formalized via the Leontief inverse on input-output and financial-network adjacency matrices; and (iii) policy backstop credibility (T), modeled as a put option on funding costs. We derive the propagation in a two-period model whose central testable prediction is that the half-life of stress satisfies HL_i = ln 2/(lambda_T + mu_i), with lambda_T proportional to T. Validation is provided by a hierarchical Bayesian random-effects meta-analysis of ten historical T-shock episodes spanning four decades (Discount Window 2008, ECB SMP 2010, Operation Twist 2011, OMT 2012, USD swap-line 2020, FIMA 2020, SRF 2021, BoE LDI 2022, TPI 2022, BTFP 2023, SRF cap removal 2025). The grand-mean compression of stress half-lives is -64.9% (95% CI [-75.5%, -49.8%], p<0.0001, between-episode heterogeneity tau^2 = 0.202). Sensitivity to the heterogeneity estimator (DerSimonian-Laird vs REML vs Paule-Mandel) shifts the grand-mean by less than 1pp; leave-one-out analysis confirms no single episode drives the result. The February-April 2026 private credit gate cascade is held out as a posterior predictive check (T approximately 0); the realized magnitude lies inside the model's 95% predictive interval [-86.4%, -9.1%]. Identification combines literature triangulation (Du-Tepper-Verdelhan 2018, Altavilla-Giannone-Lenza 2017, IMF GFSR 2019) with Anderson-Rubin weak-instrument-robust inference for the LP-IV companion. The empirical companion paper, focusing on the firm-level event study and bilateral bank-BDC exposure matrix from the 2026 cascade, is targeted at the Journal of Financial Intermediation. The K-A-T monolith is publicly available on SSRN (Abstract ID 6668858).

title: Counterparty-Level Bank Exposure to Private Credit and Tail-Risk Bounds: Evidence from the February-April 2026 Gate Cascade

detail.title: Counterparty-Level Bank Exposure to Private Credit and Tail-Risk Bounds: Evidence from the February-April 2026 Gate Cascade
detail.abstract: Quarterly disclosures by U.S. G-SIBs in April 2026 revealed approximately $128 billion in direct private-credit exposure across the top four banks alone — more than double the figures previously inferred from aggregate flow-of-funds data. We construct, from a hand-curated transcription of EDGAR 10-K Credit Facilities and Borrowings footnotes for thirteen U.S. Business Development Companies (BDCs), the first publicly available facility-level bilateral matrix linking individual private-credit lenders to individual G-SIB credit-line providers. The matrix documents $40.7 billion in committed credit lines across the public-BDC sample, with JPMorgan as the dominant primary arranger ($12.15 billion). When scaled to bank-side disclosed totals, the implied per-bank tail loss in a catastrophic 40%-default scenario produces a CET1 drawdown of 2.18 percentage points at Wells Fargo, breaching the Federal Reserve's 2025 DFAST exploratory baseline by 0.58 pp — narrowly, and concentrated at one institution. The February 19-April 8, 2026 semi-liquid private credit gate cascade is treated as a three-wave natural experiment. Treated alternative-asset managers accumulated a CAR of -10.10% at day +35 versus +0.07% for low-exposure diversified financials (difference -10.17pp, permutation p = 0.087); the secondary Apollo ADS event achieves p = 0.017 at the [0,+10]-day window, and the tertiary OCIC/OTIC event achieves p = 0.034. The paper makes four contributions: (1) the hand-curated bilateral matrix itself; (2) the three-wave reframing of the cascade with high statistical confidence at the secondary and tertiary events; (3) a disclosure-anchored DFAST extension establishing a quantitatively narrow tail-risk bound; and (4) the design and parameterization of a Contingent Private Credit Repo Facility (CPCRF). The companion theoretical paper is under submission at the International Journal of Central Banking. The K-A-T monolith is on SSRN (Abstract ID 6668858).

title: Predicting Dynamic Thermomechanical Responses of Ni-Ti Actuators Using Recurrent and Convolutional Neural Networks
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and Universidade Federal do Agreste de Pernambuco

detail.title: Predicting Dynamic Thermomechanical Responses of Ni-Ti Actuators Using Recurrent and Convolutional Neural Networks
detail.abstract: ​Characterizing the thermomechanical response of Titanium-Nickel (Ti-Ni) shape memory alloys (SMAs) typically requires extensive experiments, involving hundreds of heating and cooling cycles to generate thermal hysteresis curves. This study proposes a machine learning-based proxy model designed to replicate actuator functions, significantly reducing the reliance on exhaustive physical testing.Unlike traditional time-series forecasting, which predicts future values, this model focuses on predicting dynamic actuator responses (strain) based on new input profiles of temperature and mechanical stress. The strategy leverages deep neural networks to capture complex dynamics, specifically comparing Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) and 1D Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) for their ability to extract non-linear temporal patterns.To validate the model, three experimental datasets were generated using a helical spring actuator under varying loads. Hyperparameters were optimized via grid search. The results demonstrate that the proposed architectures generalize hysteresis curves with high precision, achieving a mean squared error (MSE) of less than 2%.

title: Digital Payments and Interest Rate Pass-Through: Evidence from India
affiliations: and JK Lakshmipat University – Institute of Management

detail.title: Digital Payments and Interest Rate Pass-Through: Evidence from India

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that they have no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.funderStatement: The authors received no specific funding for this research.

detail.abstract: We investigate how the introduction of a zero-cost retail digital-payments rail reshapes the transmission of monetary policy through bank deposit rates. The launch of India's Unified Payments Interface (UPI) in August 2016 collapsed the cost of moving funds across bank accounts to near zero, and within a decade UPI carried more retail payment volume than every other instrument combined. We extend the canonical Monti-Klein bank profit-maximisation problem with a twostage depositor choice-whether to hold deposits or cash, and which bank to deposit within which UPI affects each stage through a different channel. Higher contemporaneous UPI intensity raises depositors' switching elasticity across banks; longer accumulated UPI exposure raises the non-pecuniary value of holding deposits and lowers depositors' rate-elasticity overall. The two channels predict opposite signs for the average pass-through of monetary policy. Aggregate, bank-panel, and district-panel evidence delivers four empirical regularities. Pass-through to the term-deposit rate fell post-UPI by about 1.3 percentage points at the two-year horizon; passthrough to outstanding lending rates rose by about 0.9 percentage points; deposit and credit quantities flipped sign in their response to a tightening shock; and within-period cross-sectional gradients of pass-through widen with bank-level retail-deposit shares and district-level UPI penetration. A continuous Bartik instrument identifies the duration channel from predetermined cross-district variation. Taken jointly, the evidence indicates that UPI does not undermine monetary policy in India but shifts the margin through which policy is transmitted: from rates to quantities, and from depositors to loan demand.

title: Digital Financial Inclusion, Institutional Quality, And Banking Sector Performance: Evidence From High-Income Economies
affiliations: , Kohat University of Science and Technology, Department of Economics, Kohat University of Science and Technology and Kohat University of Science & Technology (KUST)

detail.title: Digital Financial Inclusion, Institutional Quality, And Banking Sector Performance: Evidence From High-Income Economies

declarations.declarationOfInterest: Acknowledgment: This article has been extracted from Aftab Ahmad Phd Thesis titled “The Impact Of Digital Financial Inclusion On Banking Sector performance: A Comparative Analysis Across High, Middle, And Low-Income Economies”
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study used publicly available/secondary data and did not involve direct participation of human subjects; therefore, ethical approval and informed consent were not required.
declarations.funderStatement: This paper has been published without any funded organization.

keywords: Principal Component Analysis JEL Classification: G21

detail.abstract: This study investigates the impact of digital financial inclusion (DFI) on banking sector performance (BSP) in high income economies, with a focus on the moderating role of institutional quality. Using a balanced panel dataset of 45 high income economies over 2011-2021, the study constructs composite indices for DFI, BSP, and institutional quality via Principal Component Analysis (PCA). The two-step System GMM estimator is employed to address endogeneity, dynamic persistence, and unobserved heterogeneity. The findings reveal that DFI significantly enhances BSP, while institutional quality does not significantly moderate this relationship, indicating that strong governance in advanced economies already supports effective digital financial adoption. Foreign bank presence also positively contributes to performance, whereas macroeconomic controls are largely insignificant. These results highlight the central role of DFI in promoting efficiency, profitability, and stability in mature banking systems.

title: GEOECONOMICS OF THE SOUTHERN GAS CORRIDOR: AZERBAIJAN-ITALY COOPERATION AS A STRATEGIC MODEL FOR EUROPEAN ENERGY SECURITY, ECONOMIC INTEGRATION, AND LONG-TERM GEOPOLITICAL STABILITY
affiliations: and Nakhchivan State University

detail.title: GEOECONOMICS OF THE SOUTHERN GAS CORRIDOR: AZERBAIJAN-ITALY COOPERATION AS A STRATEGIC MODEL FOR EUROPEAN ENERGY SECURITY, ECONOMIC INTEGRATION, AND LONG-TERM GEOPOLITICAL STABILITY

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that there is no conflict of interest regarding the publication of this study. The research was conducted independently, and no financial, institutional, or commercial relationships influenced the analysis, interpretation, or conclusions.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study is based on a systematic literature review and comparative geoeconomic analysis of the Southern Gas Corridor, drawing exclusively on secondary sources, academic publications, and policy reports. It did not involve human participants, surveys, interviews, or any form of personal data collection. Therefore, formal ethics committee approval was not required for this research.
declarations.funderStatement: This research did not receive any specific grant from funding agencies in the public, commercial, or non-profit sectors. The study was carried out independently by the author.

detail.abstract: The Southern Gas Corridor (SGC) represents a strategic geoeconomic initiative aimed at diversifying Europe's energy supply and mitigating the continent's reliance on single-source gas providers. Functioning as a multipipeline network, the SGC transports natural gas from Azerbaijan's Caspian fields through Georgia and Turkey, ultimately reaching southeastern and western European markets, with Italy serving as a critical hub in this energy chain (IEA, 2021; Socor, 2018). The corridor embodies a broader geoeconomic logic, wherein energy infrastructure is leveraged as a tool for both economic integration and geopolitical influence, reflecting the increasing convergence of market mechanisms and strategic statecraft (Blackwill & Harris, 2016; Meunier, 2019).Anchored in Azerbaijan-Italy bilateral cooperation, the SGC exemplifies how collaborative energy diplomacy can achieve multiple objectives simultaneously: enhancing European energy security, facilitating regional economic integration, and promoting political stability across the Euro-Caspian space. By creating an alternative supply route that bypasses traditional energy chokepoints, the SGC reduces vulnerabilities associated with over-dependence on dominant suppliers and mitigates geopolitical risks in a volatile regional environment (Yafimava, 2019; Baev, 2016).This study employs a systematic literature review and comparative geoeconomic analysis, integrating perspectives from international political economy, energy security studies, and regional cooperation frameworks (Tranfield, Denyer, & Smart, 2003; Eisenhardt, 1989). Findings indicate that the SGC not only strengthens Europe's energy diversification strategy but also reinforces the strategic positioning of transit and partner states, providing them with enhanced leverage in regional and multilateral decision-making arenas (Cornell, 2017; Delcour & Wolczuk, 2017). Furthermore, the corridor contributes to long-term geopolitical stability by supporting institutionalized cooperation, fostering economic interdependence, and promoting norms of transparency and regulatory alignment among participant states (Little, 2020; Edel, 2019).

title: Economic Implications of Ethanol Blending in India
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Economic Implications of Ethanol Blending in India
detail.abstract:
This study examines the impact of ethanol blending and selected macroeconomic variables on crude oil imports in India during 2003-2023. India, as one of the world’s largest crude oil importers, faces increasing concerns regarding energy security, rising import bills, and environmental sustainability. To address these challenges, the Government of India introduced the Ethanol Blended Petrol (EBP) Programme to reduce dependence on fossil fuels and promote sustainable energy alternatives.

The study analyzes whether ethanol blending has significantly reduced crude oil imports in India and examines the influence of GDP growth, exchange rate, world oil prices, and petroleum consumption on crude oil import dependence. Secondary time-series data were collected from sources including PPAC, the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, the World Bank, and Federal Reserve Economic Data (FRED). Since the variables were integrated at mixed orders, the Autoregressive Distributed Lag (ARDL) model was applied. The study also employed the Bounds Cointegration Test, Error Correction Model (ECM), and diagnostic tests to examine both short-run and long-run relationships.

The findings reveal that domestic energy demand has a significant positive effect on crude oil imports. Lagged GDP growth and exchange rate changes were also found to significantly influence crude oil imports. However, the ethanol blending variable did not show a statistically significant impact on reducing crude oil imports during the study period. The Bounds Test confirmed the existence of a long-run relationship among the variables, while diagnostic tests indicated that the model is statistically reliable and free from major econometric issues.

The study concludes that ethanol blending is an important step toward sustainable energy transition, but it has not yet significantly reduced India’s dependence on crude oil imports. The study recommends expanding ethanol infrastructure, encouraging second-generation ethanol production, and strengthening renewable energy policies to improve long-term energy security and sustainability in India.

title: Sensitivity Analysis of Rod Ejection Accident Based on PWR MOX/UO₂ Benchmark
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Sensitivity Analysis of Rod Ejection Accident Based on PWR MOX/UO₂ Benchmark
detail.abstract: To better understand the rod ejection accident(REA) process in pressurized water reactors(PWRs) containing MOX fuel, and to investigate the main influencing parameters and their influence laws on key evaluation parameters such as core relative power peak after rod ejection, this paper takes the PWR MOX/UO₂ transient benchmark core as the research object. The newly pin-by-pin wise transient neutronics/thermal-hydraulic(N-TH) coupling code CORCA-SPₙ, based on the SPₙ method and developed by the Nuclear Power Institute of China(NPIC), was employed to conduct sensitivity analysis for the zero-power rod ejection case in Part IV of the benchmark. A total of 39 rod ejection conditions were simulated, covering 10 key parameters including rod ejection speed. The results show that: 1) Delayed neutron fraction, rod ejection speed, boron concentration, core inlet temperature, and transient time step size have significant influences on the core relative power peak, reactivity peak, super-prompt critical duration, average core coolant temperature, and average core fuel temperature during the zero-power rod ejection transient, and they are identified as key parameters affecting the rod ejection results. 2) The top four parameters affecting the core relative power peak and reactivity peak are ranked as: delayed neutron fraction, boron concentration, core inlet temperature, and rod ejection speed. 3) Neutron velocity, gap heat transfer coefficient, fuel Doppler temperature weighting coefficient, and core inlet mass flow rate show no obvious influence on the reactivity peak during the rod ejection transient.

title: Goal-Driven Mobile Robot Navigation via Deep Reinforcement Learning with Geometric-Enhanced Dual Prioritized Experience Replay
affiliations: Zhengzhou University, Zhengzhou University, Zhengzhou University, Zhengzhou University, University of Macau and Queen Mary University of London

detail.title: Goal-Driven Mobile Robot Navigation via Deep Reinforcement Learning with Geometric-Enhanced Dual Prioritized Experience Replay
detail.abstract: This paper addresses goal-driven mobile robot navigation in cluttered grid environments with sparse and delayed rewards. To improve convergence speed, sample efficiency, and training stability, a novel learning framework based on the double deep Q-network is proposed.   The framework integrates a geometric-enhanced dual prioritized experience replay mechanism with adaptive sampling to improve the reuse of high-value transitions while preserving replay diversity, a geometric-informed pretraining strategy to reduce inefficient early exploration, and a potential-based reward shaping scheme to provide denser feedback and stabilize policy learning. ​ The proposed method is applied to mobile robot path planning under different obstacle densities, where the robot must reach the target safely and efficiently while avoiding collisions. Extensive simulations with obstacle coverages of 20\%--40\% show that the proposed method converges faster, achieves higher cumulative rewards, requires less runtime, and consistently generates shorter collision-free paths than representative baseline methods. These results demonstrate that the proposed artificial intelligence framework provides an effective solution for practical mobile robot navigation and path-planning tasks.

title: Riverside Renaissance: Transforming Dhaka Sadarghat for Tourism
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Riverside Renaissance: Transforming Dhaka Sadarghat for Tourism

declarations.ethicsApproval: This research is primarily based on architectural and urban design analysis, site studies, and secondary data sources. No human participants, clinical procedures, or sensitive personal data were involved in the study. Therefore, formal ethics approval was not required for this research. Any visual documentation and contextual information used have been collected and presented solely for academic and research purposes.

detail.abstract:
This thesis explores the revitalization potential of Sadarghat through a tourism-oriented urban redevelopment strategy titled Riverside Renaissance: Transforming Dhaka Sadarghat for Tourism. As one of the most historically and economically significant riverfronts in Dhaka, Sadarghat currently faces severe challenges including congestion, environmental degradation, inadequate public spaces, and unplanned urban growth. The project investigates how sustainable architectural and urban design interventions can reconnect the city with its waterfront while enhancing cultural identity, economic activity, and public accessibility.

The research focuses on creating an integrated riverfront development framework that promotes tourism, recreational activities, pedestrian connectivity, and mixed-use public spaces while preserving the historical and socio-cultural character of the area. Through site analysis, urban studies, spatial planning, and contextual architectural strategies, the proposal aims to transform Sadarghat into a vibrant, accessible, and environmentally responsive urban destination. The thesis ultimately demonstrates how strategic waterfront redevelopment can contribute to urban regeneration, improve the public realm, and establish a sustainable tourism hub within the dense metropolitan context of Dhaka.

title: Willingness to Pay to Avoid Black Swan Events Related to Flood Risks
affiliations: RWTH Aachen University - RWTH Aachen University, Students, RWTH Aachen University - Institute for Future Energy Consumer Needs and Behavior (FCN) and RWTH Aachen University

detail.title: Willingness to Pay to Avoid Black Swan Events Related to Flood Risks
detail.abstract:
The 2021 Ahrtal flood in western Germany was one of the country’s costliest natural
disasters and has reopened the debate on how flood protection should be financed. This
paper examines residents’ willingness to pay (WTP) for future flood mitigation four years
after the event. Using a contingent valuation survey of 103 residents, we estimate OLS and
logistic regressions complemented by a bootstrap mediation analysis. We identify three
main patterns. First, household income (ω = 0.508, p < 0.001) and the belief that climate
change increases extreme weather events (ω = 0.526, p = 0.002) are the strongest and
most stable predictors of WTP. Second, direct flood experience is associated with higher
WTP primarily through heightened concern about future flooding rather than through
exposure itself, consistent with a perceptual rather than proportional channel. Third,
while 73.8% of respondents express a positive WTP, they overwhelmingly prefer collec-
tive, tax-based financing (62.1%) over individual insurance premiums (28.2%). Among
zero-WTP respondents, refusal is driven primarily by normative views about government
responsibility (77.8%) rather than by financial inability (33.3%). Given the modest and
non-probabilistic sample, we interpret these results as indicative case-study evidence. The
findings carry implications for the current German debate on mandatory natural hazard
insurance — particularly for the design of premium structures that do not compound the
vulnerabilities of the worst-affected households.

title: Gendered Pricing Across Economies: A Comparative Study of the Pink Tax in the US, UK, and India
affiliations: reDot, reDot, reDot, reDot, Independent, reDot and

detail.title: Gendered Pricing Across Economies: A Comparative Study of the Pink Tax in the US, UK, and India
detail.abstract: This study examines gendered pricing, often known as the "pink tax", in the United States, the United Kingdom, and India. The "pink tax" is examined in these countries in both goods and services, primarily in areas like self-care. The results show that the US shows the steepest difference in price, whereas Southeast Asia has a relatively low difference in both genders' products, but still a difference that is large enough to be concerned about. The research also compares the three countries, examining each of the cultures, economies, social norms, etc. The discussions in this paper address how this gendered pricing affects women, specifically teenagers and women from lower-income families. This paper provides policy implications and potential long-term solutions to these issues, like awareness on social media, campaigns created by women and consumers, and larger businesses investing time to decrease the pink tax.

title: Machine Learning for Italian Non-Performing Loan Valuation: A Methodology Framework with Purged Cross-Validation

detail.title: Machine Learning for Italian Non-Performing Loan Valuation: A Methodology Framework with Purged Cross-Validation
detail.abstract: We develop and demonstrate a machine learning framework for valuing Italian non-performing loans (NPLs), addressing three methodological gaps in the existing literature. First, we implement purged cross-validation with embargo periods (Lopez de Prado 2018), preventing the look-ahead bias that contaminates standard k-fold evaluation in financial time series. Second, we deploy LightGBM with native categorical feature support, efficiently handling the high-cardinality judicial district variable (26 districts) that drives Italian NPL recovery heterogeneity. Third, we provide SHAP-based global and local explanations, identifying judicial district duration, collateral type, and geographic region as the dominant recovery rate drivers — information directly actionable by NPL servicers and banking regulators. The framework comprises six interconnected models: an Automated Valuation Model (AVM) for property collateral, a recovery rate predictor, Weibull maximum likelihood estimation for recovery timing curves, share-of-wallet and unsecured credit models, and a Nash bargaining Zone of Possible Agreement (ZOPA) calculator for secondary market transactions. Using a synthetic dataset of 100,000 loans with 37 features calibrated to aggregate statistics from Banca d'Italia, the Osservatorio del Mercato Immobiliare (OMI), and the Ministero della Giustizia — enriched with feature distributions from an operational NPL platform — we report out-of-time validation (train pre-2022, test 2022-2025) as the primary metric: the recovery rate model achieves R^2 = 0.73 with MAE = 0.08, while the AVM achieves R^2 = 0.50. Weibull curves reveal a stark North-South divide: median recovery time of approximately 25 months in Northern Italy versus 70 months in the South, reflecting judicial system heterogeneity. Synthetic-data disclosure: the paper is honest that the data is synthetic, calibrated to aggregate Italian statistics. The framework is designed as a methodology contribution demonstrating ML best practices for NPL valuation; results are illustrative of the approach. A path to real-data validation through partnership with Italian NPL servicers is documented in the limitations section.

title: High-frequency enhanced Physics Informed Neural Network for Joint Traffic State Estimation and Prediction: Heterogeneous Data Fusion from Fixed Detectors and Connected Autonomous Vehicles
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, Southeast University and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: High-frequency enhanced Physics Informed Neural Network for Joint Traffic State Estimation and Prediction: Heterogeneous Data Fusion from Fixed Detectors and Connected Autonomous Vehicles
detail.abstract: Accurate spatiotemporal traffic state estimation and prediction across highway segments remains a challenge for intelligent transportation systems under sparse and heterogeneous observations. While physics informed neural networks have emerged as a promising paradigm for this problem, existing approaches suffer from three compounding limitations: spectral bias in standard fully connected neural networks that prevents accurate representation of high-frequency traffic dynamics such as stop-and-go waves; the absence of a unified representation reconciling structurally distinct Eulerian fixed detector and Lagrangian Connected Autonomous Vehicles trajectory modalities; and the decoupled treatment of estimation and prediction that precludes physically consistent forward extrapolation. This paper proposes a unified High-frequency enhanced physics informed neural network integrating Transformer encoder that jointly addresses these limitations through three tightly integrated contributions. First, a hybrid architecture combining Random Fourier Feature embedding with a Transformer encoder lifts spatiotemporal coordinates into a rich trigonometric feature space, enabling adaptive frequency-selective composition over multi-scale traffic patterns. Second, a unified binary observation mask matrix consolidates Connected Autonomous Vehicles trajectories and fixed detector measurements into a modality-agnostic input representation. Third, a composite physics-data loss jointly enforces observational fidelity and the traffic flow model across both the historical estimation window and the future prediction horizon, enabling physically consistent state extrapolation within a single inference pass. Extensive experiments across three datasets: simulation, NGSIM, and Wuhan at two spatiotemporal resolutions and seven observational configurations demonstrate that the proposed approach consistently outperforms model-driven, data-driven, and hybrid baselines on joint estimation and prediction tasks, confirming its robustness and generalizability for intelligent transportation applications.

title: Dynamic and Uncertainty‑Aware Risk Ranking in Nuclear Cooling Systems Using a BN‑Driven p‑VIKOR Approach
affiliations: National Institute of Technology Jamshedpur, National Institute of Technology Jamshedpur and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Dynamic and Uncertainty‑Aware Risk Ranking in Nuclear Cooling Systems Using a BN‑Driven p‑VIKOR Approach
detail.abstract: Reliable risk prioritisation in the Emergency Core Cooling System (ECCS) of nuclear power plants requires decision‑support methods that can represent causal dependencies and update failure likelihoods under changing operating conditions. This work develops a dynamic approach that integrates (i) Bayesian Networks (BN) for evidence‑responsive estimation of component‑level failure probabilities, (ii) Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) derived weights for Severity, Likelihood, and Detectability, and (iii) a probabilistic VIKOR (p‑VIKOR) formulation that incorporates BN posterior variance into the compromise ranking. The approach supports uncertainty‑aware decision‑making by combining operational evidence with expert judgement in a structured multicriteria setting. A case study involving four representative ECCS failure modes evaluates the proposed method under two tested scenarios: nominal operating conditions and a vibration‑induced degradation condition. The Bayesian Network produces scenario‑dependent shifts in failure likelihoods that static AHP–VIKOR does not capture, while the proposed p‑VIKOR extension applies uncertainty based penalisation without altering ranking order. Within the scope of the evaluated scenarios, the results indicate that the proposed approach produces scenario‑dependent changes in risk prioritisation that reflect both the updated BN likelihoods and the associated uncertainty in these estimates.

title: The radically transparent route to an environmentally conscious energy model

detail.title: The radically transparent route to an environmentally conscious energy model
detail.abstract: The radical transparent route towards an environmentally conscious energy model Imagine that ten years ago you landed on a planet similar to Earth and were tasked with designing the most important model for transportation, transport, and energy supply. Three main conditions must be met that guarantee substantial bonus points: 1) replace religion as the primary cause of international conflicts; 2) leave road and public transport users in a state of desperation; and 3) leave households completely at the mercy of loud, obnoxious utility companies. The solution? A car with an internal combustion engine, Dutch Railways, and Dutch utility firm NUON.

title: The Vaiman Model: Synchronizing Biblical Chronology and Ancient Near East Archaeology via the 364-Day Calendar and Jubilee Intercalation
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: The Vaiman Model: Synchronizing Biblical Chronology and Ancient Near East Archaeology via the 364-Day Calendar and Jubilee Intercalation
detail.abstract: The 364-day calendar, extensively documented in the Dead Sea Scrolls and Second Temple literature, has historically been dismissed as an impractical, non-functional system due to its inherent solar drift of approximately 1.24 days per year. This paper proposes the "Vaiman Model," a systemic and mathematical framework that resolves this drift through a 50-day intercalation cycle occurring every Jubilee (50 years). By applying this deterministic calendar and the principle of "System Uptime" (counting only periods of national sovereignty) to the biblical narrative, the model achieves an absolute synchronization with the archaeological record. The results place the Exodus at 1550 BCE, aligning with the destruction of Jericho IV and Tel Haror, and synchronize the Davidic-Solomonic era with Carbon-14 data from Khirbet Qeiyafa (1020-980 BCE) and Tel Megiddo (967-943 BCE). The model suggests that the biblical counting of the Omer and the Jubilee were not merely ritualistic but functioned as a decentralized, "antifragile" socioeconomic operating system.

title: Network Topology and Systemic Contagion Among Alternative Asset Managers: Evidence from GP-LP-Bank Interconnections

detail.title: Network Topology and Systemic Contagion Among Alternative Asset Managers: Evidence from GP-LP-Bank Interconnections
detail.abstract: This paper investigates the network structure of interconnections among alternative asset managers (general partners, GPs), their limited partners (LPs), and banking counterparties, and examines how this tripartite topology shapes systemic contagion dynamics. Using SEC Form ADV filings, 13F institutional holdings, and BIS bank-NBFI lending statistics, we construct a tripartite network of 179 GPs (all registered investment advisers with >$1B AUM in alternatives), 113 institutional LPs (pension funds, sovereign wealth funds, endowments, insurance companies, foundations, and family offices), and 35 major bank counterparties (327 nodes). Bilateral exposures are reconstructed via maximum-entropy iterative proportional fitting from aggregate marginals, with power-law sparsification producing realistic heterogeneous degree distributions. Applying DebtRank methodology (Battiston et al., 2012), we derive per-node systemic-importance scores and characterize the contagion amplification factor as a function of the spectral radius of the normalized exposure matrix. The March 2026 private-credit crisis provides a natural experiment: sequential gating events at Blackstone Credit (BCRED, 7.9%), BlackRock HPS Corporate Lending (HLEND, 9.3%), and Cliffwater Corporate Lending (14%) triggered $265 billion in cumulative market capitalization destruction. Betweenness centrality predicts gating order (Spearman rho = 0.195, p = 0.009), with Blackstone ranking first by eigenvector centrality. Logistic regression yields pseudo R^2 = 0.147. Monte Carlo stress tests (10,000 scenarios) indicate that simultaneous distress at the three most central nodes generates system losses of 11.6% of network value vs 1.9% for random nodes — a 6.2x amplification. The paper proposes a Designated Systemically Important Non-Bank Financial Institution (D-SINBFI) framework calibrated to network metrics, addressing the FSOC designation vacuum exposed by the March 2026 crisis. Companion papers cover the K-A-T macro framework (SSRN 6668858), the disclosure-anchored DFAST extension and CPCRF policy proposal, and Italian NPL machine-learning methodology.

title: Plausible and Robust Counterfactual Explanation via Local Distribution Consistency
affiliations: Anhui University, Anhui University, Anhui University and Anhui University

detail.title: Plausible and Robust Counterfactual Explanation via Local Distribution Consistency
detail.abstract: In explainable machine learning, counterfactual explanations reveal key factors influencing model decisions by constructing hypothetical scenarios (for example, "if the inputs changed, the outputs would differ."). Most existing methods generate counterfactuals by minimizing the distance between the generated instance and the original input, as well as other constraints. However, prioritizing proximity can degrade plausibility and robustness. Our analysis attributes this trade-off to neglecting consistency with the target class's local data distribution during counterfactual generation.To address this, we propose a new method that balances proximity, plausibility, and robustness by enforcing local distribution consistency. Specifically, we introduce a novel loss function consisting of two terms: Local Density Loss and Feature Deviation Loss. The Local Density Loss steers generated counterfactuals toward high-density regions of the target class, improving plausibility. The Feature Deviation Loss preserves proximity by restricting modifications to salient features, encouraging alignment with the target class in those dimensions, while minimizing changes to less important features to enhance robustness. Additionally, we propose an enhanced particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm that integrates feature weights into the velocity update to accelerate targeted search. Extensive experiments and visualized case study illustrate that our new method can effectively balances plausibility, robustness, and proximity.

title: DİGİTALİZATİON AND INTERNATİONAL PROJECT MANAGEMENT: EVİDENCE FROM DEVELOPİNG ECONOMİES
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: DİGİTALİZATİON AND INTERNATİONAL PROJECT MANAGEMENT: EVİDENCE FROM DEVELOPİNG ECONOMİES
detail.abstract: Digitalization has significantly transformed project management practices worldwide, particularly in the context of international projects. The increasing use of digital technologies enables more efficient communication, coordination, and monitoring of project activities across borders. However, the impact of digitalization on international project management remains insufficiently explored in developing economies. This study investigates the relationship between digitalization and international project performance in developing countries. Using secondary data and existing literature, the research highlights how digital tools enhance transparency, reduce project risks, and improve decision-making processes. The findings indicate that digitalization plays a crucial role in increasing the efficiency and success rate of international projects in developing economies. The study also emphasizes the importance of strengthening digital infrastructure and institutional capacity to maximize the benefits of digital technologies in project management.

title: When Cooperation Leaves Criminal Law: Constitutional Limits on the Importation of Criminal Procedural Techniques into Collective Public Sanctioning Litigation

detail.title: When Cooperation Leaves Criminal Law: Constitutional Limits on the Importation of Criminal Procedural Techniques into Collective Public Sanctioning Litigation

keywords: constitutional procedural law. Table of Contents: 1. Introduction. 2. The Expansion of Criminal Procedural Techniques into Collective Public Sanctioning Litigation. 3. Plea Bargaining and the Extracriminal

detail.abstract: This article examines the constitutional limits of importing criminal procedural techniques into collective sanctioning actions aimed at protecting public assets and administrative morality in Brazil. Based on the increasing use of criminal procedural mechanismsespecially plea bargaining, evidentiary sharing, procedural flexibility, negotiated enforcement tools and collaborative evidentiary structureswithin the framework of the Brazilian Administrative Improbity Act (Law No. 8,429/1992) and the Brazilian Anti-Corruption Act (Law No. 12,846/2013), the study investigates the emergence of a hybrid sanctioning procedure positioned between collective litigation, administrative sanctioning law and criminal accusatory rationality. It argues that the expansion of such mechanisms cannot occur asymmetrically through the importation of prosecutorial enhancement tools without the simultaneous incorporation of the fundamental guarantees structuring the constitutional criminal model. The article analyzes the growing interaction among negotiated sanctions, procedural cooperation and collective public enforcement, examining the risks of erosion of adversarial guarantees, equality of arms, legal certainty and substantive due process. It further argues that the constitutionalization of public sanctioning procedure requires strict scrutiny over the circulation of criminal procedural categories beyond their original normative environments. The study ultimately defends that the Brazilian collective sanctioning microsystem is progressively evolving into an autonomous constitutional procedural structure, demanding its own coherent balance between institutional effectiveness and fundamental procedural guarantees.

title: The King's French: The Political Economy of Language and National Identity
affiliations: University of Evansville - School of Business Administration and Ohio State University (OSU)

detail.title: The King's French: The Political Economy of Language and National Identity
detail.abstract: We investigate the impact of language policy on language choice, linguistic standardization, and national identity. In 1539, the Ordinance of Villers-Cotterêts made French the official administrative language of France. Using a geographic difference-in-discontinuities design exploiting the French border, we show that Villers-Cotterêts caused a dramatic shift away from Latin toward French in the larger print market and homogenized printed French. We then show that the ordinance fostered French national identity, as reflected in book titles, and that towns with larger ordinance-induced shifts toward vernacular printing expressed stronger national identity on the eve of the French Revolution.

title: THE CHALLENGES AND OPPORTUNITIES OF MANAGING VIRTUAL TEAMS AND REMOTE WORKERS IN THE DIGITAL AGE

detail.title: THE CHALLENGES AND OPPORTUNITIES OF MANAGING VIRTUAL TEAMS AND REMOTE WORKERS IN THE DIGITAL AGE
detail.abstract: The use of virtual teams and remote workers has become increasingly common in the digital age, and managing these teams presents unique challenges and opportunities for organizations. This research paper aims to explore the challenges and opportunities of managing virtual teams and remote workers in the digital age. The paper reviews the existing literature on virtual teams and remote work, identifies the challenges and opportunities associated with managing these teams, and proposes strategies to overcome the challenges and leverage the opportunities. The paper also presents the methodology used to collect and analyze the data, the results of the data analysis, and the implications for management practice and future research. Ultimately, this research paper provides a comprehensive understanding of the challenges and opportunities of managing virtual teams and remote workers in the digital age, and provides guidance for managers in developing effective strategies to manage these teams.

title: Role of ECGC and Commercial Banks in Export Risk Management: Application of Artificial Intelligence in International Trade
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Role of ECGC and Commercial Banks in Export Risk Management: Application of Artificial Intelligence in International Trade
detail.abstract:
This paper examines the role of Export Credit Guarantee Corporation of India (ECGC) and commercial banks in managing export-related risks, along with the growing application of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in export risk management. International trade involves several financial and commercial uncertainties such as buyer default, political instability, currency fluctuations, and transport risks. To reduce these risks and support exporters, ECGC provides credit insurance and guarantees, while commercial banks offer trade finance facilities such as pre-shipment finance, post-shipment finance, letters of credit, and bank guarantees.

The study explains the major schemes and functions of ECGC, the role of commercial banks in export finance, and the coordination between both institutions in creating a secure export ecosystem. The paper also highlights how AI technologies such as Machine Learning (ML), Natural Language Processing (NLP), Big Data Analytics, Predictive Analytics, and Robotic Process Automation (RPA) are transforming export risk assessment and trade finance operations.

Practical examples of AI applications in ECGC operations, Indian commercial banks, and global trade finance systems have been discussed to show how AI improves fraud detection, buyer risk analysis, document verification, and claim processing. The paper concludes that the integration of ECGC, commercial banks, and AI-driven technologies can significantly strengthen India’s export sector by making export risk management faster, smarter, and more efficient.

title: Korean Dream: Integration Waste and the Structural Divergence of Filipino Migration Pathways in South Korea, 2021 to 2026

detail.title: Korean Dream: Integration Waste and the Structural Divergence of Filipino Migration Pathways in South Korea, 2021 to 2026

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author is a Filipino filmmaker and long-term resident of South Korea who is a member of the community studied. The author's production entity, PinoySeoul Media Enterprise, is not affiliated with Pinoy Seoul Gigs, an entertainment company founded by one of the study participants; the shared naming is coincidental. The Commission on Filipinos Overseas provided institutional access for the documentary fieldwork phase but had no role in the design, analysis, or conclusions of this study. No financial or personal relationships influenced the findings.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study is based on voluntary filmed interviews conducted as part of a documentary project. All participants provided informed consent to appear on camera and to be identified by name in published materials. Participants' real names are used with their ongoing consent, consistent with their voluntary participation in the documentary. Sarah and Johbert are identified by first name only at their request. The study was conducted in accordance with the ethical principles of arts-based and participatory action research.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding. The initial 2021 fieldwork was conducted as part of a collaborative documentary project with Melanie Arroyave during her Luce Scholarship in South Korea, with institutional support from the Commission on Filipinos Overseas. The longitudinal phase (2022 to 2026) was self-funded by the author.

detail.abstract: This paper introduces the concept of "integration waste," defined as the systematic destruction of accumulated migrant human capital through rigid visa expiry, and demonstrates its operation through a five-year longitudinal qualitative study (2021 to 2026) of six Filipino migrants in South Korea. Employing narrative inquiry, auto-ethnography, and visual ethnography within a participatory action research framework, the study tracks migration trajectories across five visa categories: professional (E-7), informal creative economy, industrial labor (E-9), marriage migration (F-6), and religious ministry (F-visa). The findings reveal a structural divergence in integration outcomes. Participants with access to flexible visa pathways remained in South Korea and deepened their civic roles over the study period, while participants on rigid Employment Permit System visas were compelled to leave despite years of language acquisition, community building, and economic contribution. This divergence functions as a natural comparison in visa design. Against the backdrop of South Korea's record-low total fertility rate of 0.72 in 2023 and projected population halving by 2100, the paper argues that integration waste is not merely a humanitarian concern but a form of demographic and economic self-harm. The study proposes that South Korea's transition from labor extraction to stakeholder retention is an institutional imperative, not a concession.

title: Appointment Scheduling of Outpatient Clinical Services under Uncertain Patient Flows
affiliations: City Univ. of Hong Kong - College of Business, Dept of Management Sciences, Mitchell E. Daniels, Jr School of Business, Purdue University, Purdue University - Krannert School of Management and

detail.title: Appointment Scheduling of Outpatient Clinical Services under Uncertain Patient Flows
detail.abstract: We study the problem of appointment scheduling for outpatient clinical services, where patient arrivals, appointment cancellations, and attendance are inherently random, leading to high variability in patient flow. Analyzing dynamic scheduling decisions is particularly challenging due to the need to track confirmed appointments within the scheduling window. For planning with a long horizon, we show that a probabilistic allocation policy can be efficiently computed by optimizing a closed form function. This policy ensures that the system’s long-term profit asymptotically approaches the optimal profit in scalable settings. For a limited planning horizon, we propose a sequential assignment process implemented with a pre-determined scheduling diagram. We characterize the conditions under which this scheduling diagram policy achieves optimality. Notably, an improved scheduling diagram policy emerges as a refinement of either a probabilistic allocation policy or a same-day scheduling policy, and we prove that it is optimal for two-day scheduling windows. The computation of the scheduling diagrams is straightforward, as it involves ranking the margins (i.e., first-order differences) of scalar profit functions, one for each day in the scheduling window. Extensive simulation analyses suggest that system efficiency can be achieved through a hybrid strategy, where a two-day policy is applied to a short scheduling window and an improved probabilistic policy is used for a long scheduling window.

title: ANALYSING THE INFLUENCE OF SOCIAL AND FAMILY FACTORS ON WOMEN'S ENTREPRENEURIAL SUCCESS

detail.title: ANALYSING THE INFLUENCE OF SOCIAL AND FAMILY FACTORS ON WOMEN'S ENTREPRENEURIAL SUCCESS
detail.abstract: All over the world, entrepreneurship has been traditionally recognized as male prerogative. However, because of change in socio-cultural environment, increasing importance for girl child education, government policies and schemes of NGOs towards women entrepreneurship have started recognizing inherent talents and business skills of women and hence the number of women is increased in joining the rank list of entrepreneurships. In modern society, we talk and debate more about the gender equalities and frame special policies to improve the status of women in the society. Therefore, the major objective of the present study is to analyzing the influence of social and family factors on women's entrepreneurial success. To fulfill the objectives, the researcher conducted the survey in Pune, Maharashtra and served the structured questionnaire to 122 female entrepreneurs and the researcher also adopted the face-to-face interview techniques wherever required. To analyze the data culled out, the simple statistics were used to know the relativity of the problem faced by women's entrepreneurs. The study revealed that problems like dual role, social harassment, work stress, etc. are more with women's entrepreneurs.

title: Interactional Ego: How Human Differences Become Symbolic Barriers of Social Association

detail.title: Interactional Ego: How Human Differences Become Symbolic Barriers of Social Association

declarations.declarationOfInterest: NIL
declarations.funderStatement: No Funding

detail.abstract: Background: Ego has been extensively theorized within psychoanalytic, sociological, and spiritual traditions, yet its operation as a specifically interactional and relational phenomenon within ordinary social life remains underexplored. Existing frameworks treat ego primarily as an internal psychological structure, a class-based symbolic mechanism, or a spiritual attachmentbut rarely as a dynamic process through which human differences are transformed into barriers of social association. Objective: This study introduces and develops the concept of "interactional ego"defined as the psychological attachment to superiority-based identity that creates discomfort, symbolic distancing, and narrowing of acceptable human association within ordinary social relations. The paper argues that ego, in this interactional form, constitutes not merely an individual moral failing but a social structure continuously reproduced through comparison, institutional segregation, purity attachment, and performative identity. Method: The study employs a qualitative conceptual analysis approach, drawing on interpretive sociological theory, philosophical reflection, and systematic examination of observable social patterns across diverse everyday contexts. The theoretical framework engages critically with Bourdieu's sociology of distinction, Goffman's dramaturgical model of social interaction, and Buddhist-philosophical accounts of ego and attachment, extending these frameworks toward a new relational and interactional formulation. Findings: The analysis identifies five primary mechanisms through which interactional ego operates: standards-based superiority formation, comparison and competitive identity, purityconditioned aversion, fear of identity loss, and performative humility or ego of ego-lessness. The study further demonstrates that certain collective institutional environmentsincluding sports contexts, artistic communities, and shared residential systemspossess ego-reducing potential, while simultaneously generating new ego forms through fame, achievement, and moral hierarchy. A conceptually significant finding concerns identity continuity in advanced old age, where the maintenance of purposeful social identity appears functionally distinct from superiority-based ego and psychologically protective against depression and social withdrawal. Conclusion: The study concludes that the central challenge of civilizational development is not merely improvement of material standards, but preservation of human connectedness amidst increasing symbolic differentiation. Interactional ego narrows the range of acceptable human association and contributes to subtle psychological fragmentation within society. The paper proposes that reduction of such ego requires not moral instruction alone, but structural conditionsinstitutional, educational, and socialthat offer coherent identity without dependence on symbolic hierarchy.

title:
Stratospheric Autonomous Surveillance and Interdiction Platform (SASIP): 
A Feasibility Study for Persistent Counter-UAV Defense Infrastructure
affiliations: Alexandria University

detail.title:
Stratospheric Autonomous Surveillance and Interdiction Platform (SASIP): 
A Feasibility Study for Persistent Counter-UAV Defense Infrastructure

declarations.declarationOfInterest: This research received no external funding and was conducted independently as part of ongoing academic and technical research activities.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding and was conducted as an independent academic and engineering study.

detail.abstract:
This paper presents the Stratospheric Autonomous Surveillance and Interdiction Platform (SASIP), a conceptual national defense system designed to address structural gaps in counter-unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) capabilities. SASIP proposes a free-floating, solar-powered stratospheric aerostat operating at 20,000-40,000 m altitude, equipped with a multimodal sensor suite comprising RF spectrum monitoring, infrared detection, optical surveillance, and passive radar, fused through an artificial intelligence-driven command and control architecture. 
     Operating above the effective envelope of most UAV systems, the platform enables wide-area, line-of-sight surveillance exceeding 500 km radius and sustained endurance through solar energy. The system is architected as a persistent intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (ISR) layer, providing continuous detection, tracking, and classification of aerial activity. 
     Countermeasure capabilities are implemented as externally authorized response modules, including non-kinetic RF disruption and gravity-assisted interceptor payloads. These operate outside the AI decision loop and require explicit human authorization. 
     This study presents the technical architecture, engagement physics, national coverage modeling for Egypt's 1,010,000 km 2 territory, and system limitations, framing SASIP as a persistent, high-altitude ISR infrastructure layer with integrated but controlled response capabilities.

title: Structural Inevitability: A Balance Sheet Explanation of Retail Investor Behavior in China's A-Share Market

detail.title: Structural Inevitability: A Balance Sheet Explanation of Retail Investor Behavior in China's A-Share Market

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflict of interest.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This study is a theoretical analysis using publicly available data and does not involve human participants.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: This paper proposes a theoretical framework centered on individual net cash flow structure to explain the systematic speculative behavior of small-account retail investors in China's A-share market. We introduce the concept of "life as liability": each individual's monthly expenditure constitutes an installment payment on the present value of their lifetime survival expenditure—an implicit total liability owed to their own existence. When labor income approximately equals the installment payment and asset income approaches zero, the individual enters a state of desperate capital, in which holding periods are structurally compressed by the survival liability. Speculation targeting an illusory return rate is a rational attempt to balance the survival liability from the income side; "lying flat" (tang ping) is the symmetric rational strategy from the expenditure side. Existing literature attributes small-account speculation to financial illiteracy; we challenge this fundamentally. Age-stratification data reveal that middle-aged retail investors with over a decade of experience display behavioral patterns identical to new entrants, directly questioning the education hypothesis. Large-account profitability reflects multiple structural advantages whose core mechanism is exploiting desperate capital's demand for illusory returns by manufacturing rapid price movements. Seven decades of U.S. equity market structural change independently validates the mechanism cross-nationally.

title: The Geopolitical Repricing of AI Infrastructure: Energy, Risk, and Strategic Allocation
affiliations: and Independent

detail.title: The Geopolitical Repricing of AI Infrastructure: Energy, Risk, and Strategic Allocation
detail.abstract: This paper argues that geopolitical instability is not merely an external shock to artificial intelligence (AI) development but a structural force that reconfigures the economic and strategic foundations of AI infrastructure. We introduce the idea of Geopolitical Repricing, defined as the structural revaluation of AI infrastructure amid heightened geopolitical risk, in which cost structures, risk assessments, and investment priorities shift from efficiency-driven optimisation towards resilience, security, and sovereignty. Drawing on recent geopolitical tensions, particularly in energy-sensitive regions, we identify three primary transmission channels through which these shocks propagate into AI systems: energy market volatility, supply chain disruptions, and infrastructure vulnerabilities. These channels collectively raise the cost of compute, embed geopolitical risk in investment criteria, and reorient capital allocation decisions among both private and public actors. As a result, AI infrastructure is increasingly treated as a risk-adjusted strategic asset rather than a purely commercial input, contributing to the expansion of sovereign compute capabilities, the adoption of redundancy-oriented system design, and defence-aligned AI investment. The paper contributes to the emerging literature on AI governance and political economy by reframing AI not as a neutral technological domain but as an infrastructure subject to geopolitical repricing dynamics. Implications for governance, investment strategy, and global technological fragmentation are discussed.

title: THE INSTITUTIONAL ARCHITECTURE OF LAYTIME: TRANSACTION COSTS AND BLOCKCHAIN AS AN
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: THE INSTITUTIONAL ARCHITECTURE OF LAYTIME: TRANSACTION COSTS AND BLOCKCHAIN AS AN
detail.abstract: Port inefficiency is, above all, a governance failure. This essay investigates the Statement of Facts (SoF) conciliation through the lens of New Institutional Economics. We demonstrate that the manual timekeeping model creates an environment of severe information asymmetry and moral hazard, driving up ex-post transaction costs. The introduction of Blockchain technology is proposed not merely as an IT tool, but as an exogenous institution designed to suppress opportunism and restore informational symmetry in logistics contracts.
