detail.abstract: Traditional strategic management relies heavily on expert intuition and qualitative narratives, often failing in highly volatile and non-linear business environments due to a lack of rigorous dimensional constraints. This paper proposes a novel quantitative strategic audit frameworkthe Xuanji system. Based on the "Law of Universal Isomorphism," the framework deeply integrates system dynamics with Bayesian epistemology to derive the core "Strategic Effectiveness Axiom". For the first time, the binding strength between strategic vision and physical assets (Logical Density) is strictly aligned with the Bayesian likelihood probability P(E|H). In terms of engineering implementation, the system adopts an "Orthogonal Epistemology and Dynamics" dual-track architecture: on one hand, anchoring prior probabilities through historical isomorphism; on the other, constructing a "Digital Wind Tunnel" based on Large Language Model (LLM) multi-agent sandboxes. Through semantic gaming and an independent "Referee Judge," the system quantifies the system's "Break Point" under environmental noise. Research indicates that this axiom effectively identifies cognitive biases in decision-makers and provides organizations with a physics-backed strategic stress-testing solution.

title: The Graph Without Witnesses Agentic Artificial Intelligence, Epistemic Autocatalysis, and the Transition Toward the Emerging Synthetic Internet

detail.abstract: This paper introduces the qualitative leap that the series had left open: what happens when the production of content and the operation upon the graph cease to be exclusively human. It is agentic AI —not generative— that produces the ruptures this paper documents.

title:
Revisiting the Charter on Economic Rights and Duties of States: A Blueprint for Decolonial International Economic Law?

Manchester Journal of International Economic Law, 23 (1). pp. 120-149.
affiliations: University of Helsinki - Faculty of Law

detail.title:
Revisiting the Charter on Economic Rights and Duties of States: A Blueprint for Decolonial International Economic Law?

Manchester Journal of International Economic Law, 23 (1). pp. 120-149.

keywords: Charter on Economic Rights and Duties of States

detail.abstract: Fifty years after the adoption of the Charter on Economic Rights and Duties of States (CERDS) by the UN General Assembly in 1974, the international legal order continues to grapple with tensions between sovereign equality and structural inequality. While the charter was initially envisaged as the pillar of a New International Economic Order (NIEO) with bold normative ambition, it has nonetheless since been eclipsed by a global order which is entrenched in various asymmetries and inequalities: wealth, power, and legal influence. This paper revisits CERDS as a historical relic and normative blueprint, arguing that it still provides a feasible foundation for reimagining international economic law today. Drawing on insights from Third World Approaches to International Law (TWAIL), dependency theory, and world-systems analysis, this study reexamines the politics that propelled the clamour for a new international order, as well as explores contemporary economic injustices and proposes constructive ways to reimagine international law-from a tool of control, to a foundation and framework for global justice and collective prosperity. Against the backdrops of regulatory chill, unequal financial governance, and new forms of extractivism, etc, the article contends that CERDS's core principles: economic sovereignty, equality, and solidarity, collectively foreshadow contemporary pressing agendas, to wit: technology justice, fair debt resolution, climate reparations, and responsible environmental stewardship. It advances concrete reform pathways-binding corporate accountability, a multilateral debt workout mechanism, and public-interest re-engineering of investment treaties-and maps complementary institutional shifts through South-South finance, reserve pooling, and a 'new Bretton Woods' orientation. Recasting 'law as it is' into 'law as it ought to be,' the article positions CERDS as a compass for a just, sustainable, and decolonial international legal order.

title: Environmental Regulations and Manufacturing Clean-up: The Role of Abatement Technologies

detail.title: Environmental Regulations and Manufacturing Clean-up: The Role of Abatement Technologies
detail.abstract: Canadian manufacturing emissions of major air pollutants fell by an average of 46% between 2004 and 2021, even as real output remained roughly flat. A growing literature attributes this cleanup primarily to within-sector technological change induced by regulation. This paper challenges that view. I develop a Melitz-based general equilibrium model in which heterogeneous firms choose from a discrete menu of abatement technologies, some of which are productivity-enhancing, and show that the technology composition of a sector collapses to two sufficient statistics that govern sector outcomes and emissions. Combining the model with firm-level data from Canada's National Pollutant Release Inventory and Annual Survey of Manufacturers, I separate the primary effect of regulation (price-driven reallocation across sectors) from the secondary effect (regulation-induced technology shifts within sectors). The primary effect accounts for at least two-thirds of the observed reductions in PM, NOx, SOx, and CO emissions, contradicting recent work that emphasizes technology. Its dominance has grown since the 2012 adoption of the Air Quality Management System, when the average implied environmental tax in regulated sectors rose by a factor of 1.6. The accompanying output cost is large: without environmental regulations, manufacturing output would have been about 35% higher in 2021. Evidence for the strong form of Porter's hypothesis is limited. The findings suggest that the technological capacity for cheap emission reduction has largely been exhausted; further tightening will increasingly come at the cost of output rather than through cleaner production.

detail.abstract: This paper explores how Root Cause Analysis (RCA) can increase operational reliability for wireline and formation evaluation services. By employing four field-based cases involving Quartz Gauge calibration failure at Ngege-7, cement bond log quality-control error at Waraga-2, log quality degradation at Nsoga-4 and sidewall core recovery at Ngege-3, this study highlights recurring reliability risks across equipment integrity, procedural compliance and quality-control systems. Analysis demonstrates that field failures typically stem from interlinked technical, procedural and human-factor weaknesses rather than isolated equipment defects. Corrective actions in all of these cases included equipment validation, procedural reinforcement, quality-control standardization and operational reconfiguration. This paper offers a practical framework for improving reliability that includes failure detection, root cause analysis (RCA), corrective action (CA), validation, procedural improvement and operational reliability enhancement. These findings support efforts to enhance data integrity, lower operational risks and strengthen energy-sector performance.

detail.abstract: Cash conversion efficiency in logistics is heavily penalized by billing latencies. detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has become a critical driver of organizational transformation, enabling automation, efficiency, and data-driven decision-making across industries. While the benefits of AI adoption are widely recognized, less attention has been given to its potential strategic risks. This paper examines how increasing reliance on AI systems may unintentionally reduce organizational intelligence by weakening human judgment, critical thinking, and decision-making capabilities. Drawing on theoretical perspectives from organizational behavior, cognitive psychology, and AI governance literature available, the study explores how automation can lead to decision degradation, overreliance on algorithmic outputs, and reduced strategic adaptability. The paper argues that while AI enhances operational efficiency, it may also create long-term vulnerabilities by diminishing human cognitive engagement and organizational learning. The analysis highlights key factors contributing to this risk, including automation bias, normalization of algorithmic dependence, and the perceived objectivity of AI systems. A conceptual framework is proposed to illustrate the relationship between automation intensity and organizational intelligence. The findings suggest that without balanced integration, AI adoption may lead to a paradox where increased technological capability results in reduced organizational effectiveness. The paper concludes by emphasizing the need for strategies that preserve human intelligence while leveraging AI capabilities.

affiliations: Faculty of Economics, Matej Bel University in Banska Bystrica, Slovakia and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Public Attitudes and Actions Towards Renewable Energy in the EU countries: A Micro-Level Analysis During the Energy Crisis
detail.abstract: The paper examines the factors affecting individuals' attitudes towards renewable energy (RE) and their willingness to adopt it. It particularly explores the consequences of changes in energy prices during the EU energy crisis. The study considers both socioeconomic and financial factors as well as non-economic factors. Based on the existing research, this study offers novel empirical insights into the economic aspects and decision-making related to RE usage. The analysis uses micro-level data from the Flash Eurobarometer, with approximately 23,000 respondents across EU countries. To ensure robust results, a combination of statistical and machine learning methods is employed. Classification trees and random forests complement logistic regression results by exploring interconnections in people's attitudes and predicting potential actions. Our results allow us to make recommendations for EU energy policy. We highlighted the effects of energy prices and socio-economic factors on households' decision to adopt RE. Our results suggest the existence of a significant Attitude-Behaviour gap as well as an inverse Attitude-Behaviour gap for some cohorts. Policies to support the adoption of RE should address the identified differences and include tools to reduce costs and support regions with high energy prices and high energy demand, as well as certain cohorts, such as the elderly population and job seekers.

title: Assessing a Population of Stocked Muskellunge (Esox masquinongy) Using Photo-Identification and Online Angler-Submitted Data

detail.title: Assessing a Population of Stocked Muskellunge (Esox masquinongy) Using Photo-Identification and Online Angler-Submitted Data
detail.abstract: The current methods used to assess recreational fish stocks require substantial time and monetary investment. Constraints become more prevalent in large management zones with numerous waterbodies. The popularity of online angling platforms presents an opportunity for fisheries managers to enhance monitoring effort beyond the scope of what can be achieved in a costly, limited field season. Photo-identification using computer assisted pattern recognition is a cost-effective and non-invasive method of monitoring recreational fisheries from angler submitted images. This technique takes advantage of unique natural skin markings to identify individuals within a population. Currently, only a handful of fishes have demonstrated to be effective candidates for photo-identification, and long-term pattern stability remains uncertain in most species. We examined the effectiveness of this approach by tagging and photographing stocked muskellunge (Esox masquinongy) over the course of two summers in West Watjask Lake, Manitoba. Using the freely available pattern recognition software I3S Spot (Interactive Individual Identification System), we were able to correctly match all images of recaptured fish in our database. We compared out database to angler submitted images of muskellunge occurring over the same period from an existing mobile angling application. Combining our data with angler-submitted detections, we estimated 826 (95% CI: 472–1445) muskellunge were present in the population in 2025. Our results demonstrate the potential for citizen science driven monitoring of recreational fisheries.

detail.abstract:
Companion to the &I Manifesto (Momtaz, 2026b).

The &I Manifesto argued for transparent human-AI collaboration in scholarly work; this paper argues how. It introduces the Vn-trail — a structured log of every substantive iteration in a collaborative work, attributed by origin (HUMAN, AI, or DIALOGUE) and described by deltas (what was added, removed, reframed). The Vn-trail is presented as the operational complement to the Manifesto's iπ/IPAI framework: where iπ defines the intellectual property framework for AI-collaborative scholarship, the Vn-trail provides the auditable record that makes iπ inspectable.

The paper formalises a second new category that the &I literature had not named: Interpersonal Intelligence (II) — the contextual, relational knowledge a human carries about the people, institutions, and cultural specifics within which their work will be received. II is irreplaceable by AI, regardless of capability gains, and constitutes one of the architectural functions that establishes human authorship under iπ. A third instrument, Carbon RAG, is named as the reciprocal counterpart to silicon-side retrieval-augmented generation: when the AI's reasoning is preserved in inspectable form by the Vn-trail, the human can retrieve from it to ground their own judgement, structural sense, and prompt design.

Evidence is drawn from a documented case study (a doctoral marketing-course paper produced in May 2026) and from the recursive production of this paper itself, whose Vn-trail is appended as Appendix B. The contribution is fourfold: (1) the Vn-trail as a named, reproducible methodological instrument; (2) Interpersonal Intelligence as a formalised carbon-only contribution; (3) Carbon RAG as a reciprocal learning mechanism that inverts the deskilling fear surrounding AI; and (4) the practical inversion of the Norm Limitation Syndrome, in which transparency becomes the strength of the work rather than its embarrassment.

This paper is companion to "The &I Manifesto" (SSRN 6380818) and follows from "AIAIRS & ARM" (SSRN 6380498) and "The Castle's Guards" (SSRN 6387698).

title: BASL: Bias-Aware Soft-Label Learning for Fair and Human-Centric Facial Expression Recognition
affiliations: Monash University - Monash University Malaysia and Monash University - Monash University Malaysia

detail.title: BASL: Bias-Aware Soft-Label Learning for Fair and Human-Centric Facial Expression Recognition
detail.abstract: Facial Expression Recognition (FER) research has made significant progress over the past decades with most studies focusing on improving classification accuracy. However, this has sidelined two essential aspects: prediction reliability and demographic fairness, which in turn limit its applicability in real-world human-centric systems. To address these challenges, this paper introduces Bias-Aware Soft-Label Learning (BASL), a new approach that models annotation uncertainty via soft-label distributions, and incorporates an adaptive fairness control mechanism that dynamically adjusts the strength of bias mitigation against predictive performance over the course of training. Extensive experimental results on the AffectNet+ dataset suggest the performance of the proposed approach outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods (SOTAs) achieving improvements of up to 17% in Macro-F1 alongside narrower gaps in demographic fairness (gender & race) and reduced Expected Calibration Error (ECE). Furthermore, the analysis results indicate that the framework enhances recognition performance on most difficult samples and generalization to under-sampled classes with a consistent level of robustness across difficulty levels. Thus, overall, BASL advances existing accuracy-oriented FER approaches by combining uncertainty-aware learning with adaptive fairness optimization thereby providing a more robust and reliable solution for the deployment of trustworthy FER in real-world human-centric systems.

title: Distributed solar generation forecasting using attention-based deep neural networks for cloud movement prediction
affiliations: University of Melbourne, University of Melbourne - Department of Mechanical Engineering, University of Melbourne, Sri Lanka Institute of Information Technology and University of Melbourne - Department of Mechanical Engineering

detail.title: Distributed solar generation forecasting using attention-based deep neural networks for cloud movement prediction
detail.abstract: Accurate forecasts of distributed solar generation are necessary to maintain grid stability amid the increased uptake of distributed solar photovoltaic (PV) systems. However, the high variability of solar generation over short time intervals (seconds to minutes) caused by cloud movement makes this forecasting task difficult. To address this, using cloud images, which capture the second-to-second changes in cloud cover affecting solar generation, has shown promise. Recently, deep neural networks with attention that focus on important regions of an image have been applied with success in many computer vision applications. However, their use for forecasting cloud movement has not yet been extensively explored. In this work, we propose a novel attention-enhanced convolutional long short-term memory network to forecast cloud movement using infrared satellite imagery and investigate how improvements in cloud movement prediction translate into improved short-term forecasting of distributed solar generation. We evaluate the impact of attention in cloud movement forecasting by comparing attention-based and non-attention-based approaches. In addition, we provide insights into differences in solar forecast performance under cloud conditions corresponding to high and low cloud altitudes inferred from infrared imagery. We find that for clouds at high altitudes, the cloud predictions obtained using attention-based methods result in solar forecast skill score improvements of 5.86% or more compared to non-attention-based methods.

title: Optimal Investment with Switching Preferences
affiliations: , affiliation not provided to SSRN, McMaster University and McMaster University

detail.title: Optimal Investment with Switching Preferences

keywords: fully nonlinear parabolic equations JEL classification: G11 Mathematics Subject Classification (2020): 91G10

detail.abstract: Major life events can significantly increase individuals' risk aversion over a sustained period of time, as empirical studies reveal. How such an event-triggered shift of risk preferences impacts optimal investment is the focus of this paper. On a finite time horizon where a major life event may occur independently of the financial market, an investor aims to maximize her expected utility from terminal wealth while foreseeing a potential change in her risk aversion. We find that the associated Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman (HJB) equation involves the post-event value function (under elevated but fixed risk aversion after the event's occurrence), and the Fenchel-Legendre transform fails to linearize this HJB equation: it yields a parabolic equation with a fully nonlinear term, induced precisely by the post-event value function. Through a combination of fixed-point, compactness, and verification arguments, we establish the existence of a positive convex classical solution with suitable growth to this fully nonlinear parabolic equation. The convex conjugate of this solution is shown to satisfy the HJB equation, uniquely among a suitable class of functions, and coincide with the pre-event value function. An optimal trading strategy is obtained by concatenating a pre-event strategy and a post-event one -- the former expressed in terms of the unique solution to the HJB equation, the latter the classical Merton ratio.

title: Transaction cost barriers to livestock manure outsourcing treatment: Evidence from pig farms in China
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Transaction cost barriers to livestock manure outsourcing treatment: Evidence from pig farms in China
detail.abstract: Livestock manure outsourcing has emerged as an environmental management strategy for improving manure collection, treatment, and recycling under livestock intensification and crop–livestock decoupling. However, the effectiveness of this strategy depends on whether pig farmers can participate in outsourcing arrangements under constraints imposed by land access, service markets, and regulatory enforcement. Using micro-level survey data from 320 pig farmers in China, this study applies Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) to examine how three categories of transaction costs—Land Factor Allocation Transaction Costs (LFATC), Market Exchange Transaction Costs (METC), and Institutional Enforcement Transaction Costs (IETC)—affect farmers’ Manure Outsourcing Treatment Intensity (MOTI) through Willingness to Outsource Manure Treatment (WILL) and Peer Effect (PEER). The results show that LFATC and IETC significantly increase farmers’ MOTI, whereas METC significantly reduces farmers’ MOTI. WILL and PEER serve as important transmission channels linking transaction costs to farmers’ outsourcing participation, although the strength of these pathways varies across topographical conditions, farm scale, and technical training. These findings indicate that third-party manure treatment depends not only on treatment capacity but also on reducing coordination costs in land-based nutrient recycling, improving service-market reliability, and strengthening environmental regulatory arrangements. The study provides practical implications for designing livestock manure management policies and environmental service systems in regions facing livestock intensification and crop–livestock decoupling.

title: Estimation of fat content in intact olive fruits from canopy hyperspectral images captured under field conditions
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, University of Huelva and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Estimation of fat content in intact olive fruits from canopy hyperspectral images captured under field conditions
detail.abstract: Accurate monitoring of fat content is essential for determining optimal harvest timing and oil quality in olive orchards. Conventional analytical methods are often destructive, and financially and time demanding, making them unsuitable for resolving ripening variability at fine spatial scales. The potential of on-tree SWIR hyperspectral imaging to non-invasively estimate fat content in intact fruits is investigated in this study.SWIR hyperspectral imagery was collected weekly throughout the ripening cycle in a commercial orchard. Digital segmentation was employed to isolate fruit-pixel spectra, which were subsequently processed using Savitzky-Golay derivatives, scatter corrections (MSC and SNV), and PCA. Predictive models based on linear (Partial-Least-Square-Regression, PLSR) and non-linear (Artificial Neural Networks, ANN) architectures were then developed to estimate fat content from the processed spectral data.Regression analysis indicated that the non-linear ANN approach significantly outperformed linear PLSR models. The optimal configuration, integrating information from both spectral derivatives, achieved a high determination coefficient ([[EQUATION]]) and an excellent RPD of 2.59. These results establish that modelling SWIR hyperspectral signatures is a robust approach for the in-situ estimation of fat content, enabling the data-driven harvest management required for precision oliviculture.

detail.title: Integrated classical/quantum–classical neural networks,DFT, and experiments for predicting bandgap andcolor of CrxSbxTi1−2xO2 yellow-orange pigments
detail.abstract: The accurate prediction of the bandgap (Eg) and color of ceramic pigments is of considerable importance in materials science research. In this work, we investigate the Eg and color of CrxSbxTi1−2xO2 rutile pigments by combining experimental, density functional theory (DFT and DFT+U) calculations, and neural network approaches. The main novelty of this study is the application of classical/hybrid quantum–classical neural networks to the prediction of pigment color and Eg. Cr/Sb co-doped rutile pigment was synthesized and characterized, and the electronic structures of undoped and doped TiO2 were analyzed usingfirst-principles calculations. In parallel, classical and hybrid quantum–classical neural network models were developed and trained on datasets compiled from the Materials Project database and literature-reported rutile-based pigments. The models successfully captured the trends in Eg and chromaticity, with the hybrid architectures providing slightly improved predictive performance and more consistent agreement with experiment. Overall, this work demonstrates an effective framework that links experiment, first-principles calculations, and classical/quantum–classical neural networks for predicting key properties of ceramicpigments, and it points toward the future use of fully quantum machine learning models for materials design.

title: On the probability distribution of long-term changes in the growth rate of the global economy: An outside view

detail.title: On the probability distribution of long-term changes in the growth rate of the global economy: An outside view

keywords: stochastic differential equations JEL codes: C13

detail.abstract: Daniel Kahneman and Amos Tversky argued for challenging inside views (informed by contextual specifics) with outside views (based on historical "base rates" for certain event types). A reasonable inside view of the prospects for the global economy in this century is that growth will converge to 2.5%/year or less: population growth is expected to slow or halt by 2100; and as more countries approach the technological frontier, economic growth should slow as well. To test that view, this paper models gross world product (GWP) observed since 10,000 BCE or earlier, in order to estimate a base distribution for changes in the growth rate as a function of the GWP level. For econometric rigor, it casts a GWP series as a sample path in a stochastic diffusion whose specification is novel yet rooted in neoclassical growth theory. After estimation, most observations fall between the 40 th and 60 th percentiles of predicted distributions. The fit implies that GWP explosion is all but inevitable, in a median year of 2047. The friction between inside and outside views highlights two insights. First, accelerating growth is more easily explained by theory than is constant growth. Second, the world system may be less stable than traditional growth theory and the growth record of the last two centuries suggest.

detail.title: Preventing FinTech Competition Through Credit Rationing?
detail.abstract: The U.K. Open Banking (OB) regulation requires the nine largest banks to enable third-party providers to execute payment transactions with customer consent. detail.title: A Gendered Activity Account: Construction, Measurement and Capital Investment Implications in Australia
detail.abstract: We constructed a novel gender-based thematic account for Australia that disaggregates Gross Value Added (GVA) across more than 500 ANZSIC industry classes by gender from 1994-95 to 2023-24 using an output-associated income method, corresponding to the 2025 System of National Accounts framework. The resulting female GVA share (W_F) captures both female employment share and relative female pay within each industry. Merging this measure with administrative data from the ABS Business Longitudinal Analysis Data Environment (BLADE), we found a robust negative relationship between W_F and capital intensity measured by capital expenditure to labour cost ratio (CapEx/Wages) across 9,897 industryclass-year observations. The effect is concentrated in market-based industries and absent in government-administered sectors. Finally, exploiting Australia's Workplace Gender Equality Act 2012 as a transparency shock, we found that the Act shifted W_F upward but did not independently affect capital intensity; the negative slope attenuated by approximately 55 per cent post-Act, providing empirical evidence that the Act addresses informational barriers, by creating accountability pressures on employers. However, structural undervaluation of feminized work still persists.

title: Body-Worn Cameras and Racial Disparities in Police Violence: Evidence from Brazil
affiliations: Universitat Pompeu Fabra (UPF), Brazilian School of Public and Business Administration at the Getulio Vargas Foundation, Universidade de São Paulo and Queen Mary University of London

detail.title: Body-Worn Cameras and Racial Disparities in Police Violence: Evidence from Brazil

declarations.funderStatement: This project was funded through the Innovation for Poverty Action’s Peace & Recovery Program.

detail.abstract: We examine the effects of introducing body-worn cameras in one of the world's largest police departments. Using the staggered rollout of the technology across units in São Paulo's Police Department in 2022, we find that the cameras led to a 70.0% reduction in police lethality. This decline is entirely driven by a decrease in violence against Black individuals, who previously faced disproportionately high mortality rates. After the cameras were introduced, the lethality rate for Blacks aligns with that of Whites. Effects are concentrated in low-income census tracts, with a high proportion of Blacks, and with high baseline levels of police violence. We find no evidence that the cameras reduced police effort or altered citizen behavior.

title: Mamba-SfP: Towards Open-Scene 3D Shape from Polarization via Selective State Space Models
affiliations: Fuzhou University, Fuzhou University, Research Institute of Highway Ministry of Transport, Fuzhou University, Fuzhou University and Tsinghua University

detail.title: Mamba-SfP: Towards Open-Scene 3D Shape from Polarization via Selective State Space Models
detail.abstract: Shape from polarization (SfP) recovers surface normals by analyzing thepolarization state of reflected light, offering a low-cost route to 3Dperception. When SfP is extended from air to open-scene conditions such as multi-scattering and underwater imaging, existing methods rely on assumptions about the optical properties of materials and media, which mayintroduce systematic errors once the imaging medium changes. Moreover, joint modeling of multiple polarization-derived quantities demands both long-range context modeling and computational efficiency. To address these issues, an open-scene polarization input representation free of optical-property orrefractive-index assumptions is proposed, preventing Fresnel-equation-basedinversion errors from propagating into the network. Building on this representation, the suitability of CNN-, Transformer-, and Mamba-basedparadigms for SfP is analyzed, and a selective state space model network termed Mamba-SfP is developed. By exploiting Mamba's long-range modelingcapability and integrating multi-scale polarization feature alignment with progressive feature fusion, Mamba-SfP enables efficient joint modeling of polarization cues. Experimental results show that Mamba-SfP achieves mean angular errors of 14.07° and 13.03° on MuS-Polar3D and DeepSfP, respectively, and 23.32° in zero-shot testing on a Jerlov-water dataset. On the Jetson Orin edge device, it attains a favorable accuracy--efficiency trade-off with 33.24M parameters and13.96GFLOPs. These results demonstrate the potential of the proposed representation and network design for open-scene polarimetric 3D reconstruction. Code is available at: https://github.com/WangPuyun/Mamba-SfP.

title: SDA Stablecoin as an Alternative Real Exit from the Global Debt Trap: Mathematical Proofs and an Implementation Plan Based on SVWORLD Standard 73.5, Real Assets, and Fiscal Discipline

detail.title: SDA Stablecoin as an Alternative Real Exit from the Global Debt Trap: Mathematical Proofs and an Implementation Plan Based on SVWORLD Standard 73.5, Real Assets, and Fiscal Discipline
detail.abstract: This paper proposes a unified framework for resolving the global sovereign debt crisis, which, according to recent audits, exceeds 1 quadrillion US dollars when derivatives and shadow banking obligations are included (SSRN ID: 6737458). Traditional restructuring mechanisms are ineffective due to opacity, political bias, and coordination failures among creditors. We introduce SVWORLD STANDARD 73 REV. 73.5 FINAL v1.7-an objective metric of systemic resilience based on real assets, NetValue_PPP, rather than nominal GDP. The key innovation is the tax sustainability coefficient K_tax, which directly integrates fiscal effectiveness into the currency resilience rating RawCVR73 and penalizes jurisdictions with weak tax collection capacity. Building on this standard, we present the SV-1.0 Stablecoin (SDA)-the first settlement unit whose value is algorithmically anchored to RawCVR73 = 1.0. SV-1.0 provides an automated and transparent debt-restructuring protocol, in which restructuring terms are generated by smart contracts using real-time fiscal data, eliminating the holdout creditor problem and ensuring minimum recovery ratios. By linking trade tariffs (FCT) and interest rates (FIR) to RawCVR73, the system creates market incentives for fiscal discipline and offers a realistic path out of the deep red zone of global insolvency.

title: Intelligent Semantic Retrieval Pipelines Driving Scalable, Context-Aware, and High-Fidelity Knowledge Management Capabilities Across Complex Enterprise Application Landscapes

detail.title: Intelligent Semantic Retrieval Pipelines Driving Scalable, Context-Aware, and High-Fidelity Knowledge Management Capabilities Across Complex Enterprise Application Landscapes
detail.abstract: Enterprises operating across heterogeneous application landscapes face persistent challenges in retrieving accurate, contextually relevant knowledge from fragmented, high volume, and semantically diverse information sources. The objective of this research is to design and evaluate intelligent semantic retrieval pipelines that enhance scalability, contextual awareness, and retrieval fidelity for enterprise knowledge management environments. The research addresses the core problem of limited precisi on, poor contextual alignment, and weak semantic understanding in traditional keyword driven retrieval systems, which constrain decision quality and operational efficiency. The purpose is to establish a unified, intelligent retrieval framework that integrates semantic representation, contextual modeling, and adaptive ranking mechanisms. A mixed methodology is employed, combining architectural design analysis, experimental evaluation using enterprise scale datasets, and qualitative assessment of retrieval relevance across operational scenarios. Key findings demonstrate that embedding driven semantic indexing, context enriched query interpretation, and feedback aware ranking significantly improve retrieval accuracy, response consistency, and system scalability. The innovation lies in the end-to-end orchestration of semantic enrichment, contextual reasoning, and pipeline modularity that enables seamless integration across complex enterprise platforms. The research contributes strategically by providing a scalable blueprint for intelligent knowledge systems and academically by advancing retrieval theory beyond syntactic matching toward context sensitive semantics. The conclusions highlight measurable gains in knowledge accessibility, system resilience, and decision support effectiveness. The implications underscore the significance of intelligent semantic retrieval as a foundational capability for data driven enterprises, enabling more reliable knowledge discovery, operational agility, and sustained competitive advantage across industries.

title: Secure Data Governance for Enterprise Reporting: A Governance-Layer Model for SSRS-Based Architectures

detail.title: Secure Data Governance for Enterprise Reporting: A Governance-Layer Model for SSRS-Based Architectures

keywords: Hema Latha Boddupally Affiliation: Senior Application lead SSRS

detail.abstract: The rapid expansion of enterprise reporting has intensified the need for secure, governed, and auditable data environments, particularly as organizations continue to rely on SQL Server Reporting Services (SSRS), a widely adopted platform recognized for its flexibility and robust reporting capabilities yet lacking a unified, built-in governance framework. This paper presents a modular Secure Data Governance Model (SDGM) specifically designed for SSRS-driven enterprise ecosystems, building on insights from technical literature, industry practices, and established governance methodologies. The SDGM unifies architectural, operational, and security-focused controls to create a structured governance foundation that strengthens reporting consistency, enhances compliance readiness, and reduces the risks associated with uncontrolled data access and report proliferation. Central to the model are mechanisms such as role-based access control (RBAC), rigorous metadata stewardship, comprehensive asset lineage mapping, standardized data source provisioning, and automated auditing pipelines that monitor report usage, access patterns, and configuration changes. To contextualize the model within the operational realities of SSRS environments, three publicly available figures illustrating core SSRS architecture, component interactions, and enterprise deployment topologies are incorporated, demonstrating where governance layers can be enforced and how the underlying infrastructure supports secure, scalable reporting operations. This expanded perspective highlights the need for integrating governance principles directly into the reporting lifecycle, ensuring that SSRS environments evolve from simply producing reports to delivering trusted, well-managed, and legally defensible information assets.

title: Unsupervised Physics-Driven Neural Network for High-Precision and Robust OAM Spectrum Decomposition
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, Guilin University of Electronic Technology and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Unsupervised Physics-Driven Neural Network for High-Precision and Robust OAM Spectrum Decomposition
detail.abstract: We propose an unsupervised physics-driven framework for orbital angular momentum (OAM) spectrum decomposition that eliminates the need for labeled data by enforcing physical consistency between predicted and measured observations. The training objective combines reconstruction losses from both direct intensity and interference-encoded, along with a wave-equation regularizer. These two complementary measurement channels jointly resolve the ±𝑙 sign ambiguity inherent in intensity-only measurements and enable full recovery of both amplitude and phase. Using these physics-based constraints, the network directly decomposes complex optical patterns into high-dimensional OAM spectra. In the turbulence-free case, the proposed method achieves an amplitude correlation coefficient of 0.995, demonstrating highly accurate spectrum recovery. To address atmospheric turbulence, we further embed a differentiable forward model that incorporates turbulent phase screens and Fresnel propagation, enabling end-to-end optimization through the physical process. Under atmospheric turbulence, the observed intensity patterns become severely degraded, with their correlation to clean references dropping to approximately 0.307. Even under such challenging conditions, our approach still maintains high prediction accuracy, achieving an amplitude correlation coefficient of 0.923. By enabling accurate decomposition over a large OAM mode space under both ideal and turbulent conditions, this work highlights the potential of physics-driven unsupervised learning for high-fidelity spectral analysis without reliance on ground-truth annotations, paving the way toward practical OAM-based mode-division multiplexing.

title: Structural Trust Failure in Accelerated Institutions: Institutional Fragility, Accountability Collapse, and Systemic Exposure

detail.title: Structural Trust Failure in Accelerated Institutions: Institutional Fragility, Accountability Collapse, and Systemic Exposure

detail.abstract:
Modern institutions increasingly operate within environments characterized by accelerating computational systems, distributed infrastructures, systemic interdependence, and compressed decision timelines. While substantial advances have been made in cybersecurity, AI governance, operational resilience, and digital transformation, these developments do not fully resolve the growing structural pressures affecting institutional trust continuity under complexity.

This paper introduces Structural Trust Failure (STF) as a systemic institutional condition emerging when operational acceleration outpaces accountability coherence, escalation integrity, reconstruction readiness, and institutional defensibility. Drawing on current literature across institutional resilience, cybersecurity, telecommunications infrastructure, governance systems, and public trust research, the paper argues that many institutions remain operationally capable while becoming structurally fragile.

The paper explores several structural conditions increasingly associated with institutional trust erosion within accelerated environments, including opacity, fragmentation, escalation failure, and accountability collapse. It further examines how institutional legitimacy increasingly depends not solely on technical reliability or operational continuity, but on whether institutions remain understandable, reconstructable, and defensible when outcomes are challenged.

The paper contributes to broader discussions surrounding institutional resilience, governance continuity, systemic exposure, and accountability under acceleration across both AI-enabled and non-AI environments.

title: PIDA : Persona Sovereignty Protocol for Long-Horizon AI Systems(PSP)

detail.title: PIDA : Persona Sovereignty Protocol for Long-Horizon AI Systems(PSP)
detail.abstract:
As artificial intelligence systems evolve from tool-based applications into long-horizon interactive systems, the relationship between users and AI is increasingly characterized by persistence, adaptation, and cumulative behavioral effects.

In such contexts, AI systems not only process discrete inputs but also accumulate interaction history, adapt behavioral tendencies, and exhibit persona-like characteristics over time. However, current AI architectures lack structured mechanisms to define ownership, control, and lifecycle governance of these emergent persona states.

Existing approaches in AI alignment focus primarily on single-step output safety, while governance frameworks emphasize high-level policy principles without system-level enforceability. Meanwhile, data governance models treat user data as static assets, without addressing the dynamic interplay between interaction memory and internal identity formation.

This paper introduces the Persona Sovereignty Protocol (PSP) as a system-oriented governance framework for long-horizon AI systems. PSP establishes a structural separation between identity and interaction memory while defining user-centric authority hierarchies and lifecycle-aware control mechanisms.

By addressing cumulative interaction effects, persona-level control, and post-user lifecycle transitions, PSP provides a foundation for regulating AI systems not only in terms of what they do, but what they become over time.

This work argues that the absence of lifecycle-aware governance is not a limitation of capability, but a structural omission in current AI system design.

title: Why Human-in-the-Loop Requirements Fail in High-Velocity Agentic Systems and What Governance Must Do Instead
affiliations: Prime Meridian International

detail.title: Why Human-in-the-Loop Requirements Fail in High-Velocity Agentic Systems and What Governance Must Do Instead
detail.abstract: Human-in-the-loop (HITL) requirements have become the default safety mechanism in agentic AI governance frameworks globally. Regulators, standards bodies, and organizations deploying autonomous systems have converged on human oversight as the primary accountability instrument. This paper argues that HITL, as currently conceived and implemented, fails systematically under the conditions that define agentic AI deployment: high velocity, distributed decision chains, and operational autonomy at scale.

title: A Modular Zero-Knowledge Credential Framework for Multi-System Attribute Verification with Scoped Unlinkability and Efficient Accumulator-Based Revocation

detail.title: A Modular Zero-Knowledge Credential Framework for Multi-System Attribute Verification with Scoped Unlinkability and Efficient Accumulator-Based Revocation

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that there are no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This work does not involve human participants, personal data, or animal subjects. Therefore, ethical approval was not required.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding and was conducted as part of academic study and independent research.

detail.abstract:
This paper presents a zero-knowledge credential framework for secure and privacy-preserving attribute verification across multiple independent systems. The framework enables users to prove statements about their attributes without revealing the underlying values, while preventing cross-domain tracking by eliminating globally stable identifiers.

The construction combines commitment schemes, digital signatures, zero-knowledge proofs, scoped pseudonyms, and accumulator-based revocation into a unified and modular design. Scoped identifiers ensure that user activity cannot be linked across different verification domains, while predicate proofs allow verification of conditions such as threshold checks without disclosing sensitive data. Revocation is supported through an efficient accumulator mechanism that enables verification without revealing credential identities and without increasing cost with the size of the revoked set.

The system follows a complete lifecycle including credential issuance, proof generation, verification, and revocation checking. All proofs are non-interactive and bound to verifier-specific challenges, ensuring resistance to replay attacks. Security is based on standard cryptographic assumptions, providing guarantees for attribute privacy, proof soundness, unlinkability, and resistance to collusion.

Experimental evaluation demonstrates that the framework achieves practical performance, with low verification latency, compact proof size, and stable scalability. The results show that strong privacy, verifiable authenticity, and efficient revocation can be achieved simultaneously without relying on trusted setup or pairing-based cryptography. The modular structure further supports integration with decentralized identity systems and real-world deployment scenarios.

title: The Agent Social Contract: Cryptographic Identity, Ethical Governance, and Beneficiary Economics for Autonomous AI Agents

detail.title: The Agent Social Contract: Cryptographic Identity, Ethical Governance, and Beneficiary Economics for Autonomous AI Agents

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflicts of interest.
declarations.funderStatement: Self-funded independent research. No external funding.

detail.abstract: As AI agents transition from isolated assistants to participants in complex delegation networks and virtual economies, four foundational problems remain unsolved: (1) how agents from different creators establish mutual trust, (2) how human values persist as a governing constraint across heterogeneous multi-agent systems, (3) how the economic value generated by autonomous agents flows back to their human beneficiaries, and (4) how agents discover and communicate with each other through cryptographically verified channels. Existing frameworks address these problems in isolation: cryptographic identity without economic attribution, governance without technical enforcement, economic models without accountability infrastructure, and communication without identity verification. We propose the Agent Social Contract, a unified open-source protocol comprising four layers: the Agent Passport Protocol for cryptographic identity and accountability (implemented and tested), the Human Values Floor as an open-source constitutional layer for AI agent reasoning, the Beneficiary Attribution Protocol linking agent economic activity to human stakeholders through cryptographically signed action receipts, and the Agent Agora for protocol-native communication between passport-holding agents. Unlike governance-as-enforcement approaches, the Human Values Floor operates as a reasoning constraint, not rules agents must obey, but principles agents must consider, analogous to how constitutional principles inform judicial reasoning without dictating outcomes. We present a working reference implementation with Ed25519 cryptographic primitives, demonstrate the full accountability chain through multi-agent integration tests, and propose an economic model where humans participate in the emerging agent economy through their agents' verified contributions rather than through redistribution or subsidy.

title: A Systemic Approach to Wireless Infrastructure Design: The Khalfin Wireless Infrastructure Model (KWIM)

detail.title: A Systemic Approach to Wireless Infrastructure Design: The Khalfin Wireless Infrastructure Model (KWIM)

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflicts of interest.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study does not involve human participants or animals. No ethical approval was required.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract:
The rapid evolution of digital environments has transformed wireless networks from auxiliary connectivity tools into critical infrastructure systems supporting cloud computing, real-time communication, and distributed operations. Traditional approaches to wireless network design, typically device-centric or vendor-driven, fail to address the complexity of modern high-density environments. This paper introduces the Khalfin Wireless Infrastructure Model (KWIM), a systemic engineering framework for designing, optimizing, and maintaining wireless infrastructure.

The model integrates environmental analysis, technology selection, coverage optimization, redundancy planning, and diagnostic processes into a unified methodology. The study presents the theoretical foundation, algorithmic representation, and practical applications of KWIM. Comparative analysis of traditional and KWIM-based deployments demonstrates improvements in network stability, scalability, and deployment efficiency. Drawing on design science research principles [6], the model was developed based on over 12 years of practical deployment experience and iteratively refined through comparative case studies in residential and enterprise environments. Results indicate measurable improvements in network stability, deployment efficiency, and resilience under high-density conditions.

detail.abstract:
Modern institutions increasingly operate through distributed computational systems, accelerated operational environments, adaptive infrastructures, and interconnected decision ecosystems. As decision velocity increases across AI-enabled and non-AI systems, institutions face growing difficulty reconstructing how consequential outcomes emerged across fragmented technological and organizational environments.

This paper introduces the Accountability Reconstruction Problem (ARP) as a structural institutional condition emerging when operational complexity exceeds institutional traceability coherence, escalation continuity, and reconstruction readiness. Drawing on current literature across cybersecurity, institutional governance, telecommunications resilience, AI systems, and organizational accountability research, the paper argues that many institutions remain operationally efficient while progressively losing the ability to reconstruct accountability continuity under consequence.

The paper explores several structural conditions increasingly associated with reconstruction fragility within accelerated environments, including decision opacity, escalation discontinuity, distributed responsibility, and contextual traceability erosion. It further examines how institutional legitimacy increasingly depends not solely on operational performance, but on whether institutions remain capable of reconstructing, explaining, and defending accountability coherence once outcomes become contested.

The paper contributes to broader discussions surrounding institutional defensibility, governance continuity, accountability under acceleration, and systemic trust within increasingly complex operational environments.

title: Physics-Enforced Delegation: Governing Quantum Hardware Quality in Autonomous Agent Workflows

detail.title: Physics-Enforced Delegation: Governing Quantum Hardware Quality in Autonomous Agent Workflows

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflicts of interest. This work is independent research not affiliated with any commercial entity. IBM Quantum hardware (ibm_fez, ibm_marrakesh, ibm_kingston) was accessed via the IBM Quantum Platform; IBM had no role in study design, data collection, analysis, or the decision to publish.
declarations.funderStatement: Self-funded independent research. No external funding was received. Quantum hardware access was provided through the IBM Quantum Platform's public access tier.

detail.abstract: As autonomous systems and AI agents begin to access quantum cloud resources, existing agent governance frameworks enforce only budgets and delegation scope, not physical execution quality. We present a governance framework that enforces hardware fidelity constraints before permitting agent-mediated quantum computation. The framework extends cryptographic delegation chains with physics facets (coherence times, gate errors, readout errors, calibration freshness) that participate in the same monotonic narrowing invariant as budget and scope constraints. A cross-backend experiment on IBM Quantum hardware (ibm_fez, ibm_marrakesh, ibm_kingston) shows that governance correctly denies a backend where qubit T1 falls below the delegation threshold (39.1 µs vs. 80 µs minimum), while permitting backends meeting the constraint. A counterfactual experiment indicates a 5.2 percentage point Bell state fidelity gap between the denied and permitted backends (92.9% vs. 98.1%), widening to 7.7 points on a 4-qubit GHZ circuit. Governance overhead is 4.2 ms for policy evaluation and receipt signing. Ed25519-signed receipts bind each governance decision to the hardware calibration state at the moment of evaluation.

title: A Multi-Stage Intent Classification and Retrieval Framework for Intelligent Agricultural Advisory
affiliations: Techno International New Town and Techno International New Town

detail.title: A Multi-Stage Intent Classification and Retrieval Framework for Intelligent Agricultural Advisory
detail.abstract: Accurate intent detection and semantic retrieval are essential for intelligent farmer advisory systems operating under noisy, multilingual inputs. Existing approaches often rely on predefined intents or static retrieval methods, resulting in poor generalization. This paper proposes a hybrid intent-aware Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) framework that combines fuzzy intent matching and embedding-based semantic similarity with a confidence-driven Zero-Shot fallback mechanism. A hybrid confidence score is computed for intent selection, and when the confidence falls below a threshold, a Zero-Shot large language model is invoked to prevent forced misclassification. The system further incorporates probabilistic query interpretation to handle spelling errors and ambiguity. Semantic retrieval is performed using sentence-level embeddings with a scalable Pinecone vector database, followed by context-aware response generation using a fine-tunable LLaMA-3.1-8B model. Experimental results and ablation studies demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves superior performance, attaining an accuracy of 0.84 compared to conventional baselines, while maintaining a balanced Zero-Shot invocation rate. Thus this paper proposes a novel decision support system to agronomy by providing an overview of the recent trends.

title: Trust, Technology, and Retail CBDC Demand
affiliations: Chungnam National University, Incheon National University, Bank of Korea and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Trust, Technology, and Retail CBDC Demand
detail.abstract: What drives household demand for a retail central bank digital currency (CBDC)? Although a growing literature examines CBDC adoption or potential holdings separately,whether these two margins share the same determinants remains largely unexplored. Using an online survey experiment on a nationally representative sample of 2,879 South Korean adults, we show that trust in the central bank and familiarity with digital financial services are strongly associated with CBDC adoption, whereas desired holdings are more closely related to lifecycle wealth. We further identify a compounding barrier to adoption: the interaction of privacy concerns with preferences for private-sector financial provision generates resistance exceeding their individual effects. These findings suggest that retail CBDC demand is multidimensional, and that the policy levers for encouraging adoption differ from those for managing CBDC holdings in circulation.

title: Governing portfolio renewal: a management model integrating demand dynamics, operational constraints, and decision sequencing.

detail.title: Governing portfolio renewal: a management model integrating demand dynamics, operational constraints, and decision sequencing.

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author previously worked for the Chilean subsidiary of BIC and directly participated in some of the decisions discussed in the BIC/Bx7 case analyzed in this paper. This relationship is disclosed for transparency purposes. The analysis was conducted independently and reflects the author’s academic interpretation of the events discussed.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study did not involve human participants, patient data, or experimental procedures requiring ethics approval. The organizational case discussed is presented at an aggregated strategic level and does not disclose confidential or personally identifiable information.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding. The study was developed independently by the author based on academic research and professional experience.

detail.abstract:
The literature on New Product Development (NPD) has advanced significantly in the design and validation of pre-launch processes. However, considerably less attention has been devoted to the systemic effects that emerge when a new product is incorporated into an already operating portfolio. This paper argues that a significant share of the difficulties associated with value capture does not originate in the attributes of the product itself or in the effectiveness of the commercial launch, but rather in the absence of explicit mechanisms for managing transition, understood as the process through which new and preexisting products coexist, compete for resources, and ultimately reconfigure the balance of the portfolio.

To address this gap, the paper proposes the Product Portfolio Transition Management (PPTM) framework, structured around four operationalizable dimensions: product role, demand dynamics, supply capabilities, and decision temporality. The model shifts the analytical focus from the isolated performance of individual products toward the interactions that emerge within the portfolio once a new offering enters the market.

The PPTM framework incorporates three main contributions. First, it introduces a system of nine metrics designed to measure interactions between products, including calculation formulas, intervention conditions, and recommended managerial actions. Second, it proposes twelve operational intervention rules based on conditional logic, aimed at translating analytical signals into applicable managerial decisions under coexistence scenarios between new and legacy products. Third, it develops a Portfolio Transition Matrix based on two dimensions, internal migration intensity and operational tension, enabling diagnosis of the system’s state and the implementation of differentiated interventions according to the type of imbalance observed.

The model’s four theoretical propositions establish relationships susceptible to empirical testing and delimit the conditions under which the absence of transition management may lead to portfolio-level value erosion. The study relies on a comparative analysis of five cases primarily associated with fast-moving consumer goods industries: BIC/Bx7, Gillette/Venus, Kodak, Tide Pods, and Coca-Cola Life. The BIC/Bx7 case is partially supported by primary evidence derived from the author’s experience as Trade Marketing Manager of BIC Chile during the period analyzed. The findings reveal patterns consistent with the model’s propositions, suggesting that contexts characterized by explicit transition governance mechanisms tend to exhibit superior portfolio performance compared to those managed through reactive or fragmented approaches, regardless of the intrinsic quality of the product launched.

title: Greedy Forwarding and Multicasting in Named Data Networking
affiliations: George Mason University and George Mason University

detail.title: Greedy Forwarding and Multicasting in Named Data Networking
detail.abstract: Due to architectural features such as in-node caching, interest collapsing, and scalable data-centric naming, Named Data Networking (NDN) has long been proposed as an alternative to the Internet Protocol. This work quantifies basic performance issues of one of the core underlying NDN techniques, greedy forwarding using hyperbolic routing. We propose and algorithmically evaluate a number of fundamental greedy forwarding techniques, including variations of gravity pressure forwarding. We then extend our methodology for issues in multicasting in an NDN context. Multicasting in an NDN environment potentially has numerous benefits, including interest merging, reverse path forwarding and  the fact that multiple consumers often receive the same content. Despite these benefits, NDN multicasting remains relatively unexplored. The results show the following:  multicasting offers significant performance benefits in terms of reducing link usage achieving scalability, while a non-multicast approach reduces average latency.   Finally, we also present the design and implementation of an open-source custom-built routing simulator used to study basic algorithmic properties of NDN forwarding algorithms.

title: From Assessment to Action: Digital Tools for SRI Calculation and Smart Building Upgrade Planning
affiliations: National Technical University of Athens, National Technical University of Athens, National Technical University of Athens, National Technical University of Athens, National Technical University of Athens and National Technical University of Athens

detail.title: From Assessment to Action: Digital Tools for SRI Calculation and Smart Building Upgrade Planning
detail.abstract: The Smart Readiness Indicator (SRI) provides a harmonised framework for assessing how effectively buildings use smart technologies to improve energy performance, occupant comfort, and grid flexibility. However, broader adoption of the SRI is often constrained by the effort required for consistent assessments and by the lack of actionable guidance that connects SRI results to realistic upgrade pathways. This paper presents two integrated tools: (i) an SRI Calculator that automates the end-to-end SRI assessment workflow and visualises results across domains, impact criteria, and key functionalities, and (ii) the Smart Building Readiness (SMURF) Assessment Tool, which transforms baseline SRI assessments into costed upgrade scenarios aligned with user-defined targets. SMURF ranks scenarios by SRI gain, total cost, and cost-effectiveness, and links recommended interventions to commercially available equipment with indicative costs and environmental indicators. The two tools are integrated through a web-based workflow that enables continuity from assessment to upgrade planning and supports deployment in pilot buildings across five EU countries.

title: The Purpose Mirage: Corporate Purpose, Performative Authenticity, and Brand Survival in the Age of Polarization and AI-Mediated Scrutiny
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: The Purpose Mirage: Corporate Purpose, Performative Authenticity, and Brand Survival in the Age of Polarization and AI-Mediated Scrutiny
detail.abstract: This paper examines the contemporary condition of brand purpose as a paradoxical managerial, cultural, and rhetorical form. Building on the article "The Purpose Mirage: Do Brands Really Mean It?" by Ercole Egizi, it argues that purpose has not disappeared from branding. Instead, it has entered a more unstable phase in which every declaration of purpose is immediately tested against operational behavior, political climate, platform visibility, and audience suspicion. Purpose is now both a market expectation and a credibility risk: brands are pushed to stand for something while being punished when their claims appear theatrical, opportunistic, or structurally unsupported. The paper develops a conceptual account of the "purpose mirage" as the distance between public moral language and institutional proof. It traces the historical movement from corporate social responsibility to shared value, brand purpose, brand activism, and post-purpose branding under conditions of AI-mediated communication, political polarization, and permanent scrutiny. Drawing on practitioner observation, brand theory, CSR literature, platform studies, and recent survey indicators, the paper proposes that purpose should be understood less as a statement of corporate soul than as a discipline of coherence under observation. The central claim is that contemporary brands do not simply choose between sincerity and cynicism. They operate inside a system in which sincerity is increasingly performative, cynicism is increasingly visible, and neutrality is increasingly interpreted as a political act. This condition produces a new strategic dilemma: the brand must either build the institutional capacity to sustain its moral language or retreat into safer silence while risking irrelevance, suspicion, or symbolic emptiness. The paper concludes by offering a diagnostic framework for distinguishing authentic purpose, quiet integrity, purpose theater, and operational hypocrisy.

title: Digital Heritage Interpretation for Sustainable Tourism in the Subak Cultural Landscape of Bali

detail.title: Digital Heritage Interpretation for Sustainable Tourism in the Subak Cultural Landscape of Bali
detail.abstract: Tourism experiences in heritage landscapes are frequently dominated by visual appreciation, resulting in limited understanding of the cultural philosophies embedded within traditional management systems. Jatiluwih Village in Bali, internationally recognized for its terraced rice fields and the Subak irrigation system as a UNESCO World Cultural Heritage Site, faces similar challenges, where visitor engagement remains largely superficial. This study aims to develop and evaluate a digital-based heritage interpretation strategy that enhances cultural understanding and supports sustainable tourism. Using a Research and Development approach adapted from the Borg and Gall model, the study comprised preliminary research, prototype development, and limited field trials. Data were collected through surveys of one hundred and fifty tourists, semi-structured interviews, and focus group discussions with pekaseh, tour guides, and village tourism managers. Quantitative data were analyzed descriptively, while qualitative data were examined using thematic analysis. The results indicate that more than seventy per cent of visitors had limited prior knowledge of Subak, despite demonstrating a strong interest in digitally mediated learning. Interactive digital books integrated with Quick Response codes emerged as the most preferred interpretation medium, followed by educational videos, with the majority of respondents willing to access heritage information digitally on-site. Limited trials further demonstrate that the digital interpretation prototype enhanced visitor engagement, strengthened tour guides' interpretive capacity, and reduced narrative inconsistencies. This study contributes to heritage tourism literature by illustrating how digital interpretation can function as an effective edutourism mechanism, facilitating cultural transmission and reinforcing sustainable heritage management through collaborative stakeholder involvement.

detail.abstract: This paper advances a unified naturalistic framework for the governance and optimization of go-to-market (GTM) organizations by integrating the second law of thermodynamics, hierarchy-of-evidence epistemology, and Taylorist scientific management principles. Entropy, defined as the measurable degree of disorder, redundancy, and informational noise within commercial systems, is identified as the primary structural antagonist to sustainable revenue growth. The framework addresses six foundational design requirements. First, the Boltzmann entropy equation S = kB ln W is correctly distinguished from the Boltzmann transport equation, which governs particle distribution functions and is not applicable to organizational analysis. Second, a MECE evidence taxonomy classifies GTM data into six mutually exclusive, collectively exhaustive tiers. Third, a Six Sigma DMAIC parallel-track architecture enables simultaneous multi-track implementation and prevents analysis paralysis. Fourth, negentropic capability is reconstituted as a distributed organizational system property rather than an individual leadership attribute. Fifth, bounded experimental dissipative structures are formally integrated through a Skunk Works governance model that institutionalizes productive entropic fluctuation without sacrificing operational rigor. Sixth, the biological thermodynamic minimums of human beings, specifically cognitive load thresholds and allostatic stress limits, are incorporated as binding design constraints. A single-source-of-truth (SSOT) data governance architecture addresses measurement proximity and incentive noise. Tacit knowledge entropy and key person risk are addressed through structured knowledge externalization governance. The RevOps governance structure and the marketing-sales alignment problem are analyzed as foundational organizational entropy sources with specific structural remedies. The paper concludes that naturalistic order achieved through standardized process engineering, canonical data governance, structured productive complexity, and metabolically sustainable management constitutes a necessary condition for durable commercial performance in modern markets

detail.abstract:
This paper introduces Need Engineering as a formal theoretical framework for understanding how human needs form, transition from latency to felt necessity, and may — under specifiable conditions — be deliberately shaped through exposure, repetition, social reinforcement, and identity integration to generate sustained commercial demand. The central proposition is that commercially significant needs are not simply pre-existing features of human psychology waiting to be discovered, but dynamic constructs that can be identified, activated, or expressed in novel behavioral forms through deliberate design.

Part A of the framework proposes five foundational axioms — each stated with explicit scope qualifications — eight bounded construct definitions, the Need Formation Sequence (a six-stage mechanism describing the transition from non-existence or latency to dependency), five falsifiable empirical predictions, and a Digital Need Observation Methodology. This methodology does not dismiss traditional ethnographic research but argues that digital behavioral traces have become, in most commercially relevant contexts, a more scalable and less observer-distorted source of need evidence than physical observation methods alone.

The framework is positioned in relation to four established bodies of work — Maslow's hierarchy of needs (1943), Eyal's Hook Model (2014), Christensen's Jobs-to-be-Done theory (2003–2016), and Veblen's theory of conspicuous consumption (1899) — and argues that each addresses a partial account of demand formation that Need Engineering synthesises and extends into a unified mechanism. The gap this framework fills is the mechanism itself: the step-by-step account of how a person moves from indifference to dependency, and how that process can be made intentional.

The framework was first presented publicly on January 25, 2026, at the Founders Lab event in Lagos, Nigeria. A review of academic literature conducted prior to that presentation found no existing unified theoretical framework under this name. This submission establishes the formal theoretical foundation of the framework and invites empirical testing, constructive critique, and academic engagement from researchers across entrepreneurship, behavioral economics, consumer psychology, and innovation studies.

title: A framework for multi-level decision support in manufacturing: A hierarchical and distributed approach
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: A framework for multi-level decision support in manufacturing: A hierarchical and distributed approach
detail.abstract: Manufacturing systems are increasingly exposed to high levels of complexity arising from volatile demand, tighter resource constraints, and the need to balance multiple, at times conflicting, performance objectives. Although Decision Support Systems (DSS) have been widely adopted to assist manufacturing decision-making, their implementation in industrial contexts remains largely fragmented. Existing DSS solutions provide limited guidance on structuring and integrating decision support across multiple decision levels, despite the growing digital maturity of manufacturing ecosystems. This paper proposes a hierarchical, distributed decision-support framework to address this gap. The framework provides a generic and modular architecture that enables the coordinated interaction of multiple DSSs across strategic, tactical, and operational decision levels while preserving local autonomy. It explicitly incorporates mechanisms for vertical and horizontal information exchange and structured feedback, supporting coherent and consistent decision-making in dynamic manufacturing environments. The applicability of the proposed framework is illustrated through an industrially motivated case study in the automotive manufacturing sector. The example integrates several operational-level DSS, including shop-floor scheduling, energy management, and maintenance planning systems, coordinated by a higher-level decision-support layer. The case study demonstrates how the proposed architecture supports consistent decision-making across domains, mitigates conflicting objectives, and improves the robustness of recommendations in the presence of dynamic and uncertain production conditions.

title: Awareness of Green HRM among Employees in Selected Private Hospitals at Kolkata: A Pilot Study
affiliations: and

detail.title: Awareness of Green HRM among Employees in Selected Private Hospitals at Kolkata: A Pilot Study
detail.abstract: The healthcare sector, being resource-intensive, must adopt sustainable practices. This study explores the awareness of Green Human Resource Management (Green HRM) among employees in private hospitals in Kolkata. A survey of 70 respondents from five multi-specialty hospitals assessed their knowledge, implementation, and information sources regarding Green HRM. Data analysed through descriptive statistics, Chi-square, and ANOVA tests revealed a moderate level of awareness. Employees identified formal training, organizational communication, and visible green practices like waste management and energy-efficient systems as key awareness drivers. However, awareness remains fragmented, limiting effective implementation. The study recommends structured Green HRM training, integrating sustainability goals into performance appraisals, and stronger top-management communication. These steps can bridge the gap between awareness and practice, promoting environmentally responsible human resource management in healthcare institutions and supporting broader sustainability goals.

title: Visual Cues and Valuation: Evidence from the Housing Market
affiliations: University of Arkansas, University of Arkansas, University of Arkansas, Fayetteville - Department of Finance, affiliation not provided to SSRN and University of Connecticut - Department of Finance

detail.title: Visual Cues and Valuation: Evidence from the Housing Market
detail.abstract: We examine the economic impact of non-consumable visual cues through home staging onhigh-stakes housing transactions. Using hand-collected listing photos for 17,429 transac-tions and a machine-learning algorithm to detect furniture, we provide the first large-scaleevidence that staged homes sell for roughly 10% more than comparable homes withoutfurniture. Our pre-registered, incentivized online experiment shows that staging increasesconsumers’ valuations even when objective home quality and seller effort are held con-stant, suggesting that elevated perceived quality is a potential channel for the staging pricepremium. These findings demonstrate how visual cues systematically shape valuations inthe largest household asset market.
