detail.abstract:
This document is a concept index and terminology registry for the Tri-System Research Program (the AI Availability framework). It establishes priority dates and operational definitions for terminology developed in the program, including concepts that appear in the program's flagship paper (González Castro 2026d) and its three companion working papers (2026a, 2026b, 2026c), and concepts that are formally introduced for the first time in this index. The index complements rather than substitutes for the foundational papers; readers should consult the cited papers for full theoretical and empirical development.

Eight sections register thirty-two concepts grouped as follows: core constructs (AI Availability, AI Availability Paradox, AIAS, Share of Model, Tri-System Framework, Light Buyer Paradox); the five propositions of the framework plus one held-back proposition; mechanism specifications (three resistance channels, selective suspension, Default Reinforcement signature, discourse coherence); measurement infrastructure (AIAS six components, AI Presence, the Protocol v1.1, the CEP-anchored prompt set, designed-for-test methodology); boundary structure (the Category-Quadrant matrix, Identity Load Index, AI-Deference Disposition Instrument); operational tools (Brand AI-Availability Audit Protocol, Portfolio-Level Diagnostic, machine-legibility investment); adjacent candidate hypotheses; and three concepts introduced here for the first time (the Corporate Portfolio Layer, the Brand Valuation Extension, the Agentic Commerce Subprogramme). A cross-reference table maps every term to its paper of record and priority status.

The index is the priority-dated registry for the program's terminology. It is offered for citation, replication, and methodological extension by the marketing-science research community. Where a term appears in adjacent literature under similar wording but with a different operational definition, the operational definition specified here is the one to which this index claims priority — not the term in the abstract.

title: A Conceptual Enterprise Architecture for Explainable AI Governance in Digital Banking Ecosystems

detail.title: A Conceptual Enterprise Architecture for Explainable AI Governance in Digital Banking Ecosystems
detail.abstract:
Digital banking ecosystems are undergoing a fundamental transformation driven by artificial intelligence. Credit scoring, fraud detection, anti-money laundering monitoring, liquidity forecasting, and algorithmic trading are now largely AI-driven processes. Yet these systems remain governance-fragile. They make consequential decisions through opaque computational processes that are difficult to trace, audit, or justify to regulators and affected individuals. Existing research has focused heavily on improving predictive performance, leaving critical gaps in enterprise governance integration, explainability orchestration, and adaptive regulatory compliance.

This paper proposes a conceptual enterprise architecture including the XAI Governance Architecture for Digital Banking (XGADB), designed to address these gaps. Drawing on enterprise architecture theory, explainable AI frameworks, AI governance theory, financial risk governance models, and socio-technical systems thinking, the architecture integrates six interdependent layers: an AI decision layer, an explainability layer, a governance layer, compliance and regulatory layer, a semantic interoperability layer, and an enterprise integration layer.

The framework is accompanied by three visual models: a layered enterprise architecture diagram, a governance lifecycle model covering the full AI model lifecycle from design to retirement, and a stakeholder interaction framework mapping the governance relationships among regulators, data scientists, enterprise leadership, compliance teams, operational users, and deployed AI systems. The paper identifies four theoretical contributions, five industry implications, and six directions for future empirical research. The XGADB framework is positioned as a blueprint for financial institutions seeking to deploy AI systems that are not merely powerful, but accountable, transparent, and trustworthy by design.

title: The Expiration of the Legal Shield: WTO Flexibilities and the Adjudicative Vulnerability of Graduating LDCs

detail.title: The Expiration of the Legal Shield: WTO Flexibilities and the Adjudicative Vulnerability of Graduating LDCs
detail.abstract: Advancing beyond least developed status triggers a severe economic shock for vulnerable nations, widely recognised as the graduation cliff. The sudden removal of unilateral trade preferences and intellectual property waivers leaves fragile export sectors fully exposed to international competition. This study evaluates the legal mechanisms available to manage such an abrupt transition. While multilateral institutions offer temporary grace periods, these top-down interventions cannot prevent the inevitable rise in tariffs or the imposition of stricter rules of origin. Consequently, this paper argues that graduating states must abandon their historical reliance on passive, non-reciprocal support and proactively rebuild their trade architecture. Securing sustainable market access requires governments to negotiate reciprocal free trade agreements and qualify for conditional preference tiers. This strategic shift demands deep domestic regulatory harmonisation, forcing countries to align their internal labour standards and customs duties with the expectations of advanced trading partners. By embracing these rigorous legal commitments, transitioning economies can successfully integrate into the modern global market.

title: Systemic Arbitrage in the European Union: Corporate Migration from Italy to the Netherlands
affiliations: University of Bologna

detail.title: Systemic Arbitrage in the European Union: Corporate Migration from Italy to the Netherlands
detail.abstract: Over the past decade, several major Italian listed companies have transferred their registered office to the Netherlands while maintaining their operational and administrative headquarters in Italy. The prevailing explanation for this phenomenon focuses on regulatory arbitrage, particularly the ability of controlling shareholders to exploit more flexible voting structures available under Dutch corporate law. This paper argues that the phenomenon is better understood as a form of systemic corporate arbitrage. Systemic corporate arbitrage occurs when companies strategically distribute their legal, administrative, and market locations across multiple jurisdictions in order to exploit fragmentation among legal systems and public authorities. By doing so, firms can increase their bargaining power vis-à-vis states and regulatory institutions, extracting private benefits while weakening the effectiveness of national governance systems. Using the recent wave of corporate migrations from Italy to the Netherlands as a case study, the paper examines the incentives that drive such relocations and the broader consequences for corporate governance, capital markets, and national regulatory institutions. The paper then evaluates the Italian legislature's recent attempt to address the phenomenon through the introduction of expanded enhanced voting rights under the 2024 Capital Law. The paper concludes that these reforms, while understandable, are unlikely to halt corporate migration. As long as the European Union combines extensive freedom of establishment with limited harmonization of corporate governance rules, systemic corporate arbitrage will remain a structural feature of the European corporate landscape.

title: Innovation Work: Discourse, Meaning, and the Social Construction of Innovation
affiliations: and University of California, Santa Barbara (UCSB)

detail.title: Innovation Work: Discourse, Meaning, and the Social Construction of Innovation

publicationDetails.detailsText: Edited Volume on Discursive Foundations of Responsibility, Sustainability and Innovation (Emerald)

detail.abstract: In this chapter, we argue for the potential usefulness of discourse analysis in innovation research. We begin with a discussion of discourse analysis as it has developed in organization and management theory starting with a historical overview of the beginnings of organizational discourse studies in the 1980s and highlighting the contribution of discourse analysis to our understanding of organizations and their contexts. We then connect our discussions of discourse analysis in organization and management theory to innovation by introducing the concept of innovation work – defined as social-symbolic work carried out to shape the processes of social construction that constitute innovations and their contexts. Innovation work, like all forms of social-symbolic work, has three dimensions: the discursive, material and relational dimensions. We argue that while the existing innovation literature deals relatively effectively with the material and relational dimensions of innovation work, there has been a lack of attention to the discursive dimension. Researchers need a way to research the processes of social construction that constitute the symbolic dimension of innovation and discourse analysis provides both a theoretical frame as well as a well-developed empirical toolkit for doing just that. We end by outlining some of the potentially productive research areas that the idea of innovation work, and a stronger focus on the discursive aspects of innovation more generally, reveal.

title: The Architecture of the Common Good: Reframing the Tragedy of the Commons in Public Administration
affiliations: and University of Macedonia

detail.title: The Architecture of the Common Good: Reframing the Tragedy of the Commons in Public Administration
detail.abstract: This systematic literature review examines the long-standing problem of the tragedy of the commons within the field of public administration. Through a synthetic evaluation of institutional diagnostic and organizational analysis tools, this study deconstructs the traditional dichotomy between centralized state control and local self-governance. The findings reveal a critical interpretive gap: the lack of a coherent theoretical framework for the active, architectural role of the state. To fill this gap, the article develops a synthetic conceptual framework that redefines public administration not as a direct manager or an absent observer, but as an architect of multilevel, polycentric governance systems. This role involves providing institutional support, ensuring access to reliable information, managing cross-scale linkages, and guaranteeing conflict resolution. This approach shifts the focus from a search for a single solution toward the design of resilient institutional ecologies.

title: Communication and Collusion in Oligopoly Experiments: A Meta-Study using Machine Learning
affiliations: University of Bremen and University of Potsdam

detail.title: Communication and Collusion in Oligopoly Experiments: A Meta-Study using Machine Learning
detail.abstract: This paper conducts a primary-data meta-study of oligopoly experiments to analyze how communication content determines collusive behavior. Using a machine learning approach on 603 independent markets involving 1,627 participants, we analyze the communication content across multiple studies. Most communication concerns the discussion of joint benefits, agreements on a specific market behavior, and punishment threats. Of these, only agreements significantly increase collusion. Other communication contents show negligible effects. In an analysis of EU cartel cases, we show that our findings closely align with the connection between real firm communication and their anti-competitive behavior.

title: Grid-Structured Image Representation for Stock Prediction and Portfolio Optimization
affiliations: Gachon University and Gachon University

detail.title: Grid-Structured Image Representation for Stock Prediction and Portfolio Optimization
detail.abstract: Financial time series forecasting remains a fundamental challenge in data-driven investment, as transforming price dynamics into structured representations that can be effectively learned by deep neural networks is inherently difficult. Traditional sequence-based models often fail to fully capture the spatial patterns embedded in financial data. To address this limitation, this study proposes a unified image-based framework that integrates representation learning, predictive modeling, and portfolio optimization. Specifically, financial time series are transformed into grid-structured image representations by redesigning the Grid Shape Context Descriptor (GSCD) to encode both structural patterns and return magnitude within a unified form. These representations are used to train a hybrid convolutional neural network–long short-term memory (CNN-LSTM) model for return prediction, and the resulting forecasts are incorporated as investor views within the Black--Litterman framework for portfolio construction. Experiments on exchange-traded funds (ETFs) across developed and emerging markets show that the proposed framework consistently outperforms both traditional time-series models and existing image-based approaches in predictive accuracy, while also delivering superior risk-adjusted portfolio performance. The results further demonstrate robust performance across diverse market conditions, highlighting the effectiveness of GSCD-based representations in linking financial forecasting with practical investment decisions.

detail.abstract: This paper presents the Antifragile Commercial Transformation Model (ACTM), an applied crisiscommercial strategy framework for mid-sized B2B companies operating under economic instability and market volatility. The framework transforms cyclical downturns from liquidity threats into structured phases of strategic business-model redesign. The approach is built around three sequential phases: differential crisis diagnostics, an operational pause supported by a 13-week liquidity forecast and contractual resilience assessment, and a strategic pivot through crossfunctional revenue integration, market adjacencies, competitive intelligence, and RevOps 2.0. The model combines ABC-XYZ portfolio analysis, threshold-based triggers, War Room governance, contract-risk controls, and restart planning. Pilot validation with B2B industrial distribution and engineering companies indicated a 70-85% reduction in crisis decision latency, Net Revenue Retention improvements to 102-105%, and improved accounts receivable turnover. The framework is designed for commercial directors, revenue leaders, CFOs, and consultants seeking to move from reactive survival to data-driven, resilient commercial transformation.

title: Progressive contrastive learning with text-anchored dynamic fusion for unsupervised multimodal semantic discovery
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, South China Normal University and South China Normal University

detail.title: Progressive contrastive learning with text-anchored dynamic fusion for unsupervised multimodal semantic discovery
detail.abstract: Unsupervised multimodal semantic discovery has recently attracted significant attention in the field of natural language processing. % and multimodal dialogue understanding. However, existing methods often fail to fully exploit complementary information across modalities and struggle with the challenges such as temporal misalignment, modality-specific noise, and unreliable signals, leading to sub-optimal results. To this end, we propose a progressive contrastive learning framework with text-anchored dynamic fusion, namely PCL-TADF in this paper. Specifically, PCL-TADF employs a text-guided cross-attention mechanism to mitigate cross-modal misalignment, by using text tokens as query anchors to retrieve relevant evidence from other modalities.  {Subsequently, to effectively fuse multiple modalities, a dynamic weighted fusion mechanism is developed via a two-stage weighting process, yielding a comprehensive trimodal representation. The proposed model is performed in a two-stage paradigm. {First, Progressive Contrastive Pre-training (PCP) is presented to explore a discriminative latent space to ensure the latent intents are well-separated, by employing a similarity-adaptive penalty mechanism to mitigate class collision.}  At the second stage, Confidence-Based Sample Selection and Progressive Multimodal Representation Learning dynamically partition samples via a dual-perspective confidence score, optimizing dual-branch contrastive objectives to iteratively refine clusters and prevent noisy pseudo-label propagation.} Extensive experimental results on three real-world benchmarks (i.e., MIntRec, MELD-DA, and IEMOCAP-DA) demonstrate that our method achieves superior performance, yielding consistent improvements of 1.0%-8.2% across all metrics against the state-of-the-art methods.

detail.abstract:
This independent self-study presents a comprehensive feasibility analysis and policy framework for the Confederated Tribes and Bands of the Yakama Nation to develop and operate a tribally-owned 5,000-bed correctional and rehabilitation complex near Fort Simcoe, Washington. The proposal envisions federal funding and construction of the core infrastructure on tribal trust land, with the Yakama Nation maintaining full ownership and operational sovereignty under ISDEAA self-governance authority.

The study examines the potential to simultaneously advance tribal sovereignty, deliver culturally grounded healing and rehabilitation programs, bring Yakama citizens home from distant state facilities, create 1,200–1,800 direct jobs (with strong tribal hiring preference), and generate substantial new revenue through intergovernmental per-diem contracts with Washington State DOC, BIA, and federal agencies.

Key components include a detailed 4-wing facility design with a central Cultural Core, economic modeling projecting $270–$548 million in annual gross revenue at 80–90% occupancy, historical sensitivity regarding the Fort Simcoe site, risk assessment, and a seven-year phased implementation roadmap. The paper argues that a Yakama-led, healing-centered justice facility represents both an exercise of treaty rights and a transformative opportunity for economic self-determination.

title: Mapping the Agility-Efficiency Frontier in Supply Chain Network Design A Bi-Objective Pareto Framework for Quantifying the Cost-Resilience Trade-off
affiliations: Novo Nordisk

detail.title: Mapping the Agility-Efficiency Frontier in Supply Chain Network Design A Bi-Objective Pareto Framework for Quantifying the Cost-Resilience Trade-off
detail.abstract: The Agility-Efficiency Frontier (AEF) was introduced as a conceptual framework representing the trade-off between total network cost and structural resilience in supply chain network design (SCND). That framework has remained schematic: the resilience axis is undefined, no algorithm exists to trace the boundary, and the mechanism by which structural innovations shift the curve has not been formalised. This paper supplies the missing mathematical structure, with deliberate scope limitations. Four contributions are made. First, the AEF is defined as the Pareto boundary of a bi-objective Mixed-Integer Linear Program (MILP), with the Structural Resilience Index (SRI)-a weighted composite of node redundancy, geographic dispersion, capacity slack, and a temporal resilience proxy-as the second objective. Second, three mathematical properties of the frontier are proved for the LP relaxation: (i) convexity under independent disruption risks; (ii) an upper bound on the resilience gap incurred by deterministic single-objective optimisation; and (iii) monotonicity of each SRI sub-index. Each proof states explicitly where it does and does not extend to the integer programme. Third, the Frontier Shift Operator and its Shift Efficiency Ratio (SE) are defined; a normalisation correction is introduced so that SE is dimensionally consistent across different cost scales. Fourth, the complete framework is demonstrated on a stylised five-facility, six-market instance. Two limitations are stated explicitly. The SRI weight vector is set to equal illustrative values (0.25 each); without industry-specific calibration, the SRI functions as an internal ranking tool and its numerical values carry no cross-industry validity. The Temporal Resilience Proxy (Rt) uses weighted-average lead time as a recovery-time approximation; the assumptions underlying this choice are set out and an alternative maximum-lead-time formulation is noted. Weight calibration and empirical validation are identified as the primary outstanding requirements before the framework can be applied operationally.

title: Convergence-Weighted Aggregation of Cross-Exchange Prediction Markets: A Dependency-Aware Index for Combining Prices Across Kalshi, Polymarket, Manifold, Metaculus, and Long-Tail Venues

detail.title: Convergence-Weighted Aggregation of Cross-Exchange Prediction Markets: A Dependency-Aware Index for Combining Prices Across Kalshi, Polymarket, Manifold, Metaculus, and Long-Tail Venues
detail.abstract: Modern prediction-market venues — Kalshi, Polymarket, Manifold, Metaculus, and a long tail of newer exchanges — increasingly host overlapping markets on identical world events. Naive aggregation methods (simple or volume-weighted means, Hanson-style market-scoring averages, information-diversity weighted aggregators) treat each venue as a conditionally independent source given the resolution outcome. This assumption is violated in practice by three documented mechanisms: cross-exchange copy-trading bots, shared news flow that drives all venues simultaneously after material announcements, and arbitrageurs whose activity compresses cross-exchange variance below the level that would reflect genuine informational dispersion. Under this dependence, weighted-mean aggregators are biased and overconfident in the contamination regimes a deployer cares about most. We adapt the Index of Convergence Multi-epistemic (ICM) framework, originally developed for cross-disciplinary scientific aggregation (Stanisljevic, 2026), to the prediction-market setting. ICM augments naive aggregation with five components — agreement (A), direction (D), uncertainty overlap (U), perturbation invariance (C), and a dependency penalty (Pi) — yielding a convergence-weighted estimator that decouples genuine cross-source agreement from cross-source contagion. Within Pi, the lead-lag primitive Pi_L is the load-bearing component for the empirical bias-reduction result. We evaluate ICM-weighted aggregation against three baselines (naive mean, volume-weighted mean, Satopaa-Pemantle-Ungar logit-pool) on (i) synthetic experiments under each contamination mechanism in isolation, (ii) hybrid backtests with real Polymarket trajectories, and (iii) a strict cross-exchange backtest on binary markets where Polymarket and Manifold both have hourly history. Synthetic experiments confirm bias-reduction under copy-trading contamination (Mechanism I); the result is regime-targeted rather than uniformly dominant. The strict cross-exchange backtest is reported with the explicit caveat that ICM degenerates to the equal-weighted naive mean at V = 2 listing venues, so the reported Polymarket+Manifold result tests the surrounding pipeline but not the pair-discriminating ICM machinery. Forward-looking evaluation across additional exchanges (Kalshi via authenticated API, plus Metaculus and the long-tail venues) is planned with rolling collection commencing May 2026. Conjecture 1 (asymptotic bias reduction under contamination) is supported by a mechanism-by-mechanism heuristic argument; the formalization of the asymptotic-rate proof is left to follow-up.

title: Strengthening trust and transparency in public administration through qualitative use of Artificial Intelligence

detail.title: Strengthening trust and transparency in public administration through qualitative use of Artificial Intelligence
detail.abstract: Creating public trust in Artificial Intelligence (AI) related to public administration is based on numerous significant aspects. This study explores how transparency, explainability, civic engagement, and digital literacy contribute to the ethical and responsible use of AI in public administration. When individuals have access to data, accountability improves, while explainable AI (XAI) can be used to unravel decisionmaking processes. It is vital to include the public in creating AI regulations to guarantee that these systems align with community principles. Additionally, equipping the public and government employees with substantial digital literacy knowledge permits them to critically examine and use AI technologies efficiently. Our research, grounded in a comprehensive review of extant literature and thematic analysis, provides useful ideas for building trust. These ideas promote diversity and strong oversight, while also encouraging varied groups to work together. This investigation ultimately lays out a structured approach to tackle the varied obstacles linked to technology, moral considerations, and public participation in the use of AI in governmental operations. The goal is to help integrate AI to increase both innovation, as well as public confidence.

title: When the Future Is Unknowable: Responsible Innovation in Mission-Oriented Deep Tech
affiliations: University of Glasgow and University of Glasgow - Adam Smith Business School

detail.title: When the Future Is Unknowable: Responsible Innovation in Mission-Oriented Deep Tech
detail.abstract: Deep Tech is increasingly expected to address grand societal challenges, yet its development is marked by profound socio-ethical uncertainty, where consequences are difficult to anticipate, contested, and not fully knowable ex ante. While Mission-Oriented Innovation (MOI) directs innovation toward societal goals and Responsible Innovation (RI) provides normative governance principles, less is understood about how organisations enact responsibility under such uncertainty.,This paper examines how Deep Tech organisations navigate socio-ethical uncertainty over time and develops the Technology Responsible Understanding (TRU) scale as a diagnostic framework for tracing how responsibility practices emerge and institutionalise across innovation processes. Drawing on exploratory qualitative, longitudinal case studies in quantum computing, connected and autonomous vehicles (CAVs), and financial technologies (FinTech), we show that RI develops through three interrelated organisational capabilities: framing, negotiating, and institutionalising. Through these capabilities, organisations identify dilemmas, embed deliberation into decision-making, and establish governance practices that mitigate unintended consequences. These capabilities evolve non-linearly as organisations iteratively interpret and govern emerging uncertainty.,We make three contributions. First, we reconceptualise RI as an evolving organisational capability rather than a static set of principles. Second, we introduce the TRU scale as a diagnostic framework for tracing how responsibility capabilities develop over time. Third, we demonstrate that RI capability depends not only on firm-level practices but also on ecosystem scaffolding, including regulatory forums, public engagement infrastructures, standard-setting spaces, and patient capital. Together, these findings extend RI and MOI scholarship by showing that mission-oriented innovation requires multi-level capability development across both organisations and ecosystems.

title: Theory building review: Η ανατομία της συλλογικής ανευθυνότητας στη δημόσια διοίκηση και το μοντέλο του προοπτικού σχεδιασμού της ευθύνης

detail.title: Theory building review: Η ανατομία της συλλογικής ανευθυνότητας στη δημόσια διοίκηση και το μοντέλο του προοπτικού σχεδιασμού της ευθύνης
detail.abstract: Η παρούσα μελέτη ανατέμνει το αποκαλούμενο «πρόβλημα των πολλών χεριών» (problem of many hands) στη σύγχρονη δημόσια διοίκηση μέσα από μια θεωρητική ανασκόπηση. Το θεμελιώδες πλαίσιο του προβλήματος εδράζεται στην εντεινόμενη σύγκρουση μεταξύ της δημοκρατικής απαίτησης για σαφή απόδοση ευθυνών και της αυξανόμενης δομικής πολυπλοκότητας της διακυβέρνησης. Η πολυπλοκότητα αυτή χαρακτηρίζεται από δικτυακές δομές, ιδιωτικοποιήσεις και αλγοριθμική λήψη αποφάσεων που καθιστούν τον εντοπισμό ενός υπεύθυνου δράστη σχεδόν αδύνατο. Σκοπός της εργασίας είναι να συνθέσει την κατακερματισμένη και διεπιστημονική βιβλιογραφία προκειμένου να αμφισβητήσει την παραδοσιακή προσέγγιση της απόδοσης ευθύνης η οποία εστιάζει στον εντοπισμό του υπαίτιου αποκλειστικά μετά από μια αποτυχία. Υιοθετώντας μια εννοιολογική μετατόπιση ως θεωρητικό φακό, η μελέτη αντιμετωπίζει την ευθύνη όχι ως μια ατομική ιδιότητα που ανακαλύπτεται εκ των υστέρων αλλά ως μια συστημική ικανότητα που σχεδιάζεται εξ αρχής. Τα κύρια ευρήματα, τα οποία προκύπτουν από τη συστηματική ανάλυση 98 μελετών οργανωμένων μέσω του πλαισίου εντοπισμού προηγούμενων αιτιών, αποφάσεων και αποτελεσμάτων (ADO), αποκαλύπτουν ότι η δομική και τεχνολογική πολυπλοκότητα δημιουργεί γνωστικά και ηθικά κενά. Αυτά τα κενά τα εκμεταλλεύονται στρατηγικά οι πολιτικοί και διοικητικοί δρώντες μέσω «παιχνιδιών επίρριψης ευθυνών» οδηγώντας σε διάχυση της ευθύνης, υποβάθμιση της δημοκρατικής λογοδοσίας και αδυναμία συστημικής μάθησης. Ως θεωρητική συμβολή το άρθρο προτείνει ένα νέο εννοιολογικό μοντέλο γνωστό ως «Προοπτικό Σχεδιασμό της Ευθύνης» (Prospective Design Responsibility). Το μοντέλο αυτό μετατοπίζει το επίκεντρο από την αναζήτηση υπαιτίων στην προληπτική θεσμική αρχιτεκτονική πλουραλιστικών δικτύων λογοδοσίας όπου η συλλογική ευθύνη καθίσταται αναπόδραστη μέσω του σχεδιασμού σαφών ρόλων, μηχανισμών συντονισμού και κοινών πληροφοριακών υποδομών.

title: Real-Time Trip Assignment for On-Demand Transit: A Large-Scale Comparative Study of Metaheuristics and Objectives
affiliations: Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology, Qassim University, Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology, Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology (BUET) and Dalhousie University

detail.title: Real-Time Trip Assignment for On-Demand Transit: A Large-Scale Comparative Study of Metaheuristics and Objectives
detail.abstract: On-demand transit (ODT) is an increasingly important component of urbanmobility, requiring effective real-time decision-making for trip assignmentand fleet management. This study integrates operations research andartificial intelligence by systematically applying metaheuristics (SimulatedAnnealing and Hybrid Genetic Search) to classical routing models (TravelingSalesman Problem and Vehicle Routing Problem with Time Windows)for ODT logistics optimization. We conduct a comprehensive comparativeevaluation of these approaches within a unified agent-based simulation, usinga large-scale, real-world case study of 10,005 trip requests over 24 hoursacross a 2,448-node road network in Halifax, Canada. The waiting-timefocusedTSP-based solution achieves the strongest performance overall, with99.36% trip completion, 3.22 minutes average wait, and a 15.15% reductionin vehicle kilometers traveled, suggesting that computational tractability is apractical asset in real-time transit environments. Our results highlight thatthe choice of optimization objective has a greater impact on service coveragethan algorithm or formulation choice, with waiting-time minimizationsubstantially widening the range of viable fleet configurations. Initial vehicleplacement is shown to be a critical operational factor, with run-to-runvariability exceeding ±30 percentage points in trip completion, underscoringthe need for effective warm-start strategies. Furthermore, intra-run distributionalanalysis of waiting and delay times reveals service inequity hiddenby mean metrics, motivating multi-objective optimization for practical deployment.These findings provide actionable insights for real-time logisticsoptimization, decision support, and equity assessment in demand-responsivetransit systems.

title: From cost efficiency to environmental integrity: Dynamic prioritization of corporate renewable energy procurement
affiliations: Seoul National University, Seoul National University - College of Engineering and Korea Institute of Energy Technology Evaluation and Planning

detail.title: From cost efficiency to environmental integrity: Dynamic prioritization of corporate renewable energy procurement
detail.abstract: As corporate renewable energy procurement shifts from voluntary commitment to mandatory compliance, firms face complex trade-offs between economic feasibility and environmental integrity. This challenge is particularly acute in nominal transition economies like South Korea, where rigid regulatory frameworks and limited accessibility create a cycle of high nominal participation yet low substantive implementation. By triangulating scenario-based Analytic Hierarchy Process data with qualitative expert feedback, this study examines the strategic priorities of diverse stakeholders regarding four key implementation alternatives: green premium, renewable energy certificates, power purchase agreements, and self-generation. The analysis identifies three fundamental barriers driving current stagnation. First, an interest mismatch creates a market deadlock between buyer cost sensitivity and supplier stability. Second, a value mismatch triggers a Green Paradox where low-quality instruments crowd out high-integrity options like power purchase agreements. Third, a temporal mismatch reveals that static grids fail to meet emerging 24/7 Carbon-Free Energy standards. These findings theoretically refute the efficacy of market neutrality in immature grids and demonstrate that passive liberalization leads to sub-optimal lock-in. Consequently, the study proposes the 3A Framework (Access-Anchor-Advance) which advocates for a shift toward strategic asymmetry. This roadmap operationalizes sequential interventions by synchronizing entry conditions, absorbing transaction risks to anchor long-term contracts, and incentivizing technology-driven integrity. These measures collectively aim to transform renewable procurement from a compliance burden into a driver of industrial competitiveness.

title: A Fatigue-aware Scheduling Framework for Transportation Robots and Human Operators in Industry 5.0
affiliations: CESI LINEACT, University of Sharjah, University of Sharjah, University of Sharjah and University of Sharjah

detail.title: A Fatigue-aware Scheduling Framework for Transportation Robots and Human Operators in Industry 5.0
detail.abstract: Human-centric manufacturing requires scheduling frameworks that jointly optimize operational efficiency and operator well-being. To this end, this paper investigates an integrated production and transportation scheduling problem incorporating operator fatigue, formulated as a mixed-integer nonlinear program. We develop a constraint programming model solved with CP-SAT, complemented by a genetic algorithm (GA) and variable neighborhood search (VNS) approaches. To assess operational validity, we design a simulation framework evaluating schedules derived without fatigue considerations. Results reveal a critical gap between classical and fatigue-aware scheduling: although fatigue-agnostic solutions may appear optimal in terms of makespan, they are largely infeasible in practice, often leading to operator exhaustion. While reactive rest insertion restores feasibility, it degrades performance by 6.72% on average. In contrast, explicitly integrating fatigue into optimization yields safer schedules with limited performance loss. Moreover, enabling fatigue recovery during machine idle periods reduces the makespan further by up to 10% without requiring explicit rest. Finally, comparing algorithms revealed a CP-SAT optimality rate of 94.37% across instances, while VNS consistently outperforms GA in producing near-optimal solutions.

title: Brand Loyalty within the Cosmetic Industry among Gen Z
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Brand Loyalty within the Cosmetic Industry among Gen Z
detail.abstract: This study investigates the determinants of brand loyalty among Generation Z consumers (ages 18–28) in Delhi’s rapidly evolving cosmetic industry, a demographic defined by high digital literacy and shifting value systems. Utilizing a quantitative approach and SPSS analysis, the research examined the impact of seven variables—hedonic value, brand self-congruity, brand trust, perceived quality, consumer engagement, price, and satisfaction—finding that the regression model explained 54.2% of loyalty variance. Results identify consumer engagement as the primary predictor (\beta = .321), followed by perceived quality, brand trust, price, and self-congruity, while hedonic values were notably found to be statistically insignificant. These findings suggest that for Gen Z in India, functional and relational attributes outweigh purely emotional motives, implying that cosmetic brands should prioritize interactive engagement and consistent quality over superficial aesthetic appeal to secure long-term market sustainability.

title: Demystifying China's Belt and Road: The Struggle to Define China's Project of the Century
affiliations: Johns Hopkins University

detail.title: Demystifying China's Belt and Road: The Struggle to Define China's Project of the Century
detail.abstract: Yuen Yuen Ang argues that the Belt and Road Initiative (BRI) is fundamentally misunderstood—not due to Chinese deception, but because of deliberate ambiguity rooted in China's domestic policymaking tradition. Lacking an official definition or enforceable standards, the BRI functions as a "policy brand" that state enterprises, local governments, and private firms claim for self-interested ends. Through fieldwork in Sihanoukville, Cambodia, Ang illustrates how analysts often conflate private Chinese capital with state-backed development. This conflation generates accusations of "debt-trap diplomacy" that often exceed empirical evidence. Ang situates the BRI within the framework of "directed improvisation"—top-down vision-setting combined with decentralized, bottom-up execution. While this model enables rapid mobilization, it produces significant coordination failures internationally. Ang contends that the transition from BRI 1.0 (xieyi, broad strokes) to BRI 2.0 (gongbi, careful inscription) requires three steps: narrowing policy priorities, establishing transparent project lists, and piloting small-scale projects—lessons drawn from China's own coevolutionary development experience.

title: Autocracy with Chinese Characteristics: Beijing's Behind-the-Scenes Reforms
affiliations: Johns Hopkins University

detail.title: Autocracy with Chinese Characteristics: Beijing's Behind-the-Scenes Reforms
detail.abstract: Yuen Yuen Ang argues that China's sustained economic growth under single-party rule is not evidence that autocracy rivals democracy, nor a temporary aberration before inevitable democratization. Rather, since Deng Xiaoping's reforms beginning in 1978, the Chinese Communist Party has introduced democratic characteristics—accountability, competition, and partial limits on power—into its bureaucratic apparatus without relinquishing political control. Through reforms such as performance-based cadre evaluation systems, term limits for elite officials, and internal profit-sharing mechanisms for rank-and-file public employees, the CCP transformed a rigid Leninist bureaucracy into an adaptive, growth-oriented machine. However, Ang contends that this strategy of substituting bureaucratic reform for genuine political liberalization is approaching its limits: rising citizen demands, Xi Jinping's consolidation of personal power, and the innovation requirements of a middle-income economy are straining a system that cannot indefinitely defer meaningful political reform.

title: Third-Generation Bioethanol from Marine Macroalgae: A Comparative Review of Pretreatment Techniques, Process Conditions, Fermentation Yields, and Integrated Valorization of Process Residues

detail.title: Third-Generation Bioethanol from Marine Macroalgae: A Comparative Review of Pretreatment Techniques, Process Conditions, Fermentation Yields, and Integrated Valorization of Process Residues

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing financial or personal interests. This review was conducted independently, without institutional affiliation or external funding. This document is a preprint posted on Zenodo (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20101229) and has not undergone formal peer review.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This manuscript is a systematic narrative review based entirely on published peer-reviewed literature. No human participants, patient data, or animal subjects were involved. Ethics approval was not required.

detail.abstract:
The global energy transition demands renewable alternatives that do not compete with food production or land use. Marine macroalgae have emerged as a compelling third-generation feedstock for bioethanol, owing to their high carbohydrate content, ranging from 4% to 64% of dry weight depending on species and season (Borines et al., 2013; Kraan, 2013), the structural absence of lignin, rapid growth rates, and their abundance as beach-cast waste in tropical coastal regions. Unlike first-generation biofuels derived from food crops or second-generation biofuels dependent on lignocellulosic terrestrial biomass, macroalgal bioethanol circumvents the foodversus-fuel conflict and avoids competition for arable land and freshwater resources (Sirajunnisa & Surendhiran, 2016; Sharmila et al., 2022). 

This review systematically compares pretreatment strategies, fermentation conditions, and ethanol yield profiles across ecologically and biochemically distinct macroalgal groups: brown algae (Phaeophyta), red algae (Rhodophyta), and green algae (Chlorophyta). Pretreatment methods examined include dilute acid hydrolysis, hydrothermal treatment, wet oxidation, steam explosion, enzymatic saccharification, ball milling, and hybrid physicochemical approaches (Schultz-Jensen et al., 2013; Milledge et al., 2018; Del Río et al., 2021). Reported ethanol conversion efficiencies range from below 30% in untreated biomass to optimized yields exceeding 89% under well-designed enzymatic-fermentative systems (Moenaert et al., 2023), and up to 48.24 g/L ethanol in fed-batch systems with salt-tolerant marine yeast (Turner et al., 2022). 

A critical analysis of process inhibitors, including salt content, heavy metals, hydroxymethylfurfural (HMF), and high ash fractions, is provided alongside mitigation strategies (Park et al., 2022; Nguyen et al., 2017). Beyond bioethanol itself, this review examines the integrated valorization of process residues within a biorefinery framework: anaerobic digestion of fermentation stillage to biomethane, extraction of high-value co-products including alginate, fucoidan, carrageenan, mannitol, and laminarin, and application of digestate as biofertilizer (Tedesco & Stokes, 2017; Kerner et al., 1991; Arias et al., 2023). The analysis concludes that the economic and environmental viability of macroalgal bioethanol is significantly enhanced by co-product integration (Llano et al., 2023; Alvarado-Morales et al., 2013), and that residual biomass streams, including beach-stranded Sargassum in tropical coastlines such as the Colombian Caribbean coast, represent an underexploited resource within a circular bioeconomy framework (Alzate-Gaviria et al., 2021; Colorado-Ríos et al., 2025).

title: An AI- and Blockchain-Based Framework for Dynamic Spectrum Access in 5G and Beyond (6G) Wireless Networks
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: An AI- and Blockchain-Based Framework for Dynamic Spectrum Access in 5G and Beyond (6G) Wireless Networks
detail.abstract: The rapid evolution of 5G and emerging 6G wireless networks has intensified the demand for efficient, adaptive, and secure spectrum utilization. Conventional static spectrum allocation policies lead to significant underutilization of available bandwidth, while existing dynamic spectrum access (DSA) approaches face challenges related to scalability, security, and real-time decision-making in highly dynamic environments. To address these limitations, this paper proposes an integrated framework that combines Artificial Intelligence (AI) and blockchain technologies for intelligent and secure spectrum management.The proposed framework employs deep learning techniques to enhance spectrum sensing accuracy under varying channel conditions, leveraging advances in neural network architectures for feature extraction and pattern recognition. Furthermore, deep reinforcement learning is utilized to enable adaptive and autonomous spectrum allocation, allowing secondary users to optimize channel selection dynamically. In parallel, a blockchain-based architecture is incorporated to ensure decentralized control, transparent spectrum transactions, and secure data sharing among network entities. This integration enhances trust, mitigates malicious behavior, and eliminates reliance on centralized authorities.Extensive simulation-based evaluation demonstrates that the proposed system significantly improves spectrum utilization, throughput, and fairness compared to conventional and standalone approaches. Additionally, the framework achieves higher detection accuracy in low signal-to-noise ratio environments while maintaining acceptable latency despite blockchain integration.The results highlight the effectiveness of combining AI-driven intelligence with blockchain-enabled security to develop a scalable and reliable spectrum access solution for next-generation wireless networks. This work provides a strong foundation for future research in intelligent, decentralized, and secure communication systems for 5G and beyond (6G) environments.

title: A Hybrid Optimisation-Large Language Model Framework for Real-Time Order Fulfilment Decision Support in Plywood Manufacturing
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and Vietnam Academy of Science and Technology

detail.title: A Hybrid Optimisation-Large Language Model Framework for Real-Time Order Fulfilment Decision Support in Plywood Manufacturing
detail.abstract: This paper presents the architecture, formulation, and empirical evaluation of the Smart Plywood Production Optimizer v5.0, a production decision-support framework that integrates a structured enumeration heuristic over a mixed-integer objective-referred to herein as the MILP-structured optimiser-with large language model (LLM) inference on the n8n open-source automation platform. The system ingests customer orders from Google Sheets, consolidates six real-time operational data streams-covering inventory, production capacity, demand history, scheduling state, cost parameters, and customer priority-and solves a multi-criteria allocation problem across three fulfilment channels (stock shipment, internal production, and outsourcing) subject to eight business constraints. The mathematically derived allocation is subsequently evaluated by a Groq-hosted Llama-3.3-70b model, which applies contextual and qualitative reasoning to assess or, where justified, revise the optimisation output. A two-tier fallback mechanism preserves workflow continuity under AI unavailability or solver infeasibility. Evaluated on a dataset of 4,823 records from a Vietnamese plywood manufacturer, the hybrid system achieves a mean end-to-end processing time of 7.2 seconds, a success rate of 99.0%, and an average modelled margin of 30.4%-a gain of 3.3 percentage points over the rule-based baseline (paired t-test: p < 0.0001; 95% CI: [2.7, 3.9] pp). A 200-order exact MILP benchmark establishes that the grid-enumeration heuristic achieves a mean composite score within 0.47% of the exact optimum, with identical allocations in 84.0% of cases. LLM output stability across five repeated invocations on 100 sampled orders yields a decision-type agreement rate of 91.0%; a three-prompt, two-model robustness experiment confirms that performance remains above the rule-based baseline even under adversarial prompt conditions. Expert consensus alignment increases from 61% to 81% with the full hybrid configuration. Inventory and capacity discrepancies are reduced by 89.0% and 87.5%, respectively. The findings demonstrate that bounded LLM-based contextual reasoning can be effectively combined with structured combinatorial optimisation to support real-time order-fulfilment decisions in small and medium-sized manufacturing enterprises.

title: Decomposing DEA efficiency for managerial improvement: A consistent input–output pure technical and scale efficiencies extension of the BCC model
affiliations: King Faisal University

detail.title: Decomposing DEA efficiency for managerial improvement: A consistent input–output pure technical and scale efficiencies extension of the BCC model
detail.abstract: This paper proposes a novel decomposition framework for pure technical efficiency within the Data Envelopment Analysis (DEA) approach. Building on the BCC model, we introduce input- and output-decomposed formulations (ID-BCC and OD-BCC) that preserve the radial structure and dual optimal weights while providing disaggregated efficiency measures. The proposed models enable the decomposition of pure technical efficiency into input-specific radial contraction factors and output-specific radial expansion potentials, respectively. Theoretical properties, including aggregation consistency and single-run computability, are formally established. Building on the decomposed CCR model results (ID-CCR and OD-CCR) for constant returns to scale (CRS) input- and output-orientated efficiency measures, we derive input and output scale efficiencies (ISE and OSE) as the ratios of ID-CCR to ID-BCC and OD-CCR to OD-BCC, respectively. An empirical illustration based on EU agricultural systems, using FAO data, provides evidence that inefficiency arises from heterogeneous sources, including input misallocation, output imbalance, and scale effects. By shifting the focus from inter-unit benchmarking to internal efficiency diagnosis, the approach enables each decision-making unit to identify targeted adjustment strategies. The paper advocates treating the proposed decomposition as a practical management tool.

title: Novel Performance Indicators for Optimal Operation and Management of Medium-Voltage Distribution Networks
affiliations: University of Tuzla

detail.title: Novel Performance Indicators for Optimal Operation and Management of Medium-Voltage Distribution Networks
detail.abstract: This paper proposes a novel framework for the optimal management and reconstruction of medium-voltage distribution networks by utilizing the electric line’s natural power (Pnat) as a fundamental operational criterion. The rationale is that operating distribution lines near the Pnat level inherently provides uniform voltage profiles along the lines and minimal network losses. To fully utilize the thermal capacity of lines—whose power flow is significantly greater than Pnat—this work proposes a methodology based on L/C compensation of distribution lines. This compensation is particularly relevant when network reconfiguration using tie-switches cannot achieve the desired equalization between thermal-based power flows and Pnat. This approach allows the natural power to be modified and increased to a value corresponding to the line's thermal capacity. To quantify the network's optimality, this work introduces three novel performance indicators: the Euclidean distance metric, the Area-Time (Arti) metric, and the Annual Utilization Index (AUI). These metrics provide a robust measure of the distribution infrastructure's utilization and efficiency by quantifying the deviation of actual power flows from the optimal natural power benchmark.
